'''Alonzo Lewis Mayes, Jr.''' (born June 4, 1975) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[tight end]] for three seasons with the [[Chicago Bears]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL).  He played [[college football]] for the [[Oklahoma State Cowboys football|Oklahoma State Cowboys]], earning consensus [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honor in 1997.

==Early life==
Mayes was born in [[Oklahoma City, Oklahoma]].<ref name=nflprofile>National Football League, Historical Players, [http://www.nfl.com/player/alonzomayes/2501925/profile  Alonzo Mayes].  Retrieved January 30, 2012.</ref>  He attended [[Douglass High School (Oklahoma City)|Frederick A. Douglass High School]] in Oklahoma City,<ref name=dbfprofile>databaseFootball.com, Players, {{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20111121234958/http://databasefootball.com/players/playerpage.htm?ilkid=MAYESALO01  Alonzo Mayes]}}.  Retrieved January 30, 2012.</ref> where he played for the Douglass Trojans [[high school football]] team.

==College career==
Mayes received an [[athletic scholarship]] to attend Oklahoma State University and play for the [[Oklahoma State Cowboys football]] team from 1994 to 1997.  As a senior in 1997, he was recognized as a consensus first-team All-American at tight end.

==Professional career==
The Chicago Bears selected Mayes in the fourth round (94th pick overall) of the [[1998 NFL draft]], and he played for the Bears from {{NFL Year|1998}} to {{NFL Year|2000}}.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1998 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1998/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-29 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He finished his professional career with the [[Miami Dolphins]], but never appeared in a regular season game for the Dolphins.  In three NFL seasons with the Bears, Mayes played in thirty-seven games, started twenty-eight of them, and compiled thirty-three receptions for 339 yards and a touchdown.<ref name="pfrprofile">{{Cite web |title=Alonzo Mayes Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MayeAl00.htm |access-date=2025-08-30 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>  He was nicknamed "Showtime" for his zany celebrations.

'''Alvin Bowen''' (born December 24, 1983) is an American former professional [[gridiron football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) and [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL). He was selected by the [[Buffalo Bills]] in the fifth round of the [[2008 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Iowa State Cyclones football|Iowa State Cyclones]]. Bowen was also a member of the [[Washington Redskins]], [[Seattle Seahawks]], [[Jacksonville Jaguars]], [[Denver Broncos]] of the NFL, and the [[Saskatchewan Roughriders]] and [[Calgary Stampeders]] of the CFL.

Born in [[East Orange, New Jersey]], Bowen was raised in nearby [[Montclair, New Jersey|Montclair]], where he played football at [[Montclair High School (New Jersey)|Montclair High School]].<ref>[http://cyclones.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=1074 Alvin Bowen], [[Iowa State Cyclones football]]. Accessed March 14, 2018. "Hometown: East Orange, N.J.; Highschool: Montclair"</ref>

==College career==
Bowen attended and played [[college football]] for the [[Iowa State Cyclones football|Iowa State Cyclones]].  During his junior year, he recorded 155 tackles (finishing first in the nation),<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/years/2006-leaders.html|title=2006 Leaders|website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com|language=en|access-date=2019-06-04}}</ref> one [[interception]], and one [[fumble]] recovery. During his senior season, Bowen recorded 99 tackles, one interception, and one fumble recovery.

===Buffalo Bills===
Bowen was selected by the [[Buffalo Bills]] in the fifth round (147th overall) of the [[2008 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2008 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2008/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-12 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> During training camp on August 1, Bowen suffered a serious knee injury. He was waived/injured on August 7 and subsequently placed on season-ending [[injured reserve]].

He was released by the Bills on September 5, 2009. He was re-signed to the [[practice squad]] on September 6, and was released on September 22.

He was on the team again for weeks 13–17<ref>{{cite web |author=Alvin Bowen |url=http://www.buffalobills.com/team/roster/alvin-bowen/bf213be5-2168-4021-9f9c-a8ce301951ea/ |title=Alvin Bowen |publisher=Buffalo Bills |accessdate=August 13, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120614110053/http://www.buffalobills.com/team/roster/alvin-bowen/bf213be5-2168-4021-9f9c-a8ce301951ea/ |archive-date=June 14, 2012 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }}</ref> due to the Bills suffering a string of injuries to their linebackers. Linebackers Paul Posluzny, Marcus Buggs, Kawika Mitchell and Keith Ellison all missed time due to injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/287065-buffalo-bills-dreadful-mid-season-injury-analysis |title=Buffalo Bills Dreadful Midseason Injury Analysis |publisher=Bleacher Report |date=November 9, 2009 |access-date=August 13, 2012}}</ref>

===Washington Redskins===
Bowen was signed to the [[Washington Redskins]] practice squad on September 24.  He was later promoted to the active roster on November 30, 2009.  After one season, he was released from the Redskins on June 9, 2010.

===Seattle Seahawks===
Bowen signed with the [[Seattle Seahawks]] on August 7, 2010. He was waived on August 17.

===Jacksonville Jaguars===
Bowen signed with the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] on August 20, 2010. He was released on September 4. He was signed to the practice squad the next day. He was signed from the practice squad on September 19 and waived on September 28. He was re-signed to the practice squad on September 30.

On August 13, 2011, Bowen was waived by the Jaguars.

===Denver Broncos===
On August 15, 2011, he was claimed off waivers by the [[Denver Broncos]].

===Saskatchewan Roughriders (first stint)===
On March 8, 2012, Alvin Bowen signed with the [[Saskatchewan Roughriders]] of the [[Canadian Football League]]. On April 19, Bowen was released by the [[Saskatchewan Roughriders|'Riders]].

===Calgary Stampeders===

'''Alonzo Brandon Ephraim''' (born November 8, 1981) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was an [[offensive lineman]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama Crimson Tide]].

Ephraim was originally signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] in 2003. In 2006, while with the [[Cleveland Browns]], he was suspended four games for violating the league's substance-abuse policy,<ref name="Suspended">{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=2551170 |title=Browns center Ephraim suspended four games |work=[[ESPN.com]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |date=August 16, 2008 |access-date=October 20, 2008}}</ref> after which he was waived by the Browns.

On July 27, 2007, Ephraim signed with the All American Football League to play for [[Team Alabama]] when the league began play.<ref name="AAFL">{{cite web|url=http://www.allamericanfootballleague.com/BirminghamsigningsPR.html |title=ALL AMERICAN FOOTBALL LEAGUE ANNOUNCES SIGNING OF FORMER ALABAMA PLAYERS DURING LEAGUE'S NATIONAL TRY-OUT AT BIRMINGHAM'S LEGION FIELD |work=[[All-American Football League]].com |publisher=PRNewswire |date=July 27, 2007 |accessdate=October 20, 2008 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20081007144138/http://www.allamericanfootballleague.com/BirminghamsigningsPR.html |archivedate=October 7, 2008 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Early life==
Ephraim attended [[Wenonah High School]],<ref name="Scout">{{cite web |url=http://alabama.scout.com/a.z?s=14&p=8&c=1&nid=389458 |title=#58 Alonzo Ephraim - Alabama Roster |work=[[Scout.com]] |publisher=BamaMag.com |accessdate=October 20, 2008}}</ref> where he played center on offense and [[defensive end]] on defense.<ref name="Rivals">{{cite web |url=http://uga.rivals.com/content.asp?CID=293259 |title=Alonzo Ephraim Update |work=[[Rivals.com]] |publisher=BamaOnline News Plus |date=May 16, 1998 |accessdate=October 20, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110715190751/http://uga.rivals.com/content.asp?CID=293259 |archive-date=July 15, 2011 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }}</ref> He was also the starting center on the school's [[basketball]] team.<ref name="Rivals"/> He was on the [[baseball]] and [[Track and Field|track]] teams as well.<ref name="Rivals"/> In 1998, as a senior he was selected as the Class 6A Offensive Lineman of the Year.<ref name="AHSFHS">{{cite web |url=http://www.ahsfhs.org/allstate/allstateteam2.asp?year=1998 |title=1998 Awards - Other Awards |accessdate=October 20, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110724230254/http://www.ahsfhs.org/allstate/allstateteam2.asp?year=1998 |archive-date=July 24, 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was a Super 12 (All-State) team Honorable Mention, along with future college teammates Dante Ellington and [[Saleem Rasheed]].<ref name="AHSFHS"/> When he graduated he had a 3.2 [[Grade Point Average|GPA]].<ref name="Rivals"/>

== College career ==
Ephraim received interest from schools such as [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama]], [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan]], [[UCLA Bruins football|UCLA]], [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Notre Dame]], [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets football|Georgia Tech]], [[Nebraska Cornhuskers football|Nebraska]].<ref name="Rivals"/> In the end, he chose Alabama. As a true freshman, he appeared in just two games, for a total of 29 plays.<ref name="Scout"/> He then played as a back-up for every game as a sophomore.<ref name="Scout"/> He became a starter as a junior, and had 708 plays that season, the most among Alabama offensive linemen. He also recorded 118 knock-down blocks.<ref name="Scout"/> He was a second-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-America]] selection his [[2002 NCAA Division I-A football season|senior]] year. He was also an All-SEC selection as a [[2001 NCAA Division I-A football season|junior]]. As a senior, he was one of seven Alabama players selected as All-SEC.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.rolltide.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/121202aad.html |title=Seven Bama Players Named to AP All-SEC Teams |work=RollTide.com |publisher=University of Alabama |date=December 12, 2002 |accessdate=October 20, 2008}}</ref> As a senior, he was named to the [[Rimington Trophy]] watchlist.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.rolltide.com/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/091002aad.html |title=Alabama Football Game Notes: North Texas |work=RollTide.com |publisher=University of Alabama |date=September 10, 2002 |accessdate=October 20, 2008}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Philadelphia Eagles===
Ephraim went unselected in the [[2003 NFL draft]]. However, he signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] with the [[Philadelphia Eagles]]<ref name="Tiders">{{cite web |url=http://alabama.scout.com/2/107992.html |title=Nine Tiders sign free agent contracts |last=White |first=Larry |work=[[Scout.com]] |publisher=[[University of Alabama]] |date=April 28, 2003 |accessdate=October 20, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110716022604/http://alabama.scout.com/2/107992.html |archive-date=July 16, 2011 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }}</ref> and played in 16 games as a [[rookie]]. In [[2004 NFL season|2004]], he played in 13 games with two starts at right guard for the Eagles. He was released on April 28, 2005.<ref name="Fins">{{cite web |url=http://www.miamidolphins.com/newsite/news/top_story.asp?contentID=3984&lid=3984 |title=Camp Dolphins Day 8: Team Signs Alonzo Ephraim And Waives Derek Curry |work=MiamiDolphins.com |publisher=[[Miami Dolphins]] |date=August 2, 2005 |accessdate=October 20, 2008 }}{{Dead link|date=October 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> 

===Miami Dolphins===
On August 2, 2005, he signed with the [[Miami Dolphins]].<ref name="Fins"/> In his lone season with the Dolphins, he played in 13 games, with three starts. 

===Cleveland Browns===
In [[2006 NFL season|2006]], he signed as an unrestricted free agent with the [[Cleveland Browns]] but was suspended for four games for violating the league's substance-abuse policy.<ref name="Suspended"/> He was waived after he completed his suspension.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/football/ephraim-let-go-by-browns-1.602054 |title=Ephraim let go by Browns |work=CBC.ca |publisher=[[CBC Sports]] |date=October 2, 2006 |access-date=October 20, 2008}}</ref> Over his four-year NFL career, he played in a total of 43 games.<ref name="AAFL"/>

===New York Dragons===
On April 24, 2008, Ephraim signed with the [[New York Dragons]] of the [[Arena Football League (1987–2008)|Arena Football League]] and played in three games as a rookie. <ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=Ex-Tide player heating it up for Dragons |url=https://www.tuscaloosanews.com/story/sports/2008/06/27/ex-tide-player-heating-it-up-for-dragons/27755181007/ |access-date=2026-05-30 |website=The Tuscaloosa News |language=en-US}}</ref>

===All American Football League===
At the [[All American Football League]]'s national try-outs held on July 27, 2007, Ephraim, along with fellow Alabama alumni [[Reggie Myles]] and Marcus Spencer, signed with the league to play for [[Team Alabama]].<ref name="AAFL"/> However, the league postponed their inaugural season until 2009.

'''Alphonso Smith, Jr.''' (born October 20, 1985) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[cornerback]] for four seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL).  Smith played [[college football]] for the [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons football|Wake Forest Demon Deacons]], and received consensus [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors.  He was selected by the [[Denver Broncos]] in the second round of the [[2009 NFL draft]], and also played for the NFL's [[Detroit Lions]].

==Early life==
Smith was born in [[Pahokee, Florida]].  He played quarterback and cornerback at [[Pahokee High School]], and was runner up for the state Player of the Year award as a senior after leading the school to a 13–1 record and the Class 2B state championship.  He earned first-team all-state honors as a senior cornerback, totaling 27 tackles, four interceptions and one sack.  On offense, he threw for 2,400 yards and 32 touchdowns while also rushing for 640 yards and six scores as a senior. He also started on the school's basketball team.

==College career==
Smith attended [[Wake Forest University]], where he played for coach [[Jim Grobe]]'s [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons football]] team from 2004 to 2008.  Smith redshirted as a true freshman in 2004.  As a redshirt freshman in 2005, Smith started all 11 games and finished the season with 60 tackles (52 unassisted), three interceptions, two sacks, 12 pass breakups and one forced fumble.  He received first-team Freshman All-America honors from CollegeFootballNews.com, ESPN.com and Scout.com.  In 2006, the sophomore played 14 games with three starts, registering 48 tackles (37 solo), three interceptions, four sacks, 11 pass breakups and one forced fumble.

As a junior in 2007, Smith started all 13 games as a junior for the Demon Deacons and had 44 tackles (36 solo), eight interceptions, three sacks, 18 pass breakups and four forced fumbles and returned three of the interceptions for touchdowns.  He tied for first in the nation with a school-record eight interceptions and was first-team All-[[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC) selection and received second-team All-America honors from Walter Camp.

In 2008 Smith started all 13 games as a senior for Wake Forest, totaling 37 tackles (28 solo), seven interceptions, 20 pass breakups and two forced fumbles and tied for first in the nation in both interceptions and pass breakups.  He was a first-team All-ACC selection and a consensus first-team All-American.  He was also named one of five finalists for the [[Bronko Nagurski Trophy]].  He continues to hold the ACC record for career interceptions (21), and broke the record previously held by [[Dré Bly]] of North Carolina in the [[2008 EagleBank Bowl]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://wakeforestsports.cstv.com/sports/m-footbl/recaps/112908aaa.html |title=Wake Forest Closes Season with 23-10 win Over Vanderbilt - Wake Forest Official Athletic Site |publisher=Wakeforestsports.cstv.com |date= |accessdate=2012-10-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081202024733/http://wakeforestsports.cstv.com/sports/m-footbl/recaps/112908aaa.html |archive-date=2008-12-02 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Denver Broncos===
[[File:Alphonso Smith.JPG|thumb|left|200px|Smith in 2010 during his tenure with the Broncos.]] 
The Broncos selected Smith in the second round (37th overall) in the [[2009 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2009 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2009/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-12 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>  The Broncos traded their first round pick in 2010 in order to select him.  This trade, among other poor decisions, led to the firing of coach Josh McDaniels.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/451409-denver-broncos-josh-mcdaniels-traded-earl-thomas-for-dan-gronkowski-other-cuts|title = Denver Broncos' Josh McDaniels Traded Earl Thomas for Dan Gronkowski, Other Cuts|website = [[Bleacher Report]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://broncoswire.usatoday.com/2017/04/25/denver-broncos-news-josh-mcdaniels-von-miller/|title=Josh McDaniels' terrible trades led to best pick in Broncos history|date=26 April 2017}}</ref>  The pick Denver traded to [[Seattle Seahawks|Seattle]] was used to select Pro Bowler [[Earl Thomas (defensive back)|Earl Thomas]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sbnation.com/nfl/2014/1/21/5329054/broncos-seahawks-super-bowl-draft-trade-earl-thomsas|title=Draft day trade could haunt Broncos|date=21 January 2014}}</ref> On July 26, 2009, Smith signed a four-year, $4.08 million contract with a $2.15 million signing bonus.  The contract allowed Smith to earn $750,000 through a one-time playing-time incentive that was guaranteed for injury.  In addition, if Smith won Defensive Rookie of the Year in 2009, he would have received $100,000.  The contract also included a $50,000 workout bonus in 2011 and a $130,000 workout bonus in 2012.  His base salary was $310,000 in 2009, $395,000 in 2010, $480,000 in 2011, and $565,000 in 2012.

===Detroit Lions===
On September 4, 2010, Smith was traded to the [[Detroit Lions]] for [[Tight end|TE]] [[Dan Gronkowski]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Klis |first=Mike |url=http://www.denverpost.com/broncos/ci_15993935 |title=Broncos trade CB Alphonso Smith to Detroit for TE Gronkowski |publisher=The Denver Post |date= 4 September 2010|accessdate=2012-10-27}}</ref> He had his first career interception on September 26 against the [[Minnesota Vikings]]. The following week, he beat [[Green Bay Packers]] receiver [[Greg Jennings]] on a jump ball for his second career interception. In a home game against the [[St. Louis Rams]] on October 10, Smith returned an interception 42 yards for a touchdown in the Lions' 44–6 win. Against the [[Washington Redskins]] on October 30, Smith had a big interception late in the game to help the Lions comeback to beat Washington. He led the Lions in interceptions for the 2010 season.

A memorable moment of his Detroit tenure came in a [[2010 Detroit Lions season#Week 12: vs. New England Patriots (Thanksgiving Day game)|Week 12 Thanksgiving loss]] to the Patriots in [[2010 Detroit Lions season|2010]]. Coming into the game, Smith was first on the team with five interceptions. While the Lions were leading in the third quarter, Smith taunted New England quarterback [[Tom Brady]] with a finger wag after an [[Incomplete pass|incompletion]]. Brady would target Smith on three of his next four touchdown passes, as the Patriots ultimately scored 24 points unanswered to win 45–24.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.essentiallysports.com/nfl-news-throwback-when-tom-brady-punished-alphonso-smith-for-mocking-him/ | title=THROWBACK: When Tom Brady Punished Alphonso Smith for Mocking Him | date=March 2021 }}</ref> Overall, he was thrown at seven times accounting for five catches and three touchdowns, the last of which led to him being benched.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.sbnation.com/nfl/2010/11/25/1836432/alphonso-smith-lions-patriots-thanksgiving | title=Alphonso Smith is Having a Rough Thanksgiving | date=25 November 2010 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.boston.com/sports/new-england-patriots/2010/11/26/smith_says_he_l/ | title=Smith says he let entire city down | date=November 26, 2010 }}</ref> Smith accepted responsibility for the turnaround, considering himself the catalyst and apologizing to the Detroit fans.<ref>{{cite web | last=Rosenthal | first=Gregg | title=Alphonso Smith blames himself for Lions loss | website=NBC Sports | date=2010-11-26 | url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/alphonso-smith-blames-himself-for-lions-loss | access-date=2025-07-31}}</ref>

On August 31, 2012, the Lions released Smith as one of their final roster cuts.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.freep.com/article/20120831/SPORTS01/120831079/detroit-lions-alphonso-smith-other-cuts?odyssey=tab%7Ctopnews%7Ctext%7CSports |title=Today's Lions cuts: Kellen Moore, Joique Bell make the 53-man roster |first=Dave |last=Birkett |date=August 31, 2012 |work=Detroit Free Press |access-date=November 26, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924113140/http://www.freep.com/article/20120831/SPORTS01/120831079/detroit-lions-alphonso-smith-other-cuts?odyssey=tab%7Ctopnews%7Ctext%7CSports |archive-date=September 24, 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was re-signed on October 18 due to injuries to [[Jacob Lacey]] and [[Bill Bentley (American football)|Bill Bentley]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.freep.com/article/20121018/SPORTS01/121018021/detroit-lions-alphonso-smith |title=Lions bring back cornerback Alphonso Smith, cut running back Keiland Williams | Detroit Lions | Detroit Free Press |publisher=freep.com |date=2012-10-18 |accessdate=2012-10-27}}</ref> In Week 7 against the [[Chicago Bears]], Smith was fined $15,750 for horse-collar tackling [[Brandon Marshall]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/fines-roundup-alphonso-smith-docked-for-horse-collar-tackle-0ap1000000085905|title=Fines roundup: Alphonso Smith docked for horse-collar tackle|work=[[National Football League]]|date=2012-10-26|access-date=2012-10-26}}</ref>

{{Short description|American gridiron football player and coach (born 1971)}} {{Use mdy dates|date=June 2024}} {{Infobox gridiron football biography | name = Alundis Brice | number = 23, 29, 21, 22 | position = [[Cornerback]], [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] | birth_date = {{Birth date and age|1970|5|1}} | birth_place = [[Brookhaven, Mississippi]], U.S. | height_ft = 5 | height_in = 10 | weight_lb = 178 | high_school = [[Brookhaven High School (Brookhaven, Mississippi)|Brookhaven (MS)]] | college = [[Ole Miss Rebels football|Mississippi]] | draftyear = 1995 | draftround = 4 | draftpick = 129 | pastteams = * [[Dallas Cowboys]] ({{NFL Year|1995|1996}}) * [[Philadelphia Eagles]] ({{NFL Year|1998}})* * [[Milwaukee Mustangs (1994–2001)|Milwaukee Mustangs]] ({{AFL Year|1998}}) * [[Tampa Bay Storm]] (1998) * [[Toronto Argonauts]] ({{CFL Year|1999}}) * [[Saskatchewan Roughriders]] ({{CFL Year|2000}}) | pastcoaching = * [[University of Idaho]] (2004–2006)
Cornerback coach * [[Portland State University]] (2007–2008)
Secondary coach | highlights = * [[Super Bowl champion]] ([[Super Bowl XXX|XXX]]) * Chuckie Mullins Courage Award (1994) * Second-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] ([[1994 College Football All-America Team|1994]]) * 2× First-team [[List of All-SEC football teams|All-SEC]] ([[1993 All-SEC football team|1993]], [[1994 All-SEC football team|1994]]) | statlabel1 = Total [[Tackle (football move)|tackle]]s | statvalue1 = 20 | statlabel2 = [[Interception]]s | statvalue2 = 1 | pfr = BricAl20 | afl = Alundis_Brice-1962 }} '''Alundis Marcell Brice''' (born May 1, 1971) is an American former professional [[Gridiron football|football]] [[cornerback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Dallas Cowboys]]. He was also a member of the [[Toronto Argonauts]] and [[Saskatchewan Roughriders]] in the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL). He played [[college football]] at the [[University of Mississippi]]. ==Early life== Brice attended [[Brookhaven High School (Brookhaven, Mississippi)|Brookhaven High School]], where he played as a [[wide receiver]] and [[cornerback]]. He received Class 5A All-State honors as a senior. He competed in [[track & field|track]], winning the state title in the [[200 metres]]. He accepted a football scholarship from the [[University of Mississippi]]. He was originally recruited as a [[wide receiver]], but after he didn't record a single reception as a sophomore even though he played in every game, he was converted into a [[cornerback]]. Brice was named the starter at [[cornerback|left cornerback]] as a junior, developing as a dominant player and a key part in the team leading all [[NCAA Division I]] schools in fewest total yards allowed per game (234.5). He had 7 interceptions (second in school history). He also became the second player in school history to return 2 interceptions for [[touchdown]]s in a single-season. As a senior, he changed his jersey number to 38, in honor of [[Chucky Mullins]] who was paralyzed in 1989. He started at left cornerback, registering 50 tackles (42 solo), 7 interceptions (4 interceptions in the last 2 games) and 9 passes defensed. At the end of the year he was shot in the chest while breaking up an on-campus altercation, with the bullet nearly hitting his heart. After an 11-day stay in the hospital, he resumed his preparation for the [[1995 NFL draft]].{{cite web| url=https://apnews.com/275a27008d2c6221e6a36814003fe368 | title=Former Mississippi defensive back Alundis Brice was released | website=[[Associated Press News]] | accessdate=January 3, 2020}} He practiced [[track & field|track]], posting personal best times of 10.75 seconds ([[100 metres]]), 21.62 seconds ([[200 metres]]) and 6.22 seconds ([[55 metres]]) as a sophomore. ==Professional career== ===Dallas Cowboys=== Brice was selected by the [[Dallas Cowboys]] in the fourth round (129th overall) of the [[1995 NFL draft]], after he dropped because of health concerns.{{Cite web |title=1995 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1995/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-31 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} When the team acquired [[Deion Sanders]], Brice was given a [[BMW]] car to switch jersey numbers so that Sanders could wear his #21, even though Brice had already stated he had no attachment to the number.{{cite web| url=http://www.espn.com/espn/page2/story?page=pearlman/080919&sportCat=nfl | title="Neon Deion" helped, and hindered, the 'Boys | accessdate=January 3, 2020}} As a rookie, he played on [[special teams]] and the [[nickel defense]]. He started against the [[Oakland Raiders]] in place of [[Larry Brown (cornerback)|Larry Brown]], who had missed the week because of a family tragedy. He finished the season with 9 defensive tackles, one interception, 2 passes defensed and 4 [[special teams]] tackles. In [[1996 NFL season|1996]], in the second game against the [[New York Giants]], he had a career-high 4 tackles. In the fourteenth game against the [[Arizona Cardinals]], he was making his second career start in place of an injured Sanders, when he suffered a torn anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee.{{cite web| url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1996-12-10-sp-7537-story.html | title=Cowboys' Brice and Bates Injured | website=[[Los Angeles Times]] | date=10 December 1996 | accessdate=January 3, 2020}} He was placed on the [[injured reserve list]]. He collected 11 defensive tackles (one for loss) and one [[special teams]] tackle. In [[1997 NFL season|1997]], he suffered a career-threatening injury during his rehab treatment, when his kneecap ruptured into two pieces. He recovered from the injury, but was released to make room for Sanders on August 21.{{cite web| url=https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/90112980/ | title=Deion finds religion, will play vs. Steelers | date=22 August 1997 | accessdate=January 3, 2020}} ===Philadelphia Eagles=== On April 24, [[1998 NFL season|1998]], he signed a one-year contract with the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] as a [[free agent]]. On August 25, he was released before the start of the season.{{cite news| url=https://www.nytimes.com/1998/08/26/sports/nfl-transactions.html | title=Transactions | work=The New York Times | date=26 August 1998 | accessdate=January 3, 2020}} ===Milwaukee Mustangs=== On March 20, [[1998 Arena Football League season|1998]], he was signed by the [[Milwaukee Mustangs (1994–2001)|Milwaukee Mustangs]] of the [[Arena Football League]].{{cite web| url=https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/499579315/ | title=Transactions | date=21 March 1998 | accessdate=January 3, 2020}} He was activated on October 15.{{cite web| url=https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/274079065/ | title=Transactions | date=16 October 1998 | accessdate=January 3, 2020}} ===Tampa Bay Storm=== On November 10, [[1998 Arena Football League season|1998]], the [[Tampa Bay Storm]] selected Brice in the third round of the expansion draft, using a pick they obtained in a trade with the [[Buffalo Destroyers]]. He was waived on April 18, [[1999 Arena Football League season|1999]]. ===Toronto Argonauts=== On June 11, [[1999 CFL season|1999]], he was signed as a [[free agent]] by the [[Toronto Argonauts]] of the [[Canadian Football League]], to play [[free safety]].{{cite web| url=https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/486022327/ | title=Transactions | date=12 June 1999 | accessdate=January 3, 2020}} He appeared in 18 games, tallying 35 defensive tackles, 2 fumble recoveries and 2 [[special teams]] tackles. ===Saskatchewan Roughriders=== On April 20, [[2000 CFL season|2000]], he signed with the [[Saskatchewan Roughriders]] of the [[Canadian Football League]].{{cite web| url=https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/77267515/ | title=Transactions | date=21 April 2000 | accessdate=January 3, 2020}} He was a backup [[free safety]], appearing in 4 games and making 14 tackles. He wasn't re-signed after the season. ==Personal life== In 2002, he began his coaching career as a graduate football assistant at the [[University of Alabama-Birmingham]]. In 2003, he was a defensive graduate assistant at the [[University of Mississippi]].{{cite web| url=https://olemisssports.com/news/2004/2/19/Cutcliffe_Announces_Staff_Position_Changes_For_2004 | title=Cutcliffe Announces Staff Position Changes For 2004 | date=19 February 2004 | accessdate=January 3, 2020}} In 2004, he was hired as the cornerback assistant coach for the [[University of Idaho]].{{cite news| url=https://www.nytimes.com/2004/01/08/sports/transactions-878758.html | title=Transactions | work=The New York Times | date=8 January 2004 | accessdate=January 3, 2020}} From 2007 to 2008, he was the secondary coach at [[Portland State University]].{{cite web| url=https://www.oregonlive.com/vikings/2009/02/glanville_names_new_assistant.html | title=Glanville names new assistant coach | date=26 February 2009 | accessdate=January 3, 2020}} From 2017 to 2019, he was an employment area Director with SL Start, later called Compass Careers Solutions. ==References== {{Reflist|30em}} ==External links== *[https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/179268215/ Another Bump In Road For Brice In Comeback Tonight] {{Cowboys1995DraftPicks}} {{Super Bowl XXX}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Brice, Alundis}} [[Category:1971 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:People from Brookhaven, Mississippi]] [[Category:Players of American football from Mississippi]] [[Category:American football cornerbacks]] [[Category:Ole Miss Rebels football players]] [[Category:Ole Miss Rebels men's track and field athletes]] [[Category:Dallas Cowboys players]] [[Category:Tampa Bay Storm players]] [[Category:Milwaukee Mustangs (1994–2001) players]] [[Category:Toronto Argonauts players]] [[Category:Saskatchewan Roughriders players]] [[Category:UAB Blazers football coaches]] [[Category:Ole Miss Rebels football coaches]] [[Category:Idaho Vandals football coaches]] [[Category:Portland State Vikings football coaches]]

'''Alonzo Loqwone Mitz''' (born June 5, 1963) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive end]] for seven seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) during the 1980s and early 1990s.  Mitz played [[college football]] for the [[Florida Gators football|Florida Gators]], and thereafter, played in the NFL for the [[Seattle Seahawks]] and the [[Cincinnati Bengals]].

== Early life ==

Mitz was born in [[Henderson, North Carolina]], in 1963.<ref name="pfrprofile">{{Cite web |title=Alonzo Mitz Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MitzAl20.htm |access-date=2025-08-18 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>  He attended [[Fort Pierce Central High School]] in [[Fort Pierce, Florida]],<ref name=dbfprofile>databaseFootball.com, Players, {{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20110515014716/http://www.databasefootball.com/players/playerpage.htm?ilkid=MITZALO01  Alonzo Mitz]}}.  Retrieved March 18, 2011.</ref> and played high school football for the Fort Pierce Central Cobras.

== College career ==

Mitz attended the [[University of Florida]] in Gainesville, Florida, where he played for coach [[Charley Pell]] and coach [[Galen Hall]]'s [[Florida Gators football|Gators]] teams from [[1982 Florida Gators football team|1982]] to [[1985 Florida Gators football team|1985]].<ref name=ufmediaguide>''[http://web.gatorzone.com/football/media/2011/media_guide.pdf  2011 Florida Gators Football Media Guide] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120402035222/http://web.gatorzone.com/football/media/2011/media_guide.pdf |date=April 2, 2012 }}'', University Athletic Association, Gainesville, Florida, pp. 105, 110, 115, 184 (2011).  Retrieved August 31, 2011.</ref>

== Professional career ==

Mitz was selected by the [[Seattle Seahawks]] in the eighth round (211th pick overall) of the [[1986 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1986 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1986/draft.htm |access-date=2023-10-03 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He played for the Seahawks from {{NFL Year|1986}} to {{NFL Year|1989}}.<ref name=nflprofile>National Football League, Historical Players, [http://www.nfl.com/players/alonzomitz/profile?id=MIT808128  Alonzo Mitz].  Retrieved March 18, 2001.</ref>   He played the last two seasons of his NFL career for the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] in {{NFL Year|1990}} and {{NFL Year|1991}}.<ref name=pfrprofile/>  During his six-season NFL career, he played in seventy-one games, started thirty-four of them, and compiled eight [[quarterback sack]]s and two [[interception]]s.<ref name=pfrprofile/>

'''Alshon Jeffery''' (born February 14, 1990) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[South Carolina Gamecocks football|South Carolina Gamecocks]], earning first-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors in 2010. Jeffery was selected by the [[Chicago Bears]] in the second round of the [[2012 NFL draft]]. As a member of the [[Philadelphia Eagles]], he won [[Super Bowl LII]]. South Carolina [[retired number|retired his number]] in 2023.

==Early life==
Jeffery attended [[Calhoun County High School]] in [[St. Matthews, South Carolina]], where he was part of a four-time state championship winning [[basketball]] team that recorded an 84–1 record.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Low |first=Chris |date=March 9, 2009 |title=A peek into recruiting with South Carolina's Jeffery |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/sec/post/_/id/1490 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181012014548/http://www.espn.com/blog/sec/post/_/id/1490 |archive-date=October 12, 2018 |access-date=October 11, 2018 |work=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> He also played two years of [[high school football|football]] and was widely recruited, giving a verbal commitment to the [[University of Southern California]] before switching his commitment to the [[University of South Carolina]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Alshon Jeffery, South Carolina Gamecocks, Wide Receiver |url=https://247sports.com/Player/Alshon-Jeffery-6838/college-25170/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221020204428/https://247sports.com/Player/Alshon-Jeffery-6838/college-25170/ |archive-date=October 20, 2022 |access-date=October 11, 2018 |work=247 Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> Jeffery's younger brother, Shamier Jeffery, committed to play football for the [[South Carolina Gamecocks football|Gamecocks]] in 2011, following in the footsteps of both of Jeffery's two older brothers Charles Ben and Darren Ben; both of whom also played basketball and football for Calhoun County High School.

==College career==

[[File:AlshonRetired2023.jpg|thumb|Jeffery's name being illuminated at [[Williams-Brice Stadium]] for the first time after his jersey number was retired in September 2023.]]

===2009 season===
As a freshman, Jeffery caught five [[Forward pass|passes]] for 61 yards in his first five games before making seven catches for 138 yards and three [[touchdown]]s against the [[2009 Kentucky Wildcats football team|University of Kentucky]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alshon Jeffery 2009 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/alshon-jeffery-1/gamelog/2009/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210723151201/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/alshon-jeffery-1/gamelog/2009/ |archive-date=July 23, 2021 |access-date=October 20, 2022 |website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com}}</ref> The performance was the second-best single-game performance in school history and Jeffery became the third Gamecock in 2009 to earn SEC Freshman of the Week, following defensive end [[Devin Taylor (American football)|Devin Taylor]] and running back [[Jarvis Giles]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Anderson |first=Reggie |date=October 12, 2009 |title=Jeffrey Named SEC Freshman of the Week |url=https://www.wltx.com/article/sports/ncaa/usc-gamecocks/jeffrey-named-sec-freshman-of-the-week/101-380406263 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221020204428/https://www.wltx.com/article/sports/ncaa/usc-gamecocks/jeffrey-named-sec-freshman-of-the-week/101-380406263 |archive-date=October 20, 2022 |access-date=October 20, 2022 |website=wltx.com |language=en-US}}</ref> He was a consensus first-team Freshman All-SEC and first-team Freshman All-American in recognition of his successful freshman season.

===2010 season===
In a Week 4 game against [[2010 Auburn Tigers football team|Auburn]], Jeffery had a breakout performance in the 35–27 loss. He was only a few yards shy of 200 receiving yards and added two touchdowns for the Gamecocks.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 26, 2010 |title=COL FB: Auburn 35, South Carolina 27 |url=https://www.upi.com/COL-FB-Auburn-35-South-Carolina-27/69501285477505/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181012054040/https://www.upi.com/COL-FB-Auburn-35-South-Carolina-27/69501285477505/ |archive-date=October 12, 2018 |access-date=October 11, 2018 |website=UPI |language=en}}</ref>  Another one of his best games in 2010 came against in-state rival [[2010 Clemson Tigers football team|Clemson]] where he had five catches for 141 yards and a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 27, 2010 |title=Garcia, No. 18 South Carolina thump Clemson |url=https://www.wltx.com/article/sports/ncaaf/garcia-no-18-south-carolina-thump-clemson/101-379008642 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221020204428/https://www.wltx.com/article/sports/ncaaf/garcia-no-18-south-carolina-thump-clemson/101-379008642 |archive-date=October 20, 2022 |access-date=October 11, 2018 |website=WLTX |language=en-US}}</ref> Through 14 games, Jeffery made 88 catches totaling 1,517 yards and nine touchdowns including eight games with 100 yards or more receiving, and a 108.4 yd/game average.  Jeffery was named a [[Biletnikoff Award]] finalist, the award given to the season's outstanding receiver. Because of his performances, helping lead the Gamecocks to their first SEC Championship Game appearance in school history, Jeffery was selected as an [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]].

==== 2013 season ====
In 2013's Week 4 loss to the [[2013 Detroit Lions season|Detroit Lions]], Jeffery recorded his first career 100-yard receiving game. The following week against the [[2013 New Orleans Saints season|New Orleans Saints]], Jeffery broke the Bears single-game receiving yards record with 218 yards, along with recording a career-high 10 receptions.  Jeffery broke the record on the final play of the game, a 21-yard pass from Jay Cutler, passing [[Harlon Hill]]'s record set in 1952 against the 49ers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mayer |first=Larry |date=October 6, 2013 |title=Jeffery sets Bears record in loss to Saints |url=http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-1/Jeffery-sets-Bears-record-in-loss-to-Saints/e4be4c81-37b1-4eee-869b-b85a82179b96 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131009112202/http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-1/Jeffery-sets-Bears-record-in-loss-to-Saints/e4be4c81-37b1-4eee-869b-b85a82179b96 |archive-date=October 9, 2013 |access-date=October 6, 2013 |publisher=[[Chicago Bears]]}}</ref> In Week 13 against the [[Minnesota Vikings]], Jeffery became the first player in franchise history to record two 200-yard games in the same season. ===Philadelphia Eagles===

====2017 season====
[[File:Alshon Jeffery vs. Redskins 2017.jpg|thumb|Jeffery at an Eagles game in 2017.|333x333px]]
On March 9, 2017, Jeffery signed a one-year, $14 million contract with the [[Philadelphia Eagles]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=March 9, 2017 |title=Alshon Jeffery, Eagles agree to one-year deal |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/alshon-jeffery-eagles-agree-to-one-year-deal-0ap3000000791958 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170310014730/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000791958/article/alshon-jeffery-eagles-agree-to-oneyear-deal |archive-date=March 10, 2017 |access-date=October 20, 2022 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> Jeffery made his Eagles debut on September 10, 2017, in the season opener against the [[2017 Washington Redskins season|Washington Redskins]]. He finished the game with 38 yards on three catches.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 10, 2017 |title=Philadelphia Eagles at Washington Redskins – September 10th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709100was.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171007220137/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709100was.htm |archive-date=October 7, 2017 |access-date=October 20, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In Week 2 on September 17 at [[2017 Kansas City Chiefs season|Kansas City]], Jeffery had 92 yards on 7 catches and one touchdown, his first as an Eagle, in a 27–20 loss to the Chiefs.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 17, 2017 |title=Philadelphia Eagles at Kansas City Chiefs – September 17th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709170kan.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190723203219/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709170kan.htm |archive-date=July 23, 2019 |access-date=October 20, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On December 2, 2017, Jeffery signed a four-year extension worth $52 million with $27 million guaranteed.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bergman |first=Jeremy |date=December 2, 2017 |title=Eagles sign Alshon Jeffery to 4-year pact through 2021 |url=http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000886208/article/eagles-sign-alshon-jeffery-to-4year-extension-through-2021 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171202203848/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000886208/article/eagles-sign-alshon-jeffery-to-4year-extension-through-2021 |archive-date=December 2, 2017 |access-date=October 20, 2022 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

The Eagles finished the season 13–3 and earned a first round bye. In the [[2017–18 NFL playoffs#NFC: Philadelphia Eagles 15, Atlanta Falcons 10|Divisional Round]] against the [[Atlanta Falcons]], Jeffery recorded 4 catches for 61 yards in a 15–10 victory. In the [[2017–18 NFL playoffs#NFC: Philadelphia Eagles 38, Minnesota Vikings 7|NFC Championship]] against the [[Minnesota Vikings]], Jeffery caught five passes for 85 yards and two touchdowns in 38–7 victory to advance to [[Super Bowl LII]]. In the Super Bowl, Jeffery caught 3 passes for 73 yards and scored the first touchdown of the game. The Eagles went on to defeat the [[New England Patriots]] 41–33 to give Jeffery and the franchise its first Super Bowl championship.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wesseling |first=Chris |date=February 4, 2018 |title=Philadelphia Eagles win Super Bowl LII |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/philadelphia-eagles-knock-off-patriots-win-super-bowl-0ap3000000914459 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200405021345/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000914459/article/philadelphia-eagles-knock-off-patriots-win-super-bowl |archive-date=April 5, 2020 |access-date=February 4, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On February 21, 2018, it was revealed that Jeffery underwent surgery for a torn rotator cuff.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sessler |first=Marc |date=February 21, 2018 |title=Eagles WR Alshon Jeffery undergoes shoulder surgery |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/eagles-wr-alshon-jeffery-undergoes-shoulder-surgery-0ap3000000916962 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180221170649/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000916962/article/eagles-wr-alshon-jeffery-undergoes-shoulder-surgery |archive-date=February 21, 2018 |access-date=February 21, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

====2018 season====
Jeffery underwent rotator cuff surgery in the offseason. He was kept out of action going into the regular season.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Caron |first=Emily |date=September 7, 2018 |title=Eagles' Alshon Jeffery still weeks away from return |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2018/09/07/alshon-jeffery-injury-news-eagles-shoulder-surgery-rehab |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181206235332/https://www.si.com/nfl/2018/09/07/alshon-jeffery-injury-news-eagles-shoulder-surgery-rehab |archive-date=December 6, 2018 |access-date=October 20, 2022 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |language=en-us}}</ref> In Week 4 of the 2018 season, Jeffery returned from his injury and recorded eight receptions for 105 receiving yards and a touchdown against the Tennessee Titans.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bobick |first=Ben |date=September 30, 2018 |title=Titans OT gamble pays off as they take down the Super Bowl champs |url=http://www.wrcbtv.com/story/39202032/titans-ot-gamble-pays-off-as-they-take-down-the-super-bowl-champs |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181012014622/http://www.wrcbtv.com/story/39202032/titans-ot-gamble-pays-off-as-they-take-down-the-super-bowl-champs |archive-date=October 12, 2018 |access-date=October 11, 2018 |website=WRCBTV |language=en}}</ref> In Week 6, against the New York Giants, he had eight receptions for 74 receiving yards and two touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 15, 2018 |title=Eagles got creative to involve Alshon Jeffery |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/eagles/eagles-film-review-alshon-jeffery-shows-screen-game |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181207045521/https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/eagles/eagles-film-review-alshon-jeffery-shows-screen-game |archive-date=December 7, 2018 |access-date=December 6, 2018 |website=NBC Sports Philadelphia}}</ref> The Eagles ended up making the [[2018–19 NFL playoffs]] with a 9–7 record. In the Wild Card round, Jeffery made six receptions for 82 receiving yards against his former team, the [[Chicago Bears]]. The Eagles won 16–15. In the [[2018–19 NFL playoffs|Divisional Round]] matchup against the [[New Orleans Saints]], Jeffery had 5 catches for 63 yards.  As the Eagles were on a successful drive late in the 4th quarter, a wide open Jeffery dropped a pass from [[Nick Foles]] that fell into the hands of Saints' cornerback [[Marshon Lattimore]].  After the interception, Jeffery and the Eagles' offense never got the ball back as the Saints won 20–14.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rabalais |first=Scott |date=January 13, 2019 |title=Marshon Lattimore's two big interceptions turn tide, save day for Saints against Eagles |url=https://www.nola.com/sports/saints/article_d72371a3-59fc-57af-afd4-f56e469da96c.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190813055528/https://www.nola.com/sports/saints/article_d72371a3-59fc-57af-afd4-f56e469da96c.html |archive-date=August 13, 2019 |access-date=August 12, 2019 |website=The Times-Picayune/The New Orleans Advocate}}</ref>
In the postgame interview, Jeffery stated that "It sucks right now. Everyone in the locker room, we're all down.  Like I said, I let my teammates down, I let the city of Philadelphia down.  That's on me.  We'll be back next year for sure.  One play don't define me, it happens.  It's part of football.  I just hated the way it happened in the playoffs, and it was the final moment."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stites |first=Adam |date=January 13, 2019 |title=Alshon Jeffery is taking the blame, but the Eagles' loss is not his fault |url=https://www.sbnation.com/2019/1/13/18181476/alshon-jeffery-philadelphia-eagles-drop-2019-nfl-playoffs |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190816052637/https://www.sbnation.com/2019/1/13/18181476/alshon-jeffery-philadelphia-eagles-drop-2019-nfl-playoffs |archive-date=August 16, 2019 |access-date=August 15, 2019 |website=www.sbnation.com}}</ref>

'''Alterraun Ennis Verner''' (born December 13, 1988) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[cornerback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[UCLA Bruins football|UCLA Bruins]], earning first-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors. Verner was selected by the [[Tennessee Titans]] in the fourth round of the [[2010 NFL draft]]. He was voted second-team [[All-Pro]] and named to the [[Pro Bowl]] with the Titans in 2013. He also played for the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] and [[Miami Dolphins]].

==Early life==
Verner attended [[Mayfair High School]] in [[Lakewood, California]], where he played [[wide receiver]], defensive back, linebacker, and [[special teams]]. As a senior, he had 50 receptions for 907 yards and 13 touchdowns. On defense, he made 56 tackles and four interceptions (one returned for a 102-yard touchdown). Verner earned second-team All-[[CIF Southern Section]] honors and was selected to play in Shrine All-Star Game, where he played for legendary coach Andrew Slome.

Verner also [[Letterman (sports)|lettered]] all four seasons in [[track & field]] for coach Josh Barker. Prior to high school, Verner won a silver medal in the 1500 meters at the 1997 California State Game, and placed fourth in the 4×100 relay at the 2000 USATF Youth Nationals. As a freshman at Mayfair, he was selected as the team's Most Valuable Performer, and was the league champ in both the 110m and [[Hurdling|300m hurdle]] (45.0) events. As a sophomore, he was the league champ in 4x400 relay, second in 110m high hurdles and [[high jump]] (6–2). As a junior, he served as team co-captain, earning Suburban League Academic All-League honors. He was the league champ in the high jump (6–4) and {{nowrap|4 × 100 m}} relay. As a senior, he had bests of {{convert|6|ft|6|in|m|abbr=on}} in the high jump, {{convert|20|ft|10|in|m|abbr=on}} in the [[long jump]], 10.7 in the [[100-meter dash]] and 39.70 in the 300m hurdles.

An excellent student, Verner held a 4.17 [[grade point average|GPA]] and achieved a 1740 [[SAT]] score. He also served as a peer tutor to his high school football team in the subjects of math and history. Considered a three-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Verner was listed as the No. 49 cornerback prospect in the nation.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 30, 2006 |title=Cornerbacks 2006 |url=https://footballrecruiting.rivals.com/viewrank.asp?ra_key=1158 |website=Rivals.com}}</ref> He chose UCLA over [[Boston College]], [[University of Oregon|Oregon]], and [[University of Washington|Washington]].

==College career==
In his [[true freshman]] year at [[University of California, Los Angeles|UCLA]], Verner finished fourth among his Bruins teammates with 59 tackles and third among his team with two interceptions, while leading the team with 123 interception yards and two touchdowns. He was named co-Freshman of the Year for the Pac-10 Conference (alongside [[Jairus Byrd]] and [[Taylor Mays]]), and was selected first-team Freshman All-America by [[College Football News]] and Scripps/FWAA, as well as second-team by ''[[The Sporting News]]'', [[Scout.com]], and Rivals.com.

As a sophomore, Verner appeared in all 13 games with 10 starts, and ranked fourth on the team with 75 tackles. He finished with 15 pass breakups and four interceptions. In his junior year, Verner was a starter in all 12 games, and was second on the team in tackles with 73. He was selected to the second-team All-Pac-10 squad chosen by the league's coaches.

In November 2009, Verner was named one of the twelve semifinalists for the 2009 [[Jim Thorpe Award]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 3, 2009 |title=Jim Thorpe Award Names 2009 Semi-Finalists |url=http://www.jimthorpeassoc.org/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=202:jim-thorpe-award-names-2009-semi-finalists&catid=5:news&Itemid=4 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120219183643/http://www.jimthorpeassoc.org/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=202:jim-thorpe-award-names-2009-semi-finalists&catid=5:news&Itemid=4 |archive-date=February 19, 2012 |website=Jim Thorpe Association}}</ref>

In his senior year, he started in all 13 games and finished with 72 tackles, of which 51 were solo. He also had five interceptions and 158 return yards, with one of them resulting in a touchdown. He had a second defensive touchdown as a fumble recovery.

In 2011, Verner returned to UCLA during the [[NFL]] off-season to complete his Bachelor of Science degree in [[mathematics]].<ref>{{cite web | last=Yoon | first=Peter | title=Yoon: Degree on Verner's lockout to-do list | website=ESPN.com | date=2011-06-07 | url=https://www.espn.com/los-angeles/nfl/news/story?id=6635659 | access-date=2025-05-02}}</ref> He graduated later that year with a degree in mathematics/applied science.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tuanh Dam |title=Alterraun Verner |url=http://graphics.dailybruin.com/alterraun-verner/ |access-date=March 25, 2018 |publisher=Daily Bruin}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Pre-draft===
Verner attended the [[NFL Scouting Combine]] and performed all of the combine and positional drills. On March 30, 2010, he attended UCLA's pro day and ran all of the combine drills again, but opted to skip the short shuttle and three-cone drill. He was able to earn better times in the 40-yard dash (4.52s) and 20-yard dash (2.63s), while also adding height to his vertical (32.5"). At the conclusion of the pre-draft process, he was projected to be a fourth or fifth round pick by NFL draft experts and scouts. He was ranked as the 18th best cornerback prospect in the draft by DraftScout.com and was also ranked the 24th best cornerback prospect in the draft by WalterFootball.com.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2010 NFL Draft Rankings: Cornerback |url=http://walterfootball.com/draft2010CB.php |access-date=April 22, 2018 |website=walterfootball.com}}</ref><ref name="DraftScout">{{Cite web |title=Alterraun Verner, DS #18 CB, UCLA |url=http://draftscout.com/dsprofile.php?PlayerId=66655&DraftYear=2010 |access-date=March 14, 2014 |website=DraftScout.com}}</ref>
