====2010====
On June 15, 2010, the Tennessee Titans signed Verner to a four-year, [[United States dollar|$]]3.16 million [[contract]] that includes a [[signing bonus]] of $790,035.<ref name="spotrac">{{Cite web |title=Spotrac.com: Alterraun Verner contract |url=http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/miami-dolphins/alterraun-verner-6612/ |access-date=April 22, 2018 |website=Spotrac.com}}</ref>

Throughout training camp, Verner competed for starting cornerback against veterans [[Jason McCourty]] and [[Ryan Mouton]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Daniels, David |date=August 2, 2010 |title=Tennessee Titans Training Camp: McCourty, Mouton, Verner Battle To Start |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/428830-tennessee-titans-training-camp-mccourty-mouton-verner-battle-to-start |access-date=April 22, 2018 |website=bleacherreport.com}}</ref> Head coach [[Jeff Fisher]] named Verner the third cornerback on the depth chart to start the regular season, behind veterans McCourty and [[Cortland Finnegan]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Tennessee Titans Depth Chart: 09/05/2010 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/111/TEN |access-date=March 23, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rayburn, Ryan |date=May 13, 2010 |title=2010 NFL Preview: Projected Depth Chart of the Tennessee Titans Defense |url=http://bleacherreport.com/articles/391857-tennessee-titans-projected-defensive-depth-chart |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101201213535/http://bleacherreport.com/articles/391857-tennessee-titans-projected-defensive-depth-chart |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 1, 2010 |access-date=April 22, 2018 |website=bleacherreport.com}}</ref>

He made his professional regular season debut in the Tennessee Titans' season-opener against the [[2010 Oakland Raiders season|Oakland Raiders]] and was credited with two tackles in their 38–13 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Game Center: Week 1–2010: Oakland Raiders @ Tennessee Titans |url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2010091205/2010/REG1/raiders@titans |access-date=April 22, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> The following week, Verner and teammate [[Patrick Bailey (American football)|Patrick Bailey]] tackled wide receiver [[Antonio Brown]] during an 18-yard return for Verner's first physical tackle of his career during a 19–11 loss to the [[2010 Pittsburgh Steelers|Pittsburgh Steelers]]. He finished the game with two combined tackles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Game Center: Week 2-2010: Pittsburgh Steelers @ Tennessee Titans |url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2010091904/2010/REG2/steelers@titans |access-date=April 22, 2010 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On October 3, Verner earned his first career start after McCourty suffered a broken right forearm the previous week and would have to undergo surgery; the latter missed four games (Weeks 4–7).<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 29, 2010 |title=Titans CB McCoutry recovering from arm surgery |url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sdut-titans-cb-mccoutry-recovering-from-arm-surgery-2010sep29-story.html |access-date=March 23, 2018 |website=sandiegouniontribune.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=October 1, 2010 |title=Titans CB McCourty has forearm surgery, out vs. Broncos |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/cb-mccourty-out-vs-broncos-after-forearm-surgery-09000d5d81afc4cf |access-date=March 23, 2010 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> Verner finished his first start with a season-high 11 solo tackles and three pass deflections during a 26–20 loss to the [[2010 Denver Broncos|Denver Broncos]]. In Week 5, Verner recorded nine combined tackles, a pass deflection, and made his first career interception off a pass by quarterback [[Tony Romo]] in the Titans' 34–27 victory at the [[2010 Dallas Cowboys|Dallas Cowboys]]. His interception occurred in the fourth quarter off a screen pass intended for tight end [[Martellus Bennett]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Game Center: Week 5-2010: Tennessee Titans @ Dallas Cowboys |url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2010101010/2010/REG5/titans@cowboys |access-date=April 22, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> In Week 14, Verner collected 12 combined tackles (ten solo) in the Titans' 30–28 loss to the [[2010 Indianapolis Colts|Indianapolis Colts]]. The following week, Verner made ten combined tackles (four solo), deflected a pass, and intercepted a pass by quarterback [[Matt Schaub]] during a 31–17 victory over the [[2010 Houston Texans|Houston Texans]].<ref name="stats10">{{Cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Alterraun Verner (2010) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/alterraunverner/494317/gamelogs?season=2010 |access-date=April 22, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He finished his rookie season with 101 combined tackles (85 solo), 11 pass deflections, three interceptions, and a forced fumble in 16 games with 12 starts.<ref name="career">{{Cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Alterraun Verner (career) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/alterraunverner/494317/careerstats |access-date=April 22, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

====2011====
On January 28, 2011, the Titans announced the firing of head coach Fisher after they finished fourth in the [[AFC South]] with a 6–10 record the previous season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jeff Fisher out in Tennessee |url=http://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=6066144 |access-date=April 23, 2018 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> Defensive coordinator [[Jerry Gray]] held a competition between Verner and McCourty to name a starting cornerback.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 2, 2011 |title=The Jason McCourty vs Alterraun Verner Debate: Part II |url=http://thesportsdaily.com/2011/08/02/the-jason-mccourty-vs-alterraun-verner-debate-part-ii/ |access-date=April 22, 2018 |website=thesportsdaily.com}}</ref> New head coach [[Mike Munchak]] named Verner the third cornerback on the depth chart to begin the season, behind Finnegan and McCourty.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Tennessee Titans Depth Chart: 09/04/2011 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/123/TEN |access-date=March 23, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref>

In Week 2, Verner made one tackle, broke up a pass, and intercepted quarterback [[Joe Flacco]] in the Titans' 26–13 victory against the [[2011 Baltimore Ravens|Baltimore Ravens]]. On December 11, Verner collected a season-high 11 combined tackles (nine solo) during a 22–17 loss to the [[2011 New Orleans Saints|New Orleans Saints]] in Week 14.<ref name="stats11">{{Cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Alterraun Verner (2011) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/alterraunverner/494317/gamelogs?season=2011 |access-date=April 22, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He finished the {{NFL Year|2011}} season with 49 combined tackles (43 solo), eight pass deflections, and an interception in 16 games with three starts.<ref name="career" />

====2012====
Verner entered training camp in 2012 slated as a starting cornerback after Finnegan departed in free agency.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Motivation and Competition: Cornerback Position |url=http://breatheifyoulovefootball.blogspot.com/2012/08/you-compete-me-cornerback-position.html?m=1 |access-date=April 23, 2018 |website=breatheifyoulovefootball.blogspot.com}}</ref> Head coach Munchak officially named Verner and McCourty the starting cornerbacks to open the regular season, ahead of [[Ryan Mouton]] and [[Coty Sensabaugh]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Tennessee Titans Depth Chart: 09/01/2012 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/135/TEN |access-date=March 23, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref>

He started in the [[2012 Tennessee Titans|Tennessee Titans']] season-opener against the [[2012 New England Patriots|New England Patriots]], recording nine combined tackles in their 34–13 loss.<ref name="stats12" /> The following week, Verner collected six combined tackles, two pass deflections, and intercepted a pass by quarterback [[Philip Rivers]] during a 38–10 loss at the [[2012 San Diego Chargers|San Diego Chargers]] in Week 2.<ref name="stats12" /> On December 30, 2012, Verner collected a season-high ten combined tackles (eight solo) in the Titans' 38–20 victory against the [[2012 Jacksonville Jaguars|Jacksonville Jaguars]] in Week 17.<ref name="stats12">{{Cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Alterraun Verner (2012) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/alterraunverner/494317/gamelogs?season=2012 |access-date=April 23, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He finished the {{NFL Year|2012}} season with 81 combined tackles (64 solo), nine pass deflections, two interceptions, and a forced fumble in 16 games with 16 starts.<ref name="career" />

The Titans did not qualify for the playoffs for the third consecutive season after finishing last in their division with a 6–10 record.

====2013====
During minicamp, defensive coordinator Gray chose to try Verner at free safety. The latter returned to starting cornerback in training camp and saw minor competition from Sensabaugh, [[Blidi Wreh-Wilson]], and [[Tommie Campbell]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Huffman, Joshua |title=Poll Results: Tennessee Titans Should Extend Alterraun Verner When |url=https://www.titansized.com/2013/07/09/poll-results-tennessee-titans-should-extend-alterraun-verner-when/ |access-date=April 23, 2018 |website=titansized.com}}</ref> HC Munchak retained Verner and McCourty as the starting cornerback duo to open the 2013 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Tennessee Titans Depth Chart: 09/05/2013 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/150/TEN |access-date=April 23, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref>

He started in the [[2013 Tennessee Titans season|Titans]]' season-opener at the [[2013 Pittsburgh Steelers season|Pittsburgh Steelers]] and recorded three combined tackles, two pass deflections, and an interception in their 16–9 victory.<ref name="stats13" /> In Week 2, he made six combined tackles, a season-high three pass deflections, an interception, and scored his first career touchdown in the Titans' 30–24 overtime loss at the [[2013 Houston Texans season|Houston Texans]].<ref name="stats13" /> During the fourth quarter, Verner intercepted a pass by quarterback Matt Schaub intended for [[DeAndre Hopkins]] and returned it 23 yards to score.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Game Center: Week 2-2013: Tennessee Titans @ Houston Texans |url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2013091505/2013/REG2/titans@texans |access-date=April 23, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On September 29, 2013, Verner recorded two tackles, two pass deflections, and intercepted two pass attempts by [[New York Jets]]' rookie quarterback [[Geno Smith]] in their 38–13 victory.<ref name="stats13">{{Cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Alterraun Verner (2013) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/alterraunverner/494317/gamelogs?season=2013 |access-date=April 23, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> It marked Verner's first game of his career with multiple interceptions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Game Center: Week 4-2013: New York Jets @ Tennessee Titans |url=http://www.nfl.com/gamecenter/2013092908/2013/REG4/jets@titans |access-date=April 23, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On December 8, he collected a season-high nine combined tackles and broke up two passes in the Titans' 51–28 loss at the Denver Broncos in Week 14.

On December 27, Verner was announced as one of the players voted to the [[2014 Pro Bowl]]. It marked his first career Pro Bowl selection. He was voted second-team All-Pro and became the first Titans player to be selected for the [[Pro Bowl]] since 2010.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 27, 2013 |title=Titans CB Alterraun Verner Voted to Pro Bowl |url=http://titansonline.com/news/article-1/Titans-CB-Alterraun-Verner-Voted-to-Pro-Bowl/576bf8af-49e7-45c8-8bd1-baba09a6db16 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180424071341/http://www.titansonline.com/news/article-1/Titans-CB-Alterraun-Verner-Voted-to-Pro-Bowl/576bf8af-49e7-45c8-8bd1-baba09a6db16 |archive-date=April 24, 2018 |access-date=April 23, 2018 |website=titansonline.com}}</ref> He finished the {{NFL Year|2013}} season with 57 combined tackles (49 solo), a career-high 22 pass deflections, a career-high five interceptions, and a touchdown in 16 games with 16 starts.<ref name="career" /> Pro Football Focus gave Verner the 12th highest overall grade among cornerbacks in 2013.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Yuille, Sean |date=March 8, 2014 |title=Lions free agency rumors: Alterraun Verner drawing interest from Detroit |url=https://www.prideofdetroit.com/2014/3/8/5486494/lions-free-agency-rumors-alterraun-verner |access-date=April 23, 2018 |website=prideofdetroit.com}}</ref>

On March 3, 2014, it was reported by ''[[The Tennessean]]'' that the Titans elected not to use their [[franchise tag]] on Verner.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gantt, Darin |date=March 3, 2014 |title=Titans have no plans to use franchise tag on Alterraun Verner |url=https://www.profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/03/03/titans-have-no-plans-to-use-franchise-tag-on-alterraun-verner/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190207070639/https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/03/03/titans-have-no-plans-to-use-franchise-tag-on-alterraun-verner/ |archive-date=February 7, 2019 |access-date=April 23, 2018 |website=profootballtalk.nbcsports.com}}</ref> The two parties attempted to work on a long-term deal, but were unable to agree to terms on a contract.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bouda, Nate |date=March 3, 2014 |title=Titans aren't close to an agreement with CB Alterraun Verner |url=http://nfltraderumors.co/titans-arent-close-agreement-cb-alterraun-verner/}}</ref>

Verner was considered as a top free agent and reportedly drew interest from multiple teams, including the [[New York Jets]], [[Pittsburgh Steelers]], [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], [[Minnesota Vikings]], and the [[Detroit Lions]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cooling, Neal |date=March 9, 2014 |title=Steelers added to group of teams reportedly interested in CB Alterraun Verner |url=https://www.behindthesteelcurtain.com/platform/2014/3/9/5487212/steelers-free-agency-alterran-verner-cornerback-titans |access-date=April 23, 2018 |website=behindthesteelcurtain.com}}{{Dead link|date=September 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Free agent remours: Bookings interested in Alterraun Verner |url=https://www.thevikingage.com/2014/03/08/free-agent-rumors-vikings-interested-alterraun-verner/ |access-date=April 23, 2018 |website=thevikingage.com}}</ref>

===Tampa Bay Buccaneers===
On March 11, 2014, the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] signed Verner to a four-year, $25.75 million contract that includes $14 million guaranteed.<ref name="spotrac" /><ref>[https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/10592289/alterraun-verner-tampa-bay-buccaneers-agree-deal Alterraun Verner heads to Bucs]</ref>

====2014====
Bucs' Pro Bowler CB [[Darrelle Revis|Darelle Revis]] was cut the day after Verner was signed. As a result, Verner entered training camp slated as the No. 1 cornerback on the Buccaneers' depth chart.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sobleski, Brent |date=March 20, 2014 |title=Bucs sign Mike Jenkins as a potential starter |url=http://sportswire.usatoday.com/2014/03/20/tampa-bay-buccanneers-sign-mike-jenkins/ |access-date=April 23, 2018 |website=sportswire.usatoday.com}}</ref> The latter was sidelined for a portion of training camp and the preseason due to a [[hamstring]] injury. Head coach [[Lovie Smith]] officially named Verner the starter to begin the regular season alongside [[Mike Jenkins (American football)|Mike Jenkins]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stroud, Rick |date=September 4, 2014 |title=Mike Jenkins set to start for Bucs at cornerback |url=https://www.tampabay.com/sports/football/bucs/mike-jenkins-set-to-start-for-bucs-at-cornerback/2195983/ |access-date=April 23, 2018 |website=TampaBay.com}}</ref>

In Week 5, Verner made a season-high three pass deflections, five combined tackles, and intercepted a pass by quarterback [[Drew Brees]] in a 37–31 loss at the [[2014 New Orleans Saints|New Orleans Saints]].<ref name="stats14" /> He was sidelined again for two games (Weeks 10–11) to help heal his hamstring injury.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alterraun Verner Injury: Updates on Buccaneers CB's Hamstring and Return |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2176034-alterraun-verner-injury-updates-on-buccaneers-cbs-hamstring-and-return |access-date=April 23, 2018 |website=bleacherreport.com}}</ref> In Week 16, he collected a season-high nine combined tackles in the Buccaneers' 20–3 loss to the [[2014 Green Bay Packers|Green Bay Packers]].<ref name="stats14">{{Cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Alterraun Verner (2013) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/alterraunverner/494317/gamelogs?season=2014 |access-date=April 23, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He finished his first season in Tampa Bay with 76 combined tackles (58 solo), nine pass deflections, two interceptions, and two forced fumbles in 14 games with 14 starts.<ref name="career" />

====2015====
Defensive coordinator [[Leslie Frazier]] retained Verner and [[Johnthan Banks]] as the starting cornerback duo for the 2015 regular season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 26, 2015 |title=Alterraun Verner, Johnthan Banks only sure things at DB for Bucs |url=http://www.espn.com/blog/tampa-bay-buccaneers/post/_/id/10179/alterraun-verner-johnthan-banks-only-sure-things-at-db-for-bucs |access-date=April 23, 2018 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> Verner started in the first two regular season games before losing his spot to [[Tim Jennings]]. He was demoted to being the fourth cornerback on the depth chart, behind Jennings, Jenkins, and Banks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Philipse, Sander |date=October 12, 2015 |title=Alterraun Verner is a slot cornerback, the Bucs wanted to run on the Jaguars and more from snap counts |url=https://www.bucsnation.com/2015/10/12/9504957/alterraun-verner-is-a-slot-cornerback-the-bucs-wanted-to-run-on-the |access-date=April 23, 2018 |website=bucsnation.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Auman, Greg |date=October 3, 2015 |title=Alterraun Verner tumbles on Bucs' depth chart (w/video) |url=https://www.tampabay.com/sports/football/bucs/alterraun-verner-tumbles-on-bucs-depth-chart-wvideo/2248098/ |access-date=April 23, 2018 |website=TampaBay.com}}</ref> Verner competed against [[Sterling Moore]] to be the Buccaneers' nickelback, taking Moore's place on the depth chart.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Philipse, Sander |date=September 25, 2015 |title=Tim Jennings is taking Alterraun Verner's starting spot |url=https://www.bucsnation.com/2015/9/25/9399321/tim-jennings-is-taking-alterraun-verners-starting-spot |access-date=April 23, 2018 |website=bucsnation.com}}</ref> In Week 9, Verner collected a season-high eight solo tackles, a pass deflection, and intercepted a pass by quarterback [[Eli Manning]] in a 32–18 loss at the [[2015 New York Giants|New York Giants]].<ref name="stats15">{{Cite web |title=NFL Player stats: Alterraun Verner (2015) |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/alterraunverner/494317/gamelogs?season=2015 |access-date=April 23, 2018 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

He finished his second season with the Buccaneers recording 56 combined tackles (45 solo), four pass deflections, and an interception in 16 games with six starts.<ref name="career" /> He received a career-low overall grade of 42.6 from Pro Football Focus for the season.<ref name="PFF" />

====2016====
On January 6, 2016, it was reported that Buccaneers' general manager [[Jason Licht]] fired head coach [[Lovie Smith]] after Tampa Bay finished fourth in their division with a 6–10 record.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tampa Bay Buccaneers fire head coach Lovie Smith |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2016/01/06/lovie-smith-fired-tampa-bay-buccaneers |access-date=April 23, 2018 |website=SI.com}}</ref> Throughout training camp, Verner competed for a job as the starting cornerback against [[Brent Grimes]] and newly acquired first round pick [[Vernon Hargreaves]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Auman, Greg |date=July 29, 2016 |title=Bucs changes bring new chance for Alterraun Verner |url=https://www.tampabay.com/sports/football/bucs/bucs-changes-bring-new-chance-for-alterraun-verner/2287391/ |access-date=April 23, 2018 |website=tampabay.com}}</ref> New defensive coordinator [[Mike Smith (American football coach)|Mike Smith]] named Verner the starting cornerback, opposite Grimes, to start the regular season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Phillips, Sander |date=September 6, 2016 |title=Buccaneers'2016 depth chart: Vernon Hargreaves shares starting job |url=https://www.bucsnation.com/2016/9/6/12814072/buccaneers-2016-depth-chart-vernon-hargreaves-shares-starting-job |access-date=April 21, 2018 |website=bucsnation.com}}</ref> He started in the first two games, but was later demoted to being the fourth cornerback on Tampa Bay's depth chart, behind Grimes, Hargreaves, and [[Jude Adjei-Barimah]].<ref name="u365">{{cite web | last=Horchy | first=Eric | title=Bucs CB Verner Will Play Tomorrow In Father's Honor | website=Pewter Report | date=2016-11-26 | url=https://www.pewterreport.com/bucs-cb-verner-will-play-tomorrow-in-fathers-honor/ | access-date=2025-03-15}}</ref> In Week 11, he collected a season-high three solo tackles and two pass deflections during a 19–17 win at the [[2016 Kansas City Chiefs|Kansas City Chiefs]]. On November 27, Verner chose to play in the Buccaneers' Week 12 matchup against the [[2017 Seattle Seahawks|Seattle Seahawks]] after his father died two days prior from a sudden heart attack. He finished the Bucs' 14–5 victory with two combined tackles, two pass deflections, and intercepted a pass from quarterback [[Russell Wilson]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Matt, Bonnie |date=November 28, 2016 |title=Bucs' Alterraun Verner has phenomenal game in honor of father who passed away |url=https://www.bucswire.usatoday.com/2016/11/28/bucs-alterraun-verner-has-phenomenal-game-in-honor-of-father-who-passed-away/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161223170012/http://bucswire.usatoday.com/2016/11/28/bucs-alterraun-verner-has-phenomenal-game-in-honor-of-father-who-passed-away/ |archive-date=December 23, 2016 |access-date=April 23, 2018 |website=bucswire.usatoday.com}}</ref> He finished the {{NFL Year|2016}} season with 16 combined tackles (15 solo), seven pass deflections, and an interception in 16 games with three starts.<ref name="career" /> [[Pro Football Focus]] gave him an overall grade of 76.6, ranking 48th among all qualified cornerbacks in 2016.<ref name="PFF">{{Cite web |last=Cox, Lorin |date=July 26, 2017 |title=Dolphins place LB Koa Misi on IR, sign CB Alterraun Verner |url=https://www.profootballfocus.com/news/pro-dolphins-place-lb-koa-misi-on-ir-sign-cb-alterraun-verner |access-date=April 23, 2018 |website=profootballfocus.com}}</ref>

====2017====
On February 23, 2017, the Buccaneers released Verner to clear $6.5 million in cap space.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith, Scott |date=February 23, 2017 |title=Buccaneers Release Alterraun Verner |url=http://buccaneers.com/s/33201/embeddedNewsPath?newsGuid=a82e54d3-d177-4e51-8565-1ce67a94b950 |website=Buccaneers.com}}{{Dead link|date=September 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

===Miami Dolphins===
On July 25, 2017, the [[Miami Dolphins]] signed Verner to a one-year, $980,000 contract with an $80,000 signing bonus.<ref name="spotrac" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Patra, Kevin |date=July 25, 2017 |title=Dolphins sign Alterraun Verner, place Koa Misi on IR |url=http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000821922/article/dolphins-sign-alterraun-verner-place-koa-misi-on-ir |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170725231858/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000821922/article/dolphins-sign-alterraun-verner-place-koa-misi-on-ir |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 25, 2017 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

Throughout training camp, he competed for starting cornerback against [[Xavien Howard]], [[Byron Maxwell]], [[Bobby McCain]], [[Tony Lippett]], and [[Cordrea Tankersley]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Staley |first=Antwan |date=August 27, 2017 |title=Dolphins CB Alterraun Verner has a shot at winning starting job |url=https://www.dolphinswire.usatoday.com/2017/08/27/dolphins-verner-has-a-shot-at-winning-starting-cb-job/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171020204458/http://dolphinswire.usatoday.com/2017/08/27/dolphins-verner-has-a-shot-at-winning-starting-cb-job/ |archive-date=October 20, 2017 |access-date=April 23, 2018 |website=Dolphins Wire|publisher=USA Today}}</ref> Head coach [[Adam Gase]] named Verner the fourth cornerback on the Dolphins' depth chart to start the season, behind Howard, Maxwell, and McCain.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ourlads.com: Miami Dolphins Depth Chart: 10/01/2017 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/200/MIA |access-date=April 23, 2018 |website=Ourlads.com}}</ref>

On November 26, Verner recorded a season-high three solo tackles in a 35–17 loss at the [[2017 New England Patriots|New England Patriots]]. In Week 14, he had a season-high two pass deflections and three combined tackles in the Dolphins' 27–20 win against the Patriots. On December 31, he was inactive for the season finale against the [[Buffalo Bills]]; this was the only game he hadn't played in for the season. He finished the {{NFL Year|2017}} season with 15 combined tackles (12 solo) and four pass deflections in 15 games with two starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alterraun Verner 2017 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/V/VernAl99/gamelog/2017/ |access-date=2024-12-26 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Retirement===
On March 18, 2019, Verner announced his retirement from the [[NFL]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wyatt, Jim |date=March 18, 2019 |title=Former Titans CB Alterraun Verner Announces NFL Retirement |url=https://www.titansonline.com/news/former-titans-cb-alterraun-verner-announces-his-retirement-from-the-nfl |access-date=March 19, 2019 |website=TitansOnline.com}}</ref> On April 16, Verner signed a one-day contract to retire as a Tennessee Titan.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bacharach, Erik |date=April 17, 2019 |title=Alterraun Verner signs one-day contract to retire a Titan |url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/nfl/titans/2019/04/17/titans-alterraun-verner-retires-one-day-contract/3477036002/ |access-date=April 21, 2020 |website=Tennessean.com}}</ref>

'''Alonzo Al Johnson''' (April 4, 1963 – February 1, 2024) was an American professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] for two seasons with the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL) during the 1980s.  Johnson played [[college football]] for the [[Florida Gators football|Florida Gators]], and was recognized twice as a first-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]].  He was selected in the second round of the [[1986 NFL draft]].

== Early life ==
Alonzo Al Johnson was born in [[Panama City, Florida]].<ref name="pfrprofile">{{Cite web |title=Alonzo Johnson Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/J/JohnAl25.htm |access-date=2025-07-13 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>  He attended [[Rutherford High School (Florida)|Rutherford High School]] in Panama City,<ref name=dbfprofile>databaseFootball.com, Players, {{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20110610094218/http://www.databasefootball.com/players/playerpage.htm?ilkid=JOHNSALO01  Alonzo Johnson]}}.  Retrieved June 4, 2010.</ref> where he was a standout high school football player for the Rutherford Rams.

== College career ==
Johnson accepted an athletic scholarship to attend the [[University of Florida]] in Gainesville, Florida, where he played for coach [[Charley Pell]] and coach [[Galen Hall]]'s [[Florida Gators football]] teams from [[1982 Florida Gators football team|1982]] to [[1985 Florida Gators football team|1985]].<ref name=ufmediaguide>''[http://web.gatorzone.com/football/media/2011/media_guide.pdf  2011 Florida Gators Football Media Guide] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120402035222/http://web.gatorzone.com/football/media/2011/media_guide.pdf |date=April 2, 2012 }}'', University Athletic Association, Gainesville, Florida, pp. 87, 92, 96, 98, 124, 153, 182 (2011).  Retrieved August 29, 2011.</ref>  Johnson was a key member of the Gators' defense in [[1984 Florida Gators football team|1984]] and 1985 when the Gators posted identical 9–1–1 overall win–loss records and led the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) with best-in-the-conference records of 5–0–1 and 5–1, respectively.  He was a first-team [[List of All-SEC football teams|All-SEC]] selection and a first-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] in [[1984 College Football All-America Team|1984]] and [[1985 College Football All-America Team|1985]], and also a team captain both years.<ref name=ufmediaguide/>  He finished his four-year college career with 335 tackles, 55 tackles for a loss and 27 [[quarterback sack]]s.<ref name=ufmediaguide/>

Johnson was later voted to the Florida Gators' [[Florida Gators football#Florida Gator All-Century Team|All-Century Team]] and [[Florida Gators football#Florida's All-Time Roster|All-Time Team]],<ref name=ufmediaguide/> and inducted into the [[List of University of Florida Athletic Hall of Fame members|University of Florida Athletic Hall of Fame]] as a "Gator Great."<ref>F Club, Hall of Fame, [http://www.gatorfclub.org/hall-of-fame/greats  Gator Greats].  Retrieved December 14, 2014.</ref><ref>"[http://www.gatorzone.com/story.php?id=4231  Nine Former Gators Named to UF Hall of Fame] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924050234/http://www.gatorzone.com/story.php?id=4231 |date=2015-09-24 }}," GatorZone.com (April 4, 2002).  Retrieved July 21, 2011.</ref>  In 2006, he was ranked as No. 35 among the top 100 Gators of the first century of Florida football by the sportswriters of ''The Gainesville Sun''.<ref>Robbie Andreu & Pat Dooley, "[http://www.gainesville.com/article/20060730/GATORS70/60724025?tc=ar  No. 35 Alonzo Johnson]," ''The Gainesville Sun'' (July 30, 2006).  Retrieved April 2, 2013.</ref>

== Professional career ==
Johnson was selected by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] in the second round (48th overall) of the [[1986 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1986 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1986/draft.htm |access-date=2023-10-02 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He played for the Eagles from {{NFL Year|1986}} to {{NFL Year|1987}}.<ref>National Football League, Historical Players, [https://www.nfl.com/players/profile?id=JOH043713  Alonzo Johnson].  Retrieved May 21, 2010.</ref>  As a rookie, he played in fifteen games and started nine of them at rightside linebacker, with three interceptions.<ref name=pfrprofile/>  He left the Eagles before the beginning of the 1987 season in order to enter a drug rehabilitation program,<ref>Associated Press, "[https://www.nytimes.com/1987/08/30/sports/eagle-reportedly-seeks-drug-help.html?pagewanted=1  Eagle Reportedly Seeks Drug Help]," ''The New York Times'' (August 30, 1987).  Retrieved May 21, 2010.</ref> and subsequently only played in three games for the Eagles in 1987.<ref name=pfrprofile/>  He was placed on the non-football injury list in December 1987,<ref>Associated Press, "[https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=ukBWAAAAIBAJ&sjid=EeoDAAAAIBAJ&pg=6895,1824739&dq=alonzo+johnson+eagles&hl=en  New setback for ex-Gator Alonzo Johnson]," ''The Gainesville Sun'', p. 9E (December 6, 1987).  Retrieved May 12, 2011.</ref> and did not play again.<ref name=pfrprofile/>

== Death ==
Johnson died in [[Bay County, Florida]], on February 1, 2024, at the age of 60.<ref>[https://www.wjhg.com/2024/02/03/rutherford-uf-football-legend-alonzo-johnson-has-passed-away/ Rutherford and UF football legend Alonzo Johnson has passed away] WJHG</ref>

'''Allen Lord Bradford''' (born August 31, 1988) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected by the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] in the sixth round of the [[2011 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2011/draft.htm |title=2011 NFL Draft Listing |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en |access-date=February 26, 2019}}</ref> He played [[college football]] for the [[USC Trojans football|USC Trojans]]. Bradford was also a member of the [[Seattle Seahawks]], [[New York Giants]], [[Jacksonville Jaguars]], [[Cleveland Browns]], and [[Atlanta Falcons]].

==Early life==
Bradford played running back and linebacker at Colton High School, where he played on the varsity squad for four years. As a senior in 2005, he ran for 1,869 yards on 143 carries with 29 touchdowns, and caught 20 passes for 429 yards with six touchdowns, plus recorded 157 tackles, 12.0 sacks, four forced fumbles and one fumble recovery.<ref name="Seattle Seahawks: Allen Bradford">{{Cite web |url=http://www.seahawks.com/team/roster/Allen-Bradford/33b65362-ec10-4f3b-bcbf-43415d938177 |title=Seattle Seahawks: Allen Bradford |access-date=December 30, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130101044254/http://www.seahawks.com/team/roster/allen-bradford/33b65362-ec10-4f3b-bcbf-43415d938177 |archive-date=January 1, 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==College career==
[[File:2010-0918-AllenBradford.JPG|thumb|left|Bradford with USC in 2010]]
Bradford played for former Seahawks head coach [[Pete Carroll]] at USC, where he finished his career with 1,585 yards rushing on 267 carries (5.9 average) and 16 touchdowns in 52 games played. Rushed for 7.2 yards per carry in 2010, good for second in the nation. Was USC’s No. 2 rusher in 2009, earning All-Pac-10 honorable mention.<ref name="Seattle Seahawks: Allen Bradford"/> Majored in American studies and ethnicity.<ref name="Seattle Seahawks: Allen Bradford"/>

==Professional career==
===Tampa Bay Buccaneers===
Bradford was selected by the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] in the sixth round, with the 187th overall pick, in the [[2011 NFL draft]]. He was waived on October 13, 2011.<ref name="transactions">{{Cite web |title=Allen Bradford Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BradAl00.htm |access-date=2024-07-03 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Seattle Seahawks (first stint)===
Bradford was claimed off waivers by the Seattle Seahawks on October 17, 2011.

He was waived two days later, and re-signed to the Seahawks' practice squad on October 21. He was switched to [[linebacker]] after re-signing with the Seahawks.

On December 28, 2012, Bradford was signed to the Seahawks 53-man roster.<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://blog.seahawks.com/2012/12/28/allen-bradford-signed-to-53-man-roster/|title = Allen Bradford signed to 53-man roster|date = December 28, 2012|access-date = December 30, 2012|archive-date = January 1, 2013|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20130101044155/http://blog.seahawks.com/2012/12/28/allen-bradford-signed-to-53-man-roster/|url-status = dead}}</ref> Bradford may be one of the first players in modern NFL history to be drafted as a running back and go on to play linebacker. He rushed for 13 yards on five carries and scored no touchdowns as a running back.

He was released on September 11, 2013, to make space for tight end [[Kellen Davis]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://blog.seattlepi.com/football/2013/09/11/report-seahawks-sign-te-kellen-davis-after-tuesday-workouts/|title = Home}}</ref>

===New York Giants===
Bradford was claimed off waivers by the [[New York Giants]] on September 12, 2013. He was released on May 12, 2014.

===Jacksonville Jaguars===
Bradford was claimed off waivers by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] on May 13, 2014. The Jaguars released Bradford on August 24, 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.jaguars.com/news/article-JaguarsNews/CB-Mike-Harris-among-11-players-released/84f13d9c-d7ac-4905-88ed-faa71930f994 |title=CB Mike Harris among 11 players released |access-date=August 24, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140826114703/http://www.jaguars.com/news/article-JaguarsNews/CB-Mike-Harris-among-11-players-released/84f13d9c-d7ac-4905-88ed-faa71930f994 |archive-date=August 26, 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Seattle Seahawks (second stint)===
Bradford was signed to the practice squad of the Seahawks on September 3, 2014, and released on September 9, 2014.<ref name="transactions" />

===Cleveland Browns===
Bradford signed with the Browns' practice squad on September 16, 2014.

===Seattle Seahawks (third stint)===
On November 12, 2014, Bradford was resigned again by the Seahawks. Bradford, in a locker-room interview on re-joining of the Seattle football team, stated how his return to Seattle "feels like home. I’m close to all the guys. They welcomed me with open arms. And I love being here. There’s not a place like this. So I’m just appreciative and I just want to work."<ref>http://www.seahawks.com/news/articles/article-1/Wednesday-in-Hawkville-Allen-Bradford-rejoins-Seahawks-and-he{{dead link|date=July 2016 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}’s-delighted-about-it/cf15d705-69c4-4125-9ed8-909685fa79c9/</ref>

===Atlanta Falcons===
Bradford signed with the [[Atlanta Falcons]] on February 13, 2015. He was released on October 27, 2015.<ref name="transactions" />

==Personal life==
Bradford is from [[Colton, California]].<ref>[http://www.usctrojans.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/bradford_allen00.html Player Bio] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110526031758/http://www.usctrojans.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/bradford_allen00.html |date=May 26, 2011 }} USCTrojans.com</ref> At Colton High School, Bradford was a linebacker and running back. Bradford has two children, Mahlia Liana Bradford and Aiden Lord Bradford. On July 2, 2016, he married Vanessa Portillo.

'''Allen Reisner''' (born September 29, 1988) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[tight end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Iowa Hawkeyes football|Iowa Hawkeyes]].

==Professional career==

===Minnesota Vikings===
Reisner was signed by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] following the end of the NFL lockout on July 26, 2011. Reisner was released from the Vikings on October 4, 2011. Reisner was signed back to the Vikings October 5, 2011 and placed on practice squad. He was signed to the Minnesota Vikings on November 26, 2011.

===Jacksonville Jaguars===
Reisner was claimed off waivers by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] on December 24, 2012.

On October 8, 2013, Reisner was placed on the injured reserve-designated for return list.<ref>{{cite web | last=Stites | first=Adam | title=Jaguars claim Young, place Reisner on IR | website=Big Cat Country|publisher=SB Nation | date=2013-10-08 | url=https://www.bigcatcountry.com/2013/10/8/4817700/jaguars-claim-ot-sam-young-place-allen-reisner-on-ir | access-date=2025-06-01}}</ref> He returned to the active roster on December 14.

===Second stint with Minnesota===
Reisner re-signed with the Minnesota Vikings on April 15, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|last=Alper|first=Josh|title=Vikings lose Josh Samuda to ankle injury, sign Allen Reisner|date=April 15, 2014 |url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/04/15/vikings-lose-josh-samuda-to-ankle-injury-sign-allen-reisner/|publisher=Pro Football Talk|accessdate=April 15, 2014}}</ref> However, despite finishing with the most touchdowns and most receptions for the Vikings in the 2014 preseason, he was cut by the team on August 30, 2014, as the roster was reduced to 53 for the season ahead.

===Baltimore Ravens===
Reisner was signed by the [[Baltimore Ravens]] on November 17, 2014. He was later waived on December 3, 2014, but re-signed on December 9, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Butt|first1=Jason|title=Antoine Cason's signing among Ravens roster moves|date=December 9, 2014 |url=http://www.baltimorebeatdown.com/2014/12/9/7362419/antoine-casons-signing-among-ravens-roster-moves|publisher=Baltimore Beatdown|accessdate=December 9, 2014}}</ref>

==Personal life==
On July 6, 2013, Reisner married longtime girlfriend and high school sweetheart, Lauren Perry, daughter of Syncbak founder Jack Perry.

'''Alvin Dewayne Bailey''' (born August 26, 1991) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[guard (gridiron football)|guard]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] at [[University of Arkansas|Arkansas]]. He was signed by the [[Seattle Seahawks]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2013.

==Early life==
A native of [[Broken Arrow, Oklahoma]], Bailey attended [[Broken Arrow Senior High School]], where he anchored the offensive line for three straight season and was regarded a three-star recruit by ''[[Rivals.com]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/football/recruiting/player-Alvin-Bailey-73515 |title=Alvin Bailey - Yahoo! Sports |access-date=November 15, 2015 |archive-date=November 18, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151118023729/https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/football/recruiting/player-Alvin-Bailey-73515 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He accepted a scholarship offer from [[University of Arkansas|Arkansas]] over offers from [[University of Nebraska–Lincoln|Nebraska]] and [[Kansas State University|Kansas State]].

==College career==
After redshirting in 2009, he started all 13 games for the Razorbacks as Arkansas was the only school in the SEC to start the same offensive line every game in 2010. In his redshirt sophomore season at Arkansas, Bailey was a Second-team All-SEC selection.<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.secdigitalnetwork.com/NEWS/tabid/473/Article/229915/2011-all-sec-football-team-announced.aspx | title=Southeastern Conference }}</ref> As a redshirt junior, he started in all 12 games.

In December 2012, Bailey announced his decision to forgo his final year of eligibility, entering the [[2013 NFL draft]]. He signed with Morgan Advisory Group, and began his preparations for the [[NFL Combine]] workouts in Arizona.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bailey Entering NFL Draft; Hogs Sign Five JUCO Players |url=https://www.arkansasnews.com/article/20121220/SPORTS/312209839 |website=Arkansas News Bureau}}</ref>

==Professional career==

Although being projected as a third-/fourth-round pick,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/nfl/draft-2013/tracker/#players/99915 |title=2013 NFL Draft - SI.com |access-date=November 20, 2013 |archive-date=October 21, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131021093409/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/nfl/draft-2013/tracker/#players/99915 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Bailey was not selected in the [[2013 NFL draft]].

'''Allen Bernard Robinson II''' (born August 24, 1993) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Penn State Nittany Lions football|Penn State Nittany Lions]], earning first-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors in 2013. Robinson was selected by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] of the National Football League (NFL) in the second round of the [[2014 NFL draft]]. He played for the Jaguars for four seasons, before signing with the [[Chicago Bears]] in 2018. Robinson has also played for the [[Los Angeles Rams]], [[Pittsburgh Steelers]], and [[Detroit Lions]].

==Early life==
Robinson was born in [[Detroit]], [[Michigan]].<ref name="about allen">{{Cite web |date=February 19, 2018 |title=About Allen |url=https://theallenrobinson.com/about-allen/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210108032632/https://theallenrobinson.com/about-allen/ |archive-date=January 8, 2021 |access-date=June 2, 2019 |website=theallenrobinson.com |language=en-US}}</ref> He attended [[St. Mary's Preparatory]], where he played on the [[high school football|football]] team. In his senior season, he led the Eaglets to the Division 3 State Championship, where they lost 35–27 to [[East Grand Rapids High School]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Maghielse |first=Ross |date=November 28, 2010 |title=For Orchard Lake St. Mary's, losing to EGR is getting OLD |url=https://www.theoaklandpress.com/news/prep-football-state-finals-for-orchard-lake-st-marys-losing-to-egr-is-getting-old/article_87cf0514-9a34-5418-b13e-0fcd620655c2.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210108032638/https://www.theoaklandpress.com/news/prep-football-state-finals-for-orchard-lake-st-marys-losing-to-egr-is-getting-old/article_87cf0514-9a34-5418-b13e-0fcd620655c2.html |archive-date=January 8, 2021 |access-date=November 25, 2020 |website=The Oakland Press |language=en}}</ref> He was a teammate of former Penn State quarterback [[Rob Bolden]].<ref name="PSU site">{{Cite web |title=Allen Robinson Profile |url=http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/robinson_allen00.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120908003943/http://www.gopsusports.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/robinson_allen00.html |archive-date=September 8, 2012 |access-date=September 5, 2012 |website=Penn State Official Athletic Site |publisher=Pennsylvania State University}}</ref> In addition to football, Robinson was a competitor for the St. Mary's Preparatory [[track and field]] team. Robinson committed to Penn State on November 29, 2010, after being recruited by Penn State assistant coach [[Ron Vanderlinden]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Allen Robinson |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/football/recruiting/player-Allen-Robinson-112616 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150403204246/https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/football/recruiting/player-Allen-Robinson-112616 |archive-date=April 3, 2015 |access-date=September 5, 2012 |website=Yahoo! Sports}}</ref> He had also received offers from [[Minnesota Golden Gophers football|Minnesota]], [[Buffalo Bulls football|Buffalo]], and [[Toledo Rockets football|Toledo]].<ref name="about allen" />

==Professional career==

Coming out of Penn State, Robinson was projected by the majority of analysts and scouts to be a first-to-third round draft selection. '''Alvester Alexander''' (born October 17, 1990) is an American former [[American football|football]] player. He played [[college football]] for the [[Wyoming Cowboys football|Wyoming Cowboys]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Hockensmitch |first=Dustin |date=August 7, 2013 |title=Pittsburgh Steelers sign Alvester Alexander and Devin Smith, release Curtis McNeal and Cordian Hagans |work=PennLive.com |url=http://www.pennlive.com/sports/index.ssf/2013/08/pittsburgh_steelers_sign_alves.html |accessdate=April 16, 2014}}</ref>

==Professional career ==
On April 29, 2012, the [[Chicago Bears]] signed Alexander as an undrafted free agent. On July 17, 2012, he was cut from the Bears roster.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2012-07-17 |title=Bears Sign RB Lorenzo Booker, Release Alexander |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/chicago/news/bears-sign-rb-lorenzo-booker-release-alexander/ |access-date=2023-11-14 |website=CBS Chicago |language=en-US}}</ref>

On August 14, 2012, he signed with the [[Indianapolis Colts]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=Josh |date=2012-08-14 |title=Colts Sign RB Alvester Alexander; Place LB Scott Lutrus on IR |url=https://www.stampedeblue.com/2012/8/14/3243273/colts-sign-rb-alvester-alexander-place-lb-scott-lutrus-on-ir |access-date=2025-06-28 |website=Stampede Blue|publisher=SB Nation}}</ref> On December 11, 2012, he was cut.<ref>{{cite web | last=Wells | first=Brad | title=Colts Roster Moves: Donald Brown To IR, Team Re-Signs Mewelde Moore | website=Stampede Blue|publisher=SB Nation | date=2012-12-11 | url=https://www.stampedeblue.com/2012/12/11/3756182/colts-roster-moves-donald-brown-to-ir-team-re-signs-mewelde-moore | access-date=2026-02-23}}</ref>

On December 26, he signed with the [[Tennessee Titans]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Riley |first=Alex |date=2012-12-26 |title=Alexander signs with Titans practice squad |url=https://www.wyomingnews.com/wyosports/university_of_wyoming/football/alexander-signs-with-titans-practice-squad/article_bf789204-18d4-5382-968b-14e3429fc44e.html |access-date=2023-11-14 |website=Wyoming Tribune Eagle |language=en}}</ref>

On August 17, 2013, he signed with the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]]. He spent the entire 2013 season on their practice squad. At the end of the season the Steelers signed him to Reserve/Future Contract. He signed with the [[Ottawa Redblacks]] in 2015.

Alexander participated in [[The Spring League]] in 2017.<ref name="Levine">{{Cite web |last=Levine, Ben |date=April 9, 2017 |title=The Spring League Announces Camp Roster |url=https://www.profootballrumors.com/2017/04/the-spring-league-announces-training-camp-roster |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170726034951/https://www.profootballrumors.com/2017/04/the-spring-league-announces-training-camp-roster |archive-date=July 26, 2017 |publisher=profootballrumors.com |accessdate=July 25, 2017}}</ref>

'''Alva Edison Liles ''' (March 6, 1956 – January 7, 1998) was an American professional [[American football|football]] [[defensive lineman]] who played in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) with the [[Detroit Lions]] and [[Oakland Raiders]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Boise State University]].

== Early life and college ==
Alva Edison Liles was born on March 6, 1956, in [[Oklahoma City|Oklahoma City, Oklahoma]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name="pfr"/> He played football at [[Sacramento High School]] in [[Sacramento, California]], graduating in 1974.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Gibson |first=Steve |date=January 18, 1998 |title=Alva Liles |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-sacramento-bee-alva-liles/140658300/ |access-date=2024-02-10 |work=[[Sacramento Bee]] |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> He played [[college football]] at [[Boise State University]], as an offensive guard, and was a four-year [[letterman (sports)|letterman]] from 1974 to 1977.<ref name=":0" /><ref name="pfa"/>

== Professional career ==
Liles signed with the [[Washington Redskins]] after going undrafted in the [[1978 NFL draft]].<ref name="transactions"/> He was released on July 25, 1978.<ref name="transactions">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/transactions/l/lile00200.html | title=Alva Liles Transactions | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=30 April 2025}}</ref>

On August 23, 1978, Liles signed with the Sacramento Buffalos of the California Football League.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-sacramento-bee/171405503/ | title=Buffalos Sign Ex-Redskin Rookie Liles | work=[[The Sacramento Bee]] | date=August 24, 1978 | accessdate=30 April 2025 | author=Menton, Bill | pages=D4}}</ref><ref name="cfl"/> However, he quit the team a few days later after his agent advised him that the Redskins might be interesting in signing him again, and that he should not risk injury by playing for the Buffalos.<ref name="cfl">{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-sacramento-bee/171405599/ | title=Liles Quits | work=[[The Sacramento Bee]] | date=August 26, 1978 | accessdate=30 April 2025 | author=Van Vliet, Jim | pages=E3}}</ref>

Liles was signed by the [[Oakland Raiders]] on March 15, 1979.<ref name="transactions"/> He was later released on August 14, 1979.<ref name="transactions"/>

He signed with the [[New York Jets]] on February 20, 1980.<ref name="transactions"/> He was released on July 18, 1979, after quitting the team to take care of his sick mother.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/newsday-suffolk-edition/171405860/ | title=Jets Left With Nothing for Owens | work=[[Newsday]] | date=July 19, 1980 | accessdate=30 April 2025 | author=Usher, George}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/lansing-state-journal/171405922/ | title=Sports deals | work=[[Lansing State Journal]] | date=July 19, 1980 | agency=[[Associated Press]] | accessdate=30 April 2025 | pages=B3}}</ref>

Liles then signed with the Raiders in early August 1980.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/oakland-tribune/171406140/ | title=Raider line's message: Hurry back, Sylvester | work=[[Oakland Tribune]] | date=August 3, 1980 | accessdate=30 April 2025 | author=Borges, Ron | pages=C5}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on August 19, released on September 20, and signed again on October 3.<ref name="transactions"/> He then played in two games for the Raiders during the 1980 season before being released on October 15, 1980.<ref name="pfr"/><ref name="transactions"/>

Liles signed with the [[Detroit Lions]] on November 4, 1980.<ref name="transactions"/> He appeared in one game for Detroit before being released on November 19, 1980.<ref name="pfr">{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/L/LileAl20.htm | title=Alva Liles | publisher=[[Pro Football Reference]] | accessdate=30 April 2025}}</ref><ref name="transactions"/> He re-signed with the Lions in 1981 but was later released on July 16, 1981.<ref name="transactions"/>

Liles was signed by the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] on July 28, 1981, but quickly released on August 4, 1981.<ref name="transactions"/>

Liles signed with the [[Oakland Invaders]] of the [[United States Football League]] (USFL) on December 30, 1982.<ref name="transactions"/> He played in 14 games for the Invaders during the 1983 season and recorded five sacks.<ref name="pfa"/>

On September 6, 1983, Liles was selected by the [[Oklahoma Outlaws]] of the USFL in an expansion draft.<ref name="transactions"/> On February 27, 1984, it was reported that Liles had been traded to the [[Arizona Wranglers]] for past considerations.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/fort-mcmurray-today/171406804/ | title=Business | work=[[Fort McMurray Today]] | date=February 27, 1984 | accessdate=30 April 2025 | pages=7}}</ref> However, he never played for the Wranglers.<ref name="pfa"/>

==Personal life==
Liles died on January 7, 1998, in Sacramento at the age of 41.<ref name="pfr"/> He had been suffering from [[non-Hodgkin lymphoma]].<ref name=":0" />

'''Allen Clark Lyday''' (born September 16, 1960) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive back]] for the [[Houston Oilers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He first played [[college football]] for the [[Texas Southern Tigers football|Texas Southern Tigers]] before transferring to the [[Nebraska Cornhuskers football|Nebraska Cornhuskers]].

==Early life==
Allen Clark Lyday was born on September 16, 1960, in [[Wichita, Kansas]].<ref name="pfa"/> He attended [[Wichita South High School]], where he participated in wrestling and football.<ref name="Oklahoman">{{cite news | url=https://www.oklahoman.com/story/news/1982/11/06/huskers-depth-big-problem-for-pokes/62867864007/ | title=Huskers' Depth Big Problem for Pokes | work=[[The Oklahoman]] | date=November 6, 1982 | accessdate=23 December 2024 | author=Kensler, Tom}}</ref><ref name="pfa">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/players/l/lyda00200.html | title=Allen Lyday | publisher=profootballarchives.com | accessdate=23 December 2024}}</ref>

==College career==
Lyday first enrolled at [[Texas Southern University]] as a [[Punter (gridiron football)|punter]].<ref name="Oklahoman"/><ref name="pfa"/> He then transferred to the [[University of Nebraska–Lincoln]] to try out for the wrestling team but did not end up wrestling there.<ref name="Oklahoman"/> He was member of the [[Nebraska Cornhuskers football]] team from 1980 to 1982 and a two-year [[letterman (sports)|letterman]] from 1981 to 1982.<ref name="pfa"/>

==Professional career==
After going undrafted in the [[1983 NFL draft]], Lyday signed with the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] on April 28.<ref name="Transactions"/> He was released on August 29, 1983.<ref name="Transactions"/>

Lyday was signed by the [[Houston Oilers]] on April 6, 1984.<ref name="Transactions"/> He was released on August 20 but later resigned on October 25.<ref name="Transactions"/> He then played in four games for the Oilers during the 1984 season, recording one interception, before being placed on injured reserve on November 21, 1984.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/L/LydaAl20/gamelog/1984/ | title=Allen Lyday 1984 Game Log | publisher=pro-football-reference.com | accessdate=23 December 2024}}</ref><ref name="Transactions"/> He was released the next year on September 3, 1985, and later re-signed on September 26, 1985.<ref name="Transactions"/> Lyday appeared in 13 games during the 1985 season, totaling one kick return for six yards, one fumble, and one fumble recovery.<ref name="pfr">{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/L/LydaAl20.htm | title=Allen Lyday | publisher=pro-football-reference.com | accessdate=23 December 2024}}</ref> He played in the first four games of the 1986 season before being placed on injured reserve on October 1.<ref name="1986g">{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/L/LydaAl20/gamelog/1986/ | title=Allen Lyday 1986 Game Log | publisher=pro-football-reference.com | accessdate=23 December 2024}}</ref><ref name="Transactions"/> He was later activated on October 31 and played in the final eight games of the season, recording three interceptions.<ref name="1986g"/><ref name="Transactions"/> Lyday appeared in seven games for the Oilers in 1987 before being placed on injured reserve again on November 23, 1987.<ref name="pfr"/><ref name="Transactions"/> He became a free agent after the 1987 season.<ref name="Transactions">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/transactions/l/lyda00200.html | title=Allen Lyday NFL Transactions | publisher=profootballarchives.com | accessdate=23 December 2024}}</ref>

'''Wayne Allen Carter''' (born December 12, 1952) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] for the [[New England Patriots]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL) in 1975 and 1976. He played [[college football]] for the [[USC Trojans football|USC Trojans]].

==High school==
Carter had outstanding high school football career at [[Bonita High School]], where he was considered by some observers to be one of the top high school running backs of the time.<ref name=payback/> He ran for 4,388 yards with 70 [[touchdown]]s during his three years on the Bonita varsity team, breaking records set by [[Glenn Davis (halfback)|Glenn Davis]] in the process.<ref name=payback/> As a senior, Carter was named the CIF-Southern Section's 3-A Division Player of the Year. Carter also participated in [[track and field]] in high school, and was the California state champion in the [[100-meter dash]] in his junior year, running the race in 9.7 seconds.<ref name=payback/>

==College==
After high school, Carter signed to play college ball at the [[University of Southern California]].<ref name=payback>{{cite web|title=Payback With Interest : Former Trojan Carter Finds His Niche Teaching at Anaheim High|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1992-10-22-sp-797-story.html|author=Foster, C.|access-date=2015-09-09|date=October 22, 1992|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]}}</ref>  In his freshman year, Allen led the USC freshman team in rushing.<ref name=payback/>  But as a sophomore in [[1972 USC Trojans football team|1972]], he suffered leg injuries and fell behind [[Anthony Davis (running back, born 1952)|Anthony Davis]] and [[Rod McNeill]] on the varsity team at [[Halfback (American football)|tailback]].<ref name=payback/>  Davis became the team's star tailback for the next three years, with Carter playing behind him.<ref name=payback/>  Carter rushed 30 times for 226 yards, a 7.5 average, that season, as USC won the National Championship.<ref name=college>{{cite web|title=Allen Carter|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/southern-california/1972.html|publisher=Sports Reference|accessdate=2015-09-09}}</ref>  As a junior in [[1973 USC Trojans football team|1973]], again playing behind Davis and McNeill, Carter rushed 43 times for 294 yards, a 6.8 yard average.<ref name=college/>  As a senior in [[1974 USC Trojans football team|1974]], Allen played behind only Davis, and rushed for 580 yards on 111 carries, a 5.2 average, helping USC to another National Championship.<ref name=college/>  Allen played a key role in USC's victory in the 1975 [[Rose Bowl Game]], rushing for 75 yards after Davis suffered a rib injury in the first half of the game.<ref name=payback/><ref>{{cite book|title=The USC Trojans Football Encyclopedia|author=Shmelter, R.J.|page=99|year=2014|publisher=McFarland|isbn=9781476615110}}</ref>

==Professional career==
Carter was selected by the Patriots in the 4th round with the 86th pick of the [[1975 NFL draft]].<ref name=carter>{{cite web|title=Allen Carter|url=
https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CartAl00.htm|publisher=Pro Football Reference|accessdate=2015-09-09}}</ref>  The Patriots had received the pick from the [[Cleveland Browns]] in exchange for [[wide receiver]] [[Reggie Rucker]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Rucker Bitter Over Patriots' Trade Decision|newspaper=[[Bangor Daily News]]|date=January 30, 1975|page=12|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=2457&dat=19750130&id=CA9bAAAAIBAJ&pg=668,4380070&hl=en|accessdate=2015-09-09}}</ref>  With the Patriots he was reunited with fellow [[running back]] [[Sam Cunningham]], who had been his [[fullback (gridiron football)|fullback]] on the 1972 USC team.

Carter was primarily a [[kick returner]] for the [[1975 New England Patriots season|1975 Patriots]].  He rushed only 22 times for 95 yards, a 4.3 yard average.<ref name=carter/>  He also caught 2 passes for 39 yards.<ref name=carter/>  He had a successful season as a [[kickoff (gridiron football)|kickoff]] return man, returning 32 kicks for 879 yards and a 27.5 yards per return average.<ref name=carter/>  His 32 returns ranked 7th in the NFL, his 879 yards ranked 6th and his 27.5 yard average ranked 3rd.<ref name=carter/>  In the final game of the season against the [[Baltimore Colts]], Carter returned the opening kickoff 99 yards for a [[touchdown]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Colts Tip Pats, Gain Playoffs|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1368&dat=19751222&id=nIVQAAAAIBAJ&pg=5630,4158921&hl=en|newspaper=[[The Milwaukee Sentinel]]|date=December 22, 1975|page=2-1|accessdate=2015-09-09}}{{Dead link|date=March 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>  His 99-yard return was the 2nd longest in the NFL that season.<ref name=carter/>  It also set a Patriots record for longest kickoff return, which was broken by [[Raymond Clayborn]]'s 100-yard return in 1977.<ref>{{cite news|title=Jets Jolt 'Bad' Pats|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1982&dat=19771003&id=l8VGAAAAIBAJ&pg=1496,441546&hl=en|newspaper=[[The Evening News (Newburgh)|The Evening News]]|date=October 2, 1977|page=4B|accessdate=2015-09-09}}</ref>  The touchdown was also enough to tie the league lead for kickoff return touchdowns for the season.<ref name=carter/>

In the first game of the 1976 season, Carter saw little action due to a knee injury.<ref>{{cite news|title=Patriots Get Jess Phillips|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=2209&dat=19760914&id=GqQrAAAAIBAJ&pg=3950,2239335&hl=en|newspaper=[[The Telegraph (Nashua)|The Telegraph]]|date=September 14, 1976|accessdate=2015-09-09|page=18}}</ref>  He returned just one kickoff for 19 yards and did not have any rushes or receptions.<ref name=carter/>  He was [[Waivers (American football)|waived]] by the Patriots the following week and was signed by the [[New York Jets]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Waived to Pats|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=799&dat=19760922&id=kEcLAAAAIBAJ&pg=2124,765093&hl=en|newspaper=[[The Bryan Times]]|accessdate=2015-09-09|date=September 22, 1976|page=13}}</ref>  He was waived by the Jets shortly thereafter.<ref>{{cite news|title=Pro Transactions|newspaper=[[Eugene Register-Guard]]|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1310&dat=19760923&id=hWdYAAAAIBAJ&pg=3919,5699765&hl=en|date=September 23, 1976|page=6C|accessdate=2015-09-09}}</ref>

==Post-retirement==
After his football career ended, Carter became a teacher, activities director, and assistant football coach at [[Anaheim High School]].<ref name=payback/>  He later became Anaheim's varsity football head coach, during which time Carter coached future [[NFL]] running back [[Reuben Droughns]].<ref>{{cite news|title=JUST GIMME THE BALL|url=https://vault.si.com/vault/2004/11/29/just-gimme-the-ball|newspaper=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=November 29, 2004|accessdate=May 6, 2020}}</ref>

'''Alois Sterling Blackwell''' (born November 12, 1954) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Dallas Cowboys]] and [[Kansas City Chiefs]]. He played [[college football]] at the [[University of Houston]].

==Early life==
Blackwell attended [[Cuero High School]]. As a sophomore, he contributed to the team making its first state final appearance.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.victoriaadvocate.com/advosports/cuero-graduate-named-to-class-of-gridiron-legends/article_39c166e2-ab26-11e8-b4cf-5329a3314034.html |title=Cuero graduate named to Class of Gridiron Legends |publisher=Victoria Advocate |date=August 29, 2018 |accessdate=August 30, 2020}}</ref> He accepted a football scholarship from the [[University of Houston]]. As a sophomore in [[1975 Houston Cougars football team|1975]], he posted 64 carries (fourth on the team), 364 rushing yards (third on the team), a 5.7-yard average and 2 touchdowns.	

As a junior in [[1976 Houston Cougars football team|1976]], he became the starter at [[running back]], registering 151 carries for 934 yards (6.2-yard avg.) and 8 [[touchdown]]s. He posted four 100-yard rushing games and contributed to the team's [[Southwest Conference]] co-championship. In the [[1977 Cotton Bowl Classic|1977 Cotton Bowl]], he rushed for 149 yards, 2 [[touchdown]]s, earned offensive MVP honors and contributed to a number 4 national ranking, which was the highest in school history.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1876&dat=19770102&id=4D8sAAAAIBAJ&sjid=9cwEAAAAIBAJ&pg=2199,152079 |title=Houston Holds Off Maryland Late In Cotton Bowl, 30-21 |publisher=Herald-Journal |date=January 2, 1977 |accessdate=August 30, 2020}}</ref>

As a senior in 1977, he tallied 213 carries for 1,169 yards (5.5-yard avg.), 7 receptions for 108 yards and 11 touchdowns. His 1,169 rushing yards were second in the SWC behind [[Earl Campbell]] and fifth best in school history. He also scored 11 [[touchdown]]s, while having six 100-yard rushing games.<ref>{{cite web |author= |url=http://www.uhcougars.com/genrel/092910aad.html |title=Athletics Department to Induct Nine into Hall of Honor |publisher=University of Houston Athletics |date=29 September 2010 |accessdate=August 30, 2020 }}{{Dead link|date=October 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>

He finished his college career with 2,467 rushing yards (fourth in school history), a 5.8-yard average and 21 [[touchdown]]s (third in school history). In 2010, he was inducted into the [[University of Houston]] Hall of Honor.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uhcougars.com/trads/hou-trads-hall-honor.html|title=Hall of Honor Inductees|publisher=University of Houston Athletics|accessdate=August 30, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161113111009/http://www.uhcougars.com/trads/hou-trads-hall-honor.html|archive-date=2016-11-13|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Dallas Cowboys===
Blackwell was selected by the [[Dallas Cowboys]] in the fourth round (110th overall) of the [[1978 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=861&dat=19780830&id=exdIAAAAIBAJ&sjid=9YAMAAAAIBAJ&pg=4245,525418 |title=Blackwell Spells Relief D-a-l-l-a-s C-o-w-b-o-y-s |publisher=The Victoria Advocate |date=August 30, 1978 |accessdate=August 30, 2020}}</ref> As a rookie, he was the third-string running back behind [[Tony Dorsett]] and [[Preston Pearson]]. He mostly covered kickoffs and was considered one of the hardest hitters on [[special teams]]. He played in [[Super Bowl XII]].

In [[1979 NFL season|1979]], he was the third-string running back. On October 22, he was waived to make room for [[defensive end]] [[John Dutton (defensive lineman)|John Dutton]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1755&dat=19791023&id=EpwcAAAAIBAJ&sjid=i2cEAAAAIBAJ&pg=6091,3519609 |title=Cowboys Activate John Dutton |publisher=Sarasota Herald-Tribune  |date=March 23, 1979 |accessdate=August 30, 2020}}</ref>

===Kansas City Chiefs===
In April [[1980 NFL season|1980]], he signed with the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] as a [[free agent]]. He was placed on the [[injured reserve list]] on August 19.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=2199&dat=19800820&id=epYyAAAAIBAJ&sjid=VucFAAAAIBAJ&pg=5724,4820620 |title=KC draft pick among 14 cuts |publisher=Lawrence Journal-World |date=August 20, 1980 |accessdate=August 30, 2020}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Blackwell worked in the Houston Department of Intercollegiate Athletics.  On January 12, 2001, he was hired as the [[Texas Southern University]] athletic director.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chron.com/sports/college/article/TSU-hires-UH-s-Blackwell-as-AD-1993083.php |title=TSU hires UH's Blackwell as AD |publisher=Houston Chronicle |date=January 13, 2001 |accessdate=August 30, 2020}}</ref> On February 11, 2008, he was relieved of his duties.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chron.com/sports/college/article/Blackwell-officially-out-as-TSU-athletic-director-1670577.php |title=Blackwell officially out as TSU athletic director |publisher=Houston Chronicle |date=February 12, 2008 |accessdate=August 30, 2020}}</ref>
Blackwell is also a member of [[Phi Beta Sigma]] fraternity. He helped charter the Zeta Zeta chapter at the [[University of Houston]] on April 6, 1974.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.zetazetasigmas.org|accessdate=April 7, 2021}}</ref>

'''Alonzo Jermey Russell''' (born September 29, 1992) is an American former professional [[Gridiron football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Toledo Rockets football|Toledo Rockets]] and signed with the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] as an undrafted free agent in 2016.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Marcum |first1=Jason |title=Alonzo Russell joining Bengals as UDFA |url=https://www.cincyjungle.com/nfldraft/2016/4/30/11546696/alonzo-russell-joining-bengals-as-udfa |website=Cincy Jungle |publisher=SB Nation |accessdate=15 October 2019 |language=en |date=30 April 2016}}</ref> He was also a member of the [[Cincinnati Bengals]], [[Arizona Cardinals]] and [[New York Giants]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL), and [[Winnipeg Blue Bombers]] and [[Ottawa Redblacks]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL).

==College career==
After redshirting the 2011 season at the [[University of Toledo]], Russell's collegiate debut came against the [[2012 Arizona Wildcats football team|Arizona Wildcats]] where he hauled in three receptions for 71 yards and one touchdown. In week 3, Russell caught six passes for a career high 152 yards and one touchdown in a 27-15 victory against the [[2012 Bowling Green Falcons football team|Bowling Green Falcons]]. He ranked second on the team with 56 catches, 960 yards and five touchdowns, earning him third-team All-MAC. In 2013, Russell earned third team All-MAC for the second straight season. Russell caught a game winning touchdown pass from 11 yards out against [[2013 Bowling Green Falcons football team|Bowling Green]] in the final two minutes of play. In 2014, Russell caught a career best eight touchdowns and also had at least two receptions in all 13 games played. He earned third team All-MAC for the third straight season. In 2015, Russell would have 36 receptions for 618 yards and five touchdowns, earning him second team All-MAC. Russell ranks fifth in Rocket's history with 202 catches, fourth in receiving yards with 3,076 and tied for forth with 24 touchdown receptions. Russell holds Toledo's record with 50 straight games with a reception.<ref>{{cite web|title=2023 Toledo Rockets Media Guide|url=https://utrockets.com/documents/2023/8/15/2023_Toledo_Football_Media_Guide.pdf|website=utrockets.com|date=August 15, 2023}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Cincinnati Bengals===
Russell signed with the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] after going undrafted in the [[2016 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hustlebelt.com/nfl/2016/5/1/11550766/cincinnati-bengals-alonzo-russell-free-agent|date=May 1, 2016|title=Cincinnati Bengals sign Alonzo Russell to free agent contract|author=Kaleb Carter|accessdate=May 7, 2016}}</ref> On September 3, 2016, he was waived by the Bengals and was signed to the practice squad the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bengals cut down to 53-man roster, Hardison to IR|url=http://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/nfl/bengals/2016/09/03/cincinnati-bengals-announce-final-cut-53/89824586/}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Bengals waive P.J. Dawson, sign Trey Hopkins, Chykie Brown|url=http://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/nfl/bengals/2016/09/04/bengals-waive-pj-dawson-sign-9-practice-squad/89866058/|last=Dehner Jr.|first=Paul}}</ref> After spending the entire season on the practice squad, Russell signed a futures contract with the Bengals on January 2, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bengals sign 5 players to futures contracts for 2017|url=http://www.cincyjungle.com/2017/1/2/14147058/bengals-sign-5-players-futures-contacts-entire-practice-squad-signed|author=Marcum, Jason|website=CincyJungle.com|date=January 2, 2017}}</ref>

On September 2, 2017, Russell was waived by the Bengals.<ref>{{cite web|title=NFL roster cuts 2017: Cincinnati Bengals 53-man roster|url=https://www.cincyjungle.com/2017/9/2/16245134/nfl-roster-cuts-2017-cincinnati-bengals-53-man-roster|author=Toback, Rebecca|website=CincyJungle.com|date=September 2, 2017}}</ref>

===Arizona Cardinals===
On November 22, 2017, Russell was signed to the [[Arizona Cardinals]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cardinals Sign WR Alonzo Russell To PS|url=http://nfltraderumors.co/cardinals-sign-wr-alonzo-russell-ps/|website=NFLTradeRumors.co|date=November 22, 2017}}</ref>

===New York Giants===
On May 14, 2018, Russell signed with the [[New York Giants]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Giants roster moves: Six players signed, six waived|url=http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Giants-roster-moves-Six-players-signed-six-waived/d5051b3e-18bc-40c8-afab-9a110ce1b20f|author=Eisen, Michael|website=Giants.com|date=May 14, 2018|access-date=May 15, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180516014612/http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Giants-roster-moves-Six-players-signed-six-waived/d5051b3e-18bc-40c8-afab-9a110ce1b20f|archive-date=May 16, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was waived on September 1, 2018, and was signed to the practice squad the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=New York Giants announce 53-man roster|url=https://www.giants.com/news/new-york-giants-announce-53-man-roster|author=Eisen, Michael|website=Giants.com|date=September 1, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Giants waive QB Davis Webb, announce practice squad among roster moves|url=https://www.giants.com/news/giants-waive-qb-davis-webb-announce-practice-squad-among-roster-moves|author=Eisen, Michael|website=Giants.com|date=September 2, 2018}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on December 29, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Giants place Jawill Davis on IR, promote Alonzo Russell to 53-man roster|url=https://giantswire.usatoday.com/2018/12/29/new-york-giants-place-jawill-davis-ir-promote-alonzo-russell/|work=Giants Wire|publisher=USA Today|date=December 29, 2018}}</ref> The following day, Russell would appear in his first NFL game against the [[Dallas Cowboys]] where he would appear in eight offensive snaps and seven on special teams.<ref>{{cite web|title=Alonzo Russell 2018 game log|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RussAl01/gamelog/2018/ |date=December 30, 2018}}</ref>

On September 1, 2019, Russell was waived by the Giants.<ref>{{cite web|title=Giants claim WR Cody Core, OT Eric Smith off waivers|url=https://www.giants.com/news/giants-claim-wr-cody-core-ot-eric-smith-off-waivers|author=Eisen, Michael|website=Giants.com|date=September 1, 2019}}</ref>

===St. Louis BattleHawks===
Russell was selected in the 9th round (70th overall) of the first phase by the [[St. Louis BattleHawks]] in the [[2020 XFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Mark |first1=The |title=XFL Skill Players Draft Tracker, Phase #1 (QB, RB, WR, TE) |url=https://xflnewshub.com/xfl-players/xfl-skill-players-draft-tracker/ |website=xflnewshub.com |date=October 15, 2019 |publisher=XFL News Hub |accessdate=15 October 2019}}</ref> He had his contract terminated when the league suspended operations on April 10, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |author=Condotta, Bob |title=XFL suspends operations, terminates all employees, but Jim Zorn says he has hopes league will continue |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/xfl-suspends-operations-terminates-all-employees/ |website=SeattleTimes.com |date=April 10, 2020 |accessdate=July 17, 2020}}</ref>

===Winnipeg Blue Bombers===
Russell signed with the [[Winnipeg Blue Bombers]] of the CFL on July 3, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=Blue Bombers add two to roster |url=https://www.bluebombers.com/2020/07/03/blue-bombers-add-two-roster-2/ |website=BlueBombers.com |date=July 3, 2020 |accessdate=July 4, 2020}}</ref> The [[2020 CFL season]] was cancelled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada|COVID-19 pandemic]]. He was released on July 19, 2021.<ref>{{cite news |title=Blue Bombers cut-down roster |url=https://www.bluebombers.com/2021/07/19/blue-bombers-cut-roster/ |website=BlueBombers.com |date=July 19, 2021 |access-date=July 20, 2021}}</ref>

===Ottawa Redblacks===
Russell signed with the CFL's [[Ottawa Redblacks]] on August 31, 2021.<ref name="db">{{cite web | url=https://www.footballdb.com/players/alonzo-russell-russeal01/transactions | title=Alonzo Russell | publisher=FootballDB.com | accessdate=1 May 2026}}</ref> He was moved to the practice roster on September 7, released on September 18, signed back to the practice roster on September 25, and released for the final time on November 2, 2021.<ref name="db"/>
