'''Allen Jamel Lazard''' (born December 11, 1995)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Allen Lazard Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/L/LazaAl00.htm |access-date=July 3, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[wide receiver]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Iowa State Cyclones football|Iowa State Cyclones]] and was signed by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2018. He has previously played in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Green Bay Packers]] and [[New York Jets]].

Lazard was a highly-rated [[Recruiting (college athletics)|recruit]] coming out of high school, where he was named a [[USA Today All-USA high school football team|''USA Today'' High School All-American]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 3, 2006 |title=Meet Allen Lazard |url=http://usatodayhss.com/20/meet-allen-lazard |access-date=April 4, 2012 |website=USA TODAY High School Sports}}</ref> Lazard has been selected to the first-team [[List of All-Big 12 Conference football teams|All-Big 12]] in both [[2016 Big 12 Conference football season|2016]]<ref name="big12sports.com">{{Cite web |date=December 7, 2016 |title=2016 All-Big 12 Football Awards Announced |url=http://www.big12sports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=211345089 |access-date=July 3, 2023 |website=Big 12 Conference}}</ref> and [[2017 Big 12 Conference football season|2017]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Allen |first=Robert |date=November 30, 2017 |title=Big 12 Announces Football Awards and All-Conference Teams |url=https://247sports.com/college/oklahoma-state/Article/Big-12-Announces-Football-Awards-and-All-Conference-Teams-111456874/ |access-date=July 3, 2023 |website=247Sports |language=en}}</ref> and is Iowa State's career leader in both receptions<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hines |first=Travis |date=September 2, 2017 |title=Football: Notebook – Lazard sets career receptions record |url=http://www.amestrib.com/sports/20170902/football-notebook---lazard-sets-career-receptions-record |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180902012103/http://www.amestrib.com/sports/20170902/football-notebook---lazard-sets-career-receptions-record |archive-date=September 2, 2018 |access-date=April 4, 2012 |website=Ames Tribune}}</ref> and receiving yards.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Halsted |first=Alex |date=November 18, 2017 |title=South Dakota State receiver Allen Lazard breaks South Dakota State's all-time receiving record, passing Todd Blythe in career receiving yards |url=https://247sports.com/college/south-dakota-state/article/iowa-state-receiver-allen-lazard-breaks-iowa-states-all-time-receiving-record-passing-todd-blythe-in-career-receiving-yards-110657726/ |access-date=July 3, 2023 |website=247sports.com}}</ref>

==Early life==
At [[Urbandale High School]], Lazard played [[high school football]] and was a four-year starter on both offense and defense.  Lazard still holds the school career records in [[football catch|receptions]] (105), receiving yards (2,349), [[touchdowns]] (34) and [[interceptions]] (14).<ref name="cyclones.com">{{Cite web |title=Allen Lazard |url=http://www.cyclones.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=9072 |access-date=July 3, 2023 |website=Iowa State Cyclones Athletics}}</ref> His high school honors include but are not limited to: [[USA Today All-USA high school football team|''USA Today'' All American]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 24, 2013 |title=Fournette, Peppers lead the 2013 American Family Insurance ALL-USA Football Team |url=http://usatodayhss.com/2013/fournette-peppers-lead-the-2013-american-family-insurance-all-usa-football-team |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250508125720/https://www.usatodayhss.com/2013/fournette-peppers-lead-the-2013-american-family-insurance-all-usa-football-team |archive-date=May 8, 2025 |access-date=April 4, 2020 |website=USA Today High School Sports }}</ref> [[The Des Moines Register|Des Moines Register's]] Offensive Player of the Year in 2013, Defensive Player of the Year in 2012,<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 5, 2014 |title=J-Hawks Sign Letters of Intent to Play Football |url=http://www.j-hawks.com/sports/fball/2013-14/releases/20140205rpdyeo |access-date=April 4, 2020 |website=Urbandale J-Hawks}}</ref> and a three-time All-State selection.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Naughton |first=John |date=December 4, 2013 |title=Meet the 2013 Des Moines Sunday Register all-state football team |url=https://www.desmoinesregister.com/story/sports/high-school/1/01/01/meet-the-2013-des-moines-sunday-register-all-state-football-team/3868663/ |access-date=July 3, 2023 |website=The Des Moines Register |language=en-US}}</ref>

A consensus four-star wide receiver, Lazard was a highly touted recruit out of high school.  He was ranked the No. 1 recruit of the state of [[Iowa]] and the 7th best receiver in the country by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Allen Lazard, 2014 Wide Receiver |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2014/allen-lazard-14325 |access-date=April 4, 2020 |website=Rivals.com}}</ref> Lazard ultimately followed his father Kevin (1990–93)<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 4, 2014 |title=Football: The curious recruitment of Allen Lazard |url=https://www.amestrib.com/article/20140204/Sports/302049888 |access-date=April 4, 2020 |website=The Ames Tribune |language=en}}</ref> and brother Anthony (2013–16) in playing for the Iowa State Cyclones over [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Notre Dame]], [[Nebraska Cornhuskers football|Nebraska]], [[Stanford Cardinal football|Stanford]], [[California Golden Bears football|California]] and [[Iowa Hawkeyes football|Iowa]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Allen Lazard – Football Recruiting – Player Profiles |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/football/recruiting/player/_/id/162082/allen-lazard |access-date=April 4, 2020 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

Prior to enrolling at Iowa State, Lazard played in the 2014 [[U.S. Army All-American Bowl]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 27, 2013 |title=2014 U.S. Army All-American Bowl rosters |url=https://247sports.com/Article/US-Army-All-American-Bowl-rosters-124381 |access-date=April 4, 2020 |website=247Sports}}</ref>

==College career==
===2014 season===
Opting not to redshirt, Lazard started 11 of the Cyclones 12 games. He finished second on the team in receptions (45) and receiving yards (593) as well as scoring three touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2014 Iowa State Cyclones Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/iowa-state/2014.html |access-date=July 3, 2023 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Both reception and receiving totals rank second all-time for an ISU freshman. The first catch of his career went for 48 yards against [[2014 North Dakota State Bison football team|North Dakota State]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 30, 2014 |title=FCS champion Bison stun Cyclones, extend FBS win streak to 5 |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/recap/_/gameId/400547840 |access-date=April 4, 2020 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> and he caught his first career touchdown pass against [[2014 Kansas State Wildcats football team|Kansas State]] the next week.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 6, 2014 |title=Jake Waters, No. 20 Kansas State rally past Iowa State |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/recap/_/gameId/400547843 |access-date=February 23, 2025 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> His season high was 96 yards and a touchdown against the [[2014 Toledo Rockets football team|Toledo Rockets]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 11, 2014 |title=Richardson rallies Iowa State past Toledo 37–20 |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/recap/_/gameId/400547872 |access-date=April 4, 2020 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

At the conclusion of the season, Lazard was named to the [[List of All-Big 12 Conference football teams|All-Big 12]] honorable mention team<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 10, 2014 |title=All-Big 12 Football Awards Announced |url=http://www.big12sports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=209801479 |access-date=April 4, 2020 |website=Big 12 Conference}}</ref> and earned ESPN.com Big 12 All-Underclassman honors.<ref name="cyclones.com" />

===2015 season===
Lazard built on the success from his freshman season by starting all 11 games he played in and led the team in receptions (56), receiving yards (808) and touchdown catches (6).<ref>{{Cite web |title=2015 Iowa State Cyclones Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/iowa-state/2015.html#all_team |access-date=April 4, 2020 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref> He ranked fifth in the [[Big 12 Conference football|Big 12]] and 59th nationally in receptions per game (5.1) and was sixth in the Big 12 and 51st in the nation in receiving yardage (73.5).<ref>{{Cite web |title=2015 Big 12 Conference Receiving Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/conferences/big-12/2015-receiving.html |access-date=April 4, 2020 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2015 Receiving Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/years/2015-receiving.html |access-date=April 4, 2020 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref> His seasons highs included a then career-high 147 yards receiving and a career-long 74-yard touchdown against [[2015 TCU Horned Frogs football team|TCU]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 17, 2015 |title=Boykin throws for 4 TDs, No. 3 TCU rolls past Iowa St 45–21 |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/recap/_/gameId/400763438 |access-date=April 4, 2020 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> and a pair of touchdowns on five catches for 87 yards against [[2015 Kansas State Wildcats football team|Kansas State]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 21, 2015 |title=Cantele kicks 42-yard FG; Kansas St. beats Iowa St. 38–35 |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/recap/_/gameId/400763460 |access-date=April 4, 2020 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

Lazard was named Second-team All-Big 12 by the [[Associated Press|AP]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 16, 2015 |title=2015 Associated Press All-Big 12 team |url=https://collegefootball.ap.org/article/2015-associated-press-all-big-12-team |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151221041615/https://collegefootball.ap.org/article/2015-associated-press-all-big-12-team |archive-date=December 21, 2015 |website=AP.org |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> and ESPN's Big 12 All-Underclassman team for second-straight season as well receiving the Pete Taylor Most Valuable Player.

===2016 season===
Lazard's breakout season was in [[2016 Iowa State Cyclones football team|2016]] and was one of the greatest single seasons in Cyclone history.  He once again led the team in receptions (69), receiving yards (1,018) and TD catches (7)<ref>{{Cite web |title=2016 Iowa State Cyclones Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/iowa-state/2016.html#all_rushing_and_receiving |access-date=April 4, 2020 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref> as well as breaking the school record for 100-yard receiving games with six and becoming the fourth player in school history to record a 1,000-yard season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Iowa State Athletics |url=http://www.cyclones.com/documents/2015/5/5/FB_Records.pdf |access-date=April 4, 2020 |website=cyclones.com |archive-date=March 6, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200306040705/https://cyclones.com/documents/2015/5/5/FB_Records.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> He ranked sixth in the Big 12 and 37th nationally in receptions per game (5.8) and ranked fifth in the Big 12 and 29th nationally in receiving yards per game (84.8).<ref>{{Cite web |title=2016 Big 12 Conference Receiving Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/conferences/big-12/2016-receiving.html |access-date=April 4, 2020 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2016 Receiving Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/years/2016-receiving.html |access-date=April 4, 2020 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref> Lazard opened the season with back-to-back 100-yard games against in-state rivals [[2016 Northern Iowa Panthers football team|UNI]] (129)<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 4, 2016 |title=Northern Iowa rallies to beat Iowa State 25–20 |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/recap/_/gameId/400868887 |access-date=April 4, 2020 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> and [[2016 Iowa Hawkeyes football team|Iowa]] (111).<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 10, 2016 |title=No. 16 Iowa throttles Iowa State 42–3 |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/recap/_/gameId/400868888 |access-date=April 4, 2020 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> Against [[2016 Kansas State Wildcats football team|Kansas State]], he tallied eight receptions for 134 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=K-State holds off Iowa State 31–26 for 3rd win in 4 games |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/recap/_/gameId/400869592 |access-date=April 4, 2020 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> He recorded a career-high 10 receptions for 120 yards and a touchdown against [[2016 Kansas Jayhawks football team|Kansas]].<ref name="ESPN">{{Cite web |title=Iowa State vs. Kansas – Game Recap – November 12, 2016 |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/game?gameId=400869594 |access-date=April 8, 2020 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> Lazard finished the season with three straight 100-yard games against Kansas (120),<ref name="ESPN" /> [[2016 Kansas Jayhawks football team|Texas Tech]] (137)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Iowa State clobbers Texas Tech 66–10 |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/recap/_/gameId/400869595 |access-date=April 4, 2020 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> and [[2016 West Virginia Mountaineers football team|West Virginia]] (103).<ref>{{Cite web |title=No. 18 West Virginia rolls past Iowa State 49–19 |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/recap/_/gameId/400869596 |access-date=April 4, 2020 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

Lazard was named First-team All-Big 12 by the Coaches<ref name="big12sports.com" /> and ESPN<ref>{{Cite web |last=Olson |first=Max |date=December 6, 2016 |title=2016 ESPN.com All-Big 12 team: Sooners' Heisman finalists lead way |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/big12/post/_/id/117081/2016-espn-com-all-big-12-team |access-date=April 4, 2020 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> and as the Pete Taylor Most Valuable Player for the second straight year.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 4, 2016 |title=Lazard Earns MVP Honors at Football Banquet |url=http://www.cyclones.com/news/2016/12/4/lazard-earns-mvp-honors-at-football-banquet.aspx? |access-date=April 4, 2020 |website=Iowa State Cyclones Athletics}}</ref>

===2017 season===
[[file:2017-0717-Big12MD-AllenLazard.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Lazard in college at [[Iowa State Cyclones football|Iowa State]] in 2017]]
In [[2017 Iowa State Cyclones football team|2017]], Lazard continued on his success of 2016. He again led the team in receptions, receiving yards, and touchdowns with 71, 941, and 10 respectively.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2017 Iowa State Cyclones Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/iowa-state/2017.html |access-date=January 25, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]]}}</ref> Against [[2017 Northern Iowa Panthers football team|Northern Iowa]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Northern Iowa vs. Iowa State – Game Summary – September 2, 2017 |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/game?gameId=400934488 |access-date=January 25, 2018 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> Lazard had eight receptions for 108 yards, he followed that up with two touchdown catches against [[2017 Iowa Hawkeyes football team|Iowa]] the next week.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Iowa vs. Iowa State – Game Summary – September 9, 2017 |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/game?gameId=400934499 |access-date=January 25, 2018 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> In the win at No. 3 [[2017 Oklahoma Sooners football team|Oklahoma]], Allen had 69 yards and a game-sealing touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Iowa State vs. Oklahoma – Game Summary – October 7, 2017 |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/game?gameId=400934523 |access-date=January 25, 2018 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> In the home victory ===Jacksonville Jaguars===
Lazard signed with the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] as an undrafted free agent on April 30, 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Crow |first=Alfie |date=April 30, 2018 |title=Jaguars announce 13 undrafted free agent signings |url=https://www.bigcatcountry.com/2018/4/30/17304202/jaguars-announce-13-undrafted-free-agent-signings |access-date=September 15, 2018 |website=Big Cat Country|publisher=SB Nation}}</ref> He was waived on September 1, 2018, and was signed to the [[practice squad]] the next day.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Oehser |first=John |date=September 1, 2018 |title=Roster reduction: Jaguars move to 53 players |url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/roster-reduction-jaguars-move-to-53-players |access-date=April 4, 2020 |website=Jaguars.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Oehser |first=John |date=September 2, 2018 |title=Jaguars sign 10 players to practice squad |url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/jaguars-sign-10-players-to-practice-squad |access-date=April 4, 2020 |website=Jaguars.com}}</ref>

===Green Bay Packers===
====2018 season====
On December 18, 2018, Lazard was signed by the [[Green Bay Packers]] off the Jaguars' practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 18, 2018 |title=Packers place RB Aaron Jones on IR |url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-place-rb-aaron-jones-on-ir |access-date=April 4, 2020 |website=Packers.com}}</ref>

====2019 season====
Lazard was waived on August 31, 2019, and was signed to the practice squad the next day. He was promoted to the active roster on September 4, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 4, 2019 |title=Packers sign WR Allen Lazard to active roster |url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-sign-wr-allen-lazard-to-active-roster |access-date=October 15, 2019 |website=Packers.com}}</ref> Lazard recorded his first professional touchdown, a 35-yard reception from [[Aaron Rodgers]], during a Week 6 win over the [[Detroit Lions]] on October 14, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Linton |first=Chance |date=October 14, 2019 |title=Allen Lazard fuels Packers' comeback "win" over Lions |url=https://247sports.com/Article/Green-Bay-Packers-Allen-Lazard-fuels-comeback-win-over-Detroit-Lions-136998747/ |access-date=October 15, 2019 |website=247Sports.com}}</ref> He had a breakout performance on December 1, 2019, in a 31–13 Week 13 victory over the [[New York Giants]], posting three catches for 103 yards and a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kruse |first=Zach |date=December 1, 2019 |title=Packers WR Allen Lazard sparks fast start, sets new career-high during win over Giants |url=https://packerswire.usatoday.com/2019/12/01/packers-wr-allen-lazard-sparks-fast-start-sets-new-career-high-during-win-over-giants/ |access-date=December 1, 2019 |website=USA Today}}</ref> Overall, Lazard finished the 2019 season with 35 receptions for 477 receiving yards and three receiving touchdowns, while also adding one rushing attempt for 21 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Allen Lazard 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/L/LazaAl00/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=April 5, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

====2020 season====
On March 17, 2020, the Packers tendered Lazard as an [[exclusive-rights free agent]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kruse |first=Zach |date=March 17, 2020 |title=Packers tender all 5 exclusive rights free agents |url=https://packerswire.usatoday.com/2020/03/17/packers-tender-all-5-exclusive-rights-free-agents/ |access-date=April 4, 2020 |website=Packers Wire|publisher=USA Today}}</ref> He signed the one-year tender on April 27, 2020.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Williams |first=Charean |date=April 27, 2020 |title=Allen Lazard, Chandon Sullivan sign tenders to return to Packers |work=NBCSports.com |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2020/04/27/allen-lazard-chandon-sullivan-sign-tenders-to-return-to-packers/ |access-date=April 28, 2020}}</ref> In the season-opener against the [[Minnesota Vikings]], Lazard caught four passes for 63 yards and his first touchdown of the season during the 43–34 road victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Green Bay Packers at Minnesota Vikings – September 13th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202009130min.htm |access-date=September 17, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> During ''Sunday Night Football'' against the [[New Orleans Saints]] in Week 3, Lazard finished with six receptions for 146 yards and a touchdown in the 37–30 road victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Green Bay Packers at New Orleans Saints – September 27th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202009270nor.htm |access-date=September 29, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on October 3, 2020, after undergoing core muscle surgery.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 3, 2020 |title=Packers place LB Christian Kirksey and WR Allen Lazard on injured reserve |url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-place-lb-christian-kirksey-and-wr-allen-lazard-on-injured-reserve |access-date=March 2, 2026 |website=Packers.com}}</ref> Lazard was activated on November 17, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 17, 2020 |title=Packers activate WR Allen Lazard |url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-activate-wr-allen-lazard |access-date=March 2, 2026 |website=Packers.com}}</ref> In Week 12, in his second game off of injured reserve, Lazard caught his third touchdown of the season in a 41–25 victory over the [[Chicago Bears]], along with 23 receiving yards. Lazard finished the season with 33 receptions for 451 yards and three touchdowns, nearly matching his previous year total despite playing in six fewer games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Allen Lazard 2020 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/L/LazaAl00/gamelog/2020/ |access-date=July 3, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

In the [[2020–21 NFL playoffs#NFC: Green Bay Packers 32, Los Angeles Rams 18|Divisional Round]] of the playoffs against the [[Los Angeles Rams]], Lazard recorded four catches for 96 yards, including a 58-yard touchdown, during the 32–18 win.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Divisional Round – Los Angeles Rams at Green Bay Packers – January 16th, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202101160gnb.htm |access-date=January 20, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the [[2020–21 NFL playoffs#NFC: Tampa Bay Buccaneers 31, Green Bay Packers 26|NFC Championship]] against the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], Lazard recorded three catches for 62 yards during the 31–26 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFC Championship – Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Green Bay Packers – January 24th, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202101240gnb.htm |access-date=January 31, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

====2021 season====
[[File:NFL 2021 - Week 7 - Washington vs. Packers JMG 1824 (51631520253).jpg|thumb|right|225px|Lazard (right) in 2021]]
On July 28, 2021, Lazard signed his exclusive rights tender, keeping him in Green Bay for the [[2021 Green Bay Packers season|2021 season]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sullivan |first=Tyler |date=July 27, 2021 |title=Allen Lazard reportedly signs tender with Packers; Green Bay also announces release of Blake Bortles |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/allen-lazard-reportedly-signs-tender-with-packers-green-bay-also-announces-release-of-blake-bortles/ |access-date=July 28, 2021 |website=CBSSports.com}}</ref> Lazard's season started off slowly, having 15 catches for 184 yards through the first eight games of the season. On October 26, ahead of the Packers' Week 9 game against the [[Arizona Cardinals]], fellow wide receiver [[Davante Adams]] tested positive for COVID-19. Lazard, who was unvaccinated, was placed on the COVID-19/Reserve list due to being a close contact.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Demovsky |first=Rob |date=October 26, 2021 |title=WR Lazard joins Adams on Packers' COVID list |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/32480650/green-bay-packers-place-allen-lazard-reserve-covid-19-list |access-date=October 28, 2021 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> He was activated off the COVID-19/Reserve list on November 1, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 1, 2021 |title=Packers activate WR Allen Lazard from reserve/COVID-19 list |url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-activate-wr-allen-lazard-from-reserve-covid-19-list |access-date=November 1, 2021 |website=Packers.com}}</ref> Lazard was fined $14,650 for violating NFL COVID-19 protocols along with quarterback Aaron Rodgers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Florio |first=Mike |author-link=Mike Florio |date=November 9, 2021 |title=NFL fines Packers $300,000, Aaron Rodgers and Allen Lazard $14,650 each |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/nfl-fines-packers-300000-aaron-rodgers-and-allen-lazard-14650 |access-date=July 3, 2023 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref>

Lazard was the recipient of backup quarterback Jordan Love's first NFL touchdown in a Week 9 13–7 road loss to the [[Kansas City Chiefs]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Huber |first=Bill |date=November 7, 2021 |title=Not Much to Love as Chiefs Beat Packers |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/packers/gameday/not-much-to-love-as-chiefs-beat-packers |access-date=December 29, 2021 |website=Sports Illustrated |language=en}}</ref> Lazard picked up the pace through the second half of the season. In Week 14, Lazard had six receptions for 75 yards and a touchdown in a 45–30 win over the Bears. In Week 16, in a Christmas Day showdown with the [[Cleveland Browns]], Lazard caught Rodgers' 443rd career touchdown pass with the Packers, breaking the previous record of 442, held by [[Brett Favre]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=December 25, 2021 |title=Aaron Rodgers sets Packers record with 443rd career TD pass |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/aaron-rodgers-sets-packers-record-with-443rd-career-td-pass |access-date=July 3, 2023 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> The following week, he caught all six of his targets for 72 yards and a touchdown as the Packers won 37–10 against the Vikings to clinch home-field advantage throughout the playoffs. In the regular-season finale, Lazard played just one half as the Packers rested their starters in the second half against the [[Detroit Lions]]; despite that, Lazard matched a season-high 75 receiving yards and notched a career-high two touchdowns in a single game as the Packers lost on the road by a score of 37–30.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Green Bay Packers at Detroit Lions – January 9th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202201090nor.htm |access-date=January 29, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

Lazard finished the 2021 season with 40 receptions for 513 yards and eight touchdowns, all career highs. His five touchdowns over the final five weeks of the season were tied for second most in the NFL over that time span, second only to teammate Davante Adams.<ref>{{Cite tweet |number=1481041674834956295 |user=mattschneidman |title=Most TD catches in the NFL over the final five regular season games}} {{Primary source inline|date=July 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Allen Lazard 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/L/LazaAl00/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=July 3, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2021 Green Bay Packers Rosters, Stats, Schedule, Team Draftees, Injury Reports |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/gnb/2021.htm |access-date=July 3, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

====2022 season====
On March 15, 2022, the Packers placed a second-round restricted free agent tender on Lazard.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kruse |first=Zach |date=March 15, 2022 |title=Packers place second-round tender on restricted free agent Allen Lazard |url=https://packerswire.usatoday.com/2022/03/15/packers-place-second-round-tender-on-restricted-free-agent-allen-lazard/ |access-date=July 3, 2023 |website=Packers Wire}}</ref> It was signed on June 13, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shook |first=Nick |date=June 13, 2022 |title=Packers WR Allen Lazard signs RFA tender after sitting out minicamp for long-term deal |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/packers-wr-allen-lazard-signs-rfa-tender-after-sitting-out-minicamp-for-long-ter |access-date=June 17, 2022 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> In Week 4, against the [[New England Patriots]], Lazard had six receptions for 116 receiving yards in the 27–24 overtime victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New England Patriots at Green Bay Packers – October 2nd, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202210020gnb.htm |access-date=July 3, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> In the 2022 season, Lazard appeared in and started 15 games. He finished with 60 receptions for 788 receiving yards and six receiving touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Allen Lazard 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/L/LazaAl00/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=July 3, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

===New York Jets===
[[File:Allen Lazard vs Christian Benford 2023.jpg|thumb|right|Lazard (#10) lining up against [[Christian Benford]] of the [[Buffalo Bills]] in 2023]]
On March 17, 2023, Lazard signed a four-year, $44 million contract with the [[New York Jets]], preceding Rodgers' trade to New York from the Packers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lange |first=Randy |date=March 17, 2023 |title=Jets Sign Free Agent WR Allen Lazard |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-free-agent-wr-allen-lazard |access-date=March 17, 2023 |website=NewYorkJets.com}}</ref> In 14 games in the 2023 season, he finished with 23 receptions for 311 yards and one touchdown,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Allen Lazard 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/L/LazaAl00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=July 6, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> playing without Rodgers under center for the vast majority of the season as the latter suffered a season-ending Achilles injury in week 1.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sullivan |first=Phil |date=September 12, 2023 |title=Jets Place Aaron Rodgers on Injured Reserve; Saleh Commits To Zach Wilson |url=https://www.jetnation.com/2023/09/13/jets-place-aaron-rodgers-on-injured-reserve-saleh-commits-to-zach-wilson/ |access-date=September 14, 2023 |website=JetNation.com}}</ref> With his signing seen by many as an "appeasement" move to get Rodgers to agree to the trade, Lazard was deactivated when Rodgers was ruled out the last two games of the season.<ref name="Rodgers return NYP">{{Cite web |last=Bondy |first=Stefan |date=September 20, 2024 |title=Allen Lazard's resurgence continues under Aaron Rodgers' Jets return |url=https://nypost.com/2024/09/20/sports/allen-lazards-resurgence-continues-under-aaron-rodgers-jets-return/ |access-date=October 13, 2024 |language=en-US}}</ref> He finished the 2023 season with 23 receptions for 311 yards and a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Allen Lazard 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/L/LazaAl00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=February 23, 2025 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

The following season, Lazard caught Rodgers' first touchdown pass as a Jet during week 1. Despite dropping a crucial pass during the game's opening drive, Lazard finished with two touchdowns during the 32–19 loss to the San Francisco 49ers.<ref name="r920">{{cite web | last=Teape | first=Kenneth | title=New York Jets Embattled Playmaker Explains Monster Week 1 Performance | website=SI.com| date=September 13, 2024 | url=https://www.si.com/nfl/jets/news/new-york-jets-embattled-playmaker-explains-monster-week-1-performance | access-date=October 19, 2024}}</ref> In the first six games of 2024 alone, Lazard surpassed his total receptions and yards from the previous season and caught five touchdowns. On October 31, 2024, Lazard was placed on [[injured reserve]] due to a chest injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-place-allen-lazard-leku-fotu-ir-sign-riley-patterson-alec-lindstrom-to-active-roster-10-31-2024|work=NewYorkJets.com|title=Jets Place WR Allen Lazard, DT Leku Fotu on IR; Sign K Riley Patterson, OL Alec Lindstrom to Active Roster|first=Ethan|last=Greenberg|date=October 31, 2024|accessdate=October 31, 2024}}</ref> He was activated on December 7.<ref name="v802">{{cite web | last=Greenberg | first=Ethan | title=Jets Activate WR Allen Lazard, OL Wes Schweitzer from Injured Reserve | website=New York Jets | date=December 7, 2024 | url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-activate-allen-lazard-wes-schweitzer-12-07-2024 | access-date=February 23, 2025}}</ref> He finished the 2024 season with 37 receptions for 530 yards and six touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Allen Lazard 2024 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/L/LazaAl00/gamelog/2024/ |access-date=February 23, 2025 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

On December 16, 2025, Lazard was released by the Jets.<ref>{{cite web |last=Weir |first=Susanna |date=December 16, 2025 |title=Jets Release WR Allen Lazard |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-ochaun-mathis-to-practice-squad-release-allen-lazard-12-16-2025 |access-date=March 2, 2026 |website=NewYorkJets.com}}</ref> He finished the season with 10 catches for 70 yards and one touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Allen Lazard 2025 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/L/LazaAl00/gamelog/2025/ |access-date=2026-03-02 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

'''Alvin Wilbert Blount''' (born February 12, 1965) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Dallas Cowboys]]. He also was a member of the [[Washington Commandos]] and [[Albany Firebirds]] of the [[Arena Football League]] (AFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Maryland Terrapins football|Maryland Terrapins]].

==Early life==
Blount attended [[Eleanor Roosevelt High School (Maryland)|Eleanor Roosevelt High School]], where he practiced football, [[baseball]] and [[track & field|track]]. He was a two-way player at [[running back]] and [[defensive back]].

==College career==
He accepted a football scholarship from the [[University of Maryland, College Park]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Wilbon |first=Michael |date=August 14, 1983 |title=Maryland's Class of '83 Looks Like 'Fastest Ever' |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/sports/1983/08/14/marylands-class-of-83-looks-like-fastest-ever/7678acc5-b2e9-49a2-9fe4-841627683d01/ |access-date=January 12, 2019}}</ref> As a freshman, he was a backup running back, only having 8 carries for 66 yards (8.3-yard avg.).

As a sophomore, he shared the running back position with [[Rick Badanjek]], collecting 128 carries for 759 yards (5.9-yard avg.) and 5 [[touchdown]]s. Against both [[Wake Forest University]] and the [[University of North Carolina]], he had matching 52-yard touchdown receptions. He was a part of one of the greatest comebacks in college football history, in the 42–40 win against the [[University of Miami]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Wilbon |first=Michael |date=November 11, 1984 |title=Maryland: Greatest Comeback Ever |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/sports/1984/11/11/maryland-greatest-comeback-ever/7a037372-58e0-4f2e-9181-a0f1f4f9e0d7/ |access-date=January 12, 2019}}</ref> Against [[Clemson University]], he had a career-high 214 rushing yards.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Terrapins Gain 577 Yards In 41-23 Win Over Tigers |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/sports/1984/11/18/terrapins-gain-577-yards-in-41-23-win-over-tigers/16592372-611f-4d83-82f5-bd9aa73d4603/ |access-date=January 12, 2019}}</ref> Against the [[University of Virginia]], he had a career long 72-yard touchdown run, finishing with 104 rushing yards.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Maryland Runs Over Virginia For ACC Title |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/sports/1984/11/25/maryland-runs-over-virginia-for-acc-title/7a0cde93-d8ef-41e1-8ced-8ea2ba078c24/ |access-date=January 12, 2019}}</ref>

As a junior, he was named the regular starter, although he still shared the [[running back]] position with Badanjek. He registered 171 carries for 828 yards (4.8-yard avg.) and 4 touchdowns. Against the [[University of Virginia]], he had 26 carries for 186 yards.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Terrapins Take Cavaliers, ACC Title, 33-21 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/sports/1985/11/30/terrapins-take-cavaliers-acc-title-33-21/cc9a1aab-1cca-4f3f-866b-6d83f9a49313/ |access-date=January 12, 2019}}</ref>

As a senior co-captain, he had 119 carries for 505 yards (4.2-yard avg.) and 3 touchdowns. He didn't have any 100-yard games, but showed he was an all-round running back, displaying solid receiving and blocking skills.

He finished his college career with 426 carries for 2,158 yards (fifth in school history), a 5.1-yard rushing average, 12 rushing touchdowns, six 100-yard games, 64 receptions for 567 yards and 5 receiving touchdowns.

===Dallas Cowboys===
Blount was selected by the [[Dallas Cowboys]] in the 9th round (235th overall) of the [[1987 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1987 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1987/draft.htm |access-date=October 1, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL Draft List |url=https://www.upi.com/Archives/1987/04/29/NFL-Draft-List/6040546667200/ |access-date=January 12, 2019}}</ref> As a rookie, he set the club record for a vertical leap (39 inches). He was waived on September 7.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Dallas Cowboys went with experience at quarterback |url=https://www.upi.com/Archives/1987/09/07/The-Dallas-Cowboys-went-with-experience-at-quarterback-and/8353557985600/ |access-date=January 12, 2019}}</ref>

After the [[NFLPA]] strike was declared on the third week of the [[1987 NFL season|1987 season]], those contests were canceled (reducing the 16-game season to 15) and the NFL decided that the games would be played with replacement players. He was re-signed to be a part of the Dallas replacement team that was given the mock name "Rhinestone Cowboys" by the media.<ref>{{Cite news |date=October 4, 1987 |title=Who's playing today and for whom |work=Lakeland Ledger}}</ref> He started against the [[New York Jets]], leading the team with 28 carries for 72 yards and one touchdown. He started against the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] and although he shared the position with [[Tony Dorsett]], he posted 18 carries for 53 yards and 2 touchdowns. He suffered a knee injury in the third game against the [[Washington Redskins]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Veterans Bring Boos |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/sports/1987/10/20/veterans-bring-on-boos/f48337b4-050b-4e69-9275-d6cef4cdd254/ |access-date=January 12, 2019}}</ref> On October 27, he was placed on the [[injured reserve list]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=For the Record |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/sports/1987/10/28/for-the-record/699f57f3-58b3-472a-8a5b-007f8a0ec7d0/ |access-date=January 12, 2019}}</ref> He wasn't re-signed after the season.

===San Francisco 49ers===
On February 9, [[1988 NFL season|1988]], he was signed as a [[free agent]] by the [[San Francisco 49ers]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=For the Record |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/sports/1988/02/10/for-the-record/450e3031-e108-420b-a4b8-813d30206858/ |access-date=January 12, 2019}}</ref> He was released before the start of the season.

===Edmonton Eskimos===
In [[1989 CFL season|1989]], he signed as a free agent with the [[Edmonton Eskimos]] of the [[Canadian Football League]]. He was released before the start of the season in July.

===Washington Commandos===
In [[1990 Arena Football League season|1990]], he signed with the [[Washington Commandos]] of the [[Arena Football League]] (AFL) as a [[Fullback (gridiron football)|fullback]]-[[linebacker]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Commandos Head Back Into The Arena |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/sports/1990/06/09/commandos-head-back-into-the-arena/a2345cf9-3a48-4227-9c27-889543da4061/ |access-date=January 12, 2019}}</ref> He appeared in 5 games, tallying 15 receptions for 149 yards, 6 carries for 27 yards and 12 tackles.

===Albany Firebirds===
On June 5, [[1991 Arena Football League season|1991]], he was signed by the [[Albany Firebirds]] of the AFL as a fullback-linebacker.<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 6, 1991 |title=Transactions |url=https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/452029576/ |access-date=January 12, 2019}}</ref> He appeared in 9 games, making 13 carries for 25 yards, one touchdown, 5 receptions for 27 yards, 33 tackles, one interception and 1.5 sacks.

==Personal life==
In 1989, he had a tryout with the U.S. national [[bobsledding]] team.<ref>{{Cite news |date=August 27, 1989 |title=Ex-Terrapin Tries Hand At Bobsledding |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/sports/1989/08/28/ex-terrapin-tries-hand-at-bobsledding/fb15372c-ffe7-4e15-9dc7-bc6532dbf1f3/ |access-date=January 12, 2019 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref>

'''Alton Ledell Robinson''' (born June 2, 1998) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Syracuse Orange football|Syracuse Orange]].

==Early life==
Robinson was born in [[San Antonio, Texas]] and grew up in [[Converse, Texas]]. He attended [[Judson High School]] where he was a member of the basketball, football and track & field teams. He recorded 15 sacks and 20 tackles for loss as a junior and was named first-team All-District 25-6A.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Robinson latest in long line of blue-chip Judson defensive players |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2015/robinson-latest-in-long-line-of-bluechip-judson-defensive-players |last=Flores |first=David |date=August 21, 2015 |website=USATodayHSS.com |access-date=March 20, 2020}}</ref> He committed to play [[college football]] for the [[Texas A&M Aggies football|Texas A&M Aggies]] over offers from [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama]], [[Texas Longhorns football|Texas]], [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan]], [[Baylor Bears football|Baylor]] and [[Oklahoma State Cowboys football|Oklahoma State]] after his junior year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Holland |first=EJ |date=June 12, 2015 |title=Texas A&M adds commitment from three-star DE Alton Robinson |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/2015/06/12/texas-am-adds-commitment-from-three-star-de-alton-robinson/ |access-date=March 20, 2020 |website=[[The Dallas Morning News]]}}</ref> As a senior, Robinson recorded 44 tackles, including 23 for a loss, and 12 sacks and was named honorable mention All-State and All-Area by the ''[[San Antonio Express-News]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=HS FOOTBALL: Three Midland players earn Class 6A all-state nods |url=https://www.mrt.com/sports/highschool/article/HS-FOOTBALL-Three-Midland-players-earn-Class-6A-7417751.php |date=December 17, 2015 |website=MRT.com |access-date=March 20, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Football: Steele's Jackson, Clemens' Harris lead E-N All-Area team |url=https://www.expressnews.com/sports/high_school/high_school_football/article/Football-Steele-s-Jackson-Clemens-Harris-6721927.php |date=December 26, 2015 |website=[[San Antonio Express-News]] |access-date=March 20, 2020}}</ref> Shortly after National Signing Day, Robinson was charged with second-degree felony robbery after being accused of stealing an ex-girlfriend's purse, and eventually, Texas A&M withdrew their scholarship offer.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alton Robinson, Texas A&M Recruit, Arrested for Robbery: Details, Comments |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2617151-alton-robinson-texas-am-recruit-arrested-for-robbery-details-comments |last=Wells |first=Adam |date=February 16, 2016 |website=[[Bleacher Report]] |access-date=March 20, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Alton Robinson has lost football scholarship with A&M |url=https://www.khou.com/article/sports/college/alton-robinson-has-lost-football-scholarship-with-am/285-288327359 |last=Flores |first=David |date=August 5, 2016 |website=KHOU.com |access-date=March After charges were dropped Robinson was close to signing with Oklahoma State, but was unable to due to the [[Big 12 Conference]]'s misconduct policy.<ref name="Dismissed charges">{{Cite web |title=How dismissed charges are still keeping ex-Texas A&M signee Alton Robinson out of the Power Five |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/2017/08/03/how-dismissed-charges-are-still-keeping-ex-texas-am-signee-alton-robinson-out-of-the-power-five/ |last=Baby |first=Ben |date=August 3, 2017 |website=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |access-date=March 20, 2020}}</ref>

==College career==
Robinson began his collegiate career at [[Northeastern Oklahoma A&M College]]. In his only season with the Golden Norsemen, he recorded 67 total tackles, 17 tackles for loss and 14 sacks and was named second-team All-[[Southwest Junior College Football Conference]]. Following the end of the season Robinson again recruited by Oklahoma State but was not offered a scholarship due to uncertainty regarding the Big 12's moral conduct policy.<ref name="Dismissed charges" /> He committed to transfer to [[New Mexico State Aggies football|New Mexico State]], but he ultimately de-committed in August and opted to sign with [[Syracuse Orange football|Syracuse]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Report: Former A&M signee Alton Robinson headed to NMSU |url=https://247sports.com/college/texas-am/Article/Report-Former-Texas-AM-signee-Alton-Robinson-headed-to-New-Mexico-State-Aggies-53493280/ |last=Perroni |first=Brian |date=July 8, 2017 |website=247Sports.com |access-date=March 20, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Syracuse football adds JUCO DE Alton Robinson; eligible to play immediately |url=https://www.syracuse.com/orangefootball/2017/08/syracuse_football_adds_juco_de_alton_robinson_eligible_to_play_immediately.html |last=Bailey |first=Stephen |date=August 20, 2017 |website=[[The Post-Standard]] |access-date=March 20, 2020}}</ref>

Robinson became a starter at defensive end for the Orange early in his first season with the team and led the team with five sacks and the defensive line with 30 tackles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=REDEMPTION:Alton Robinson faced up to 20 years in prison on a robbery charge. Robinson sat out the team's bowl game for personal reasons.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Syracuse to be without DE Alton Robinson, NT McKinley Williams for bowl game |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/25610090/syracuse-orange-de-alton-robinson-nt-mckinley-williams-camping-world-bowl |last=Hale |first=David |date=December 24, 2018 |website=[[ESPN.com]] |access-date=March 20, 2020}}</ref> Robinson was named honorable mention All-ACC as a senior after recording 46 tackles, 9.5 tackles for loss, 4.5 sacks and a forced fumble.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Six Syracuse football players receive All-ACC honors for 2019 |url=https://www.nunesmagician.com/2019/12/3/20993577/six-syracuse-football-players-receive-all-acc-honors-for-2019-orange-conference-hofrichter |last=Cassillo |first=John |date=December 3, 2019 |website=NunesMagician.com |publisher=[[SB Nation]] |access-date=March 20, 2020}}</ref>

'''Asai Alohilaniokala''' "'''Alohi'''" '''Gilman'''<ref>{{cite web |last1=Miller |first1=Jeff |title=Drue Tranquill recommended Chargers draft Notre Dame teammate Alohi Gilman |url=https://www.yahoo.com/entertainment/drue-tranquill-recommended-chargers-draft-214653929.html |website=Yahoo |publisher=Los Angeles Times |access-date=14 January 2021 |date=12 July 2020}}</ref> (born September 17, 1997) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] for the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Notre Dame Fighting Irish]] and [[Navy Midshipmen football|Navy Midshipmen]] and was drafted by the [[Los Angeles Chargers]] in the sixth round of the [[2020 NFL draft]]. His younger brother, Alaka'i Gilman, played safety for the [[Utah Utes football|Utah Utes]] and is now a pit crew member for [[Hendrick Motorsports]]<ref>{{cite news |last1=DeMello |first1=Rob |title=Hawaii’s Gilman tackles new sport on NASCAR pit crew |url=https://www.khon2.com/sports/hawaiis-gilman-tackles-new-sport-on-nascar-pit-crew/ |access-date=16 May 2026 |work=KHON2 |date=30 Sep 2025}}</ref>.

==College career==
[[File:IX8A1254 (30584747868).jpg |left|thumb|Gilman with Notre Dame in 2018]]
Gilman played his freshman year at the [[United States Naval Academy]]. He played in all 14 of the [[Navy Midshipmen football|Midshipmen]]'s games and was named honorable mention All-[[American Athletic Conference]] after finishing second on the team with 76 tackles along with five passes defended and two fumble recoveries.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.capitalgazette.com/sports/navy/ph-ac-cs-alohi-gilman-transfer-0602-20170601-story.html|title=Standout safety Alohi Gilman transferring from Navy|work=[[Capital Gazette]]|date=June 2017}}</ref> Gilman transferred to Notre Dame after his freshman year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/19596557/alohi-gilman-transfers-navy-midshipmen-notre-dame-fighting-irish|title=Alohi Gilman transfers to Notre Dame from Navy|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=June 10, 2017}}</ref>

Gilman sat out his sophomore year per [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA) transfer rules. As a junior he started 13 games and finished the season with 95 tackles, three tackles for loss, and three forced fumbles, with two interceptions with five passes broken up.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://irish.nbcsports.com/2019/07/18/notre-dame-99-to-2-no-11-alohi-gilman-senior-safety/|title=Notre Dame 99-to-2: No. 11 Alohi Gilman, senior safety|work=[[NBC Sports]]|date=July 18, 2019 }}</ref> He was named a team captain as a senior and recorded 74 tackles, three tackles for loss and one sack with one interception, two passes broken up, one fumble recovery and three forced fumbles.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/2020/04/19/sports/safety-alohi-gilman-prepared-his-star-turn-nfl/|title=Safety Alohi Gilman prepared for his star turn in the NFL, and he's got a quality Bill Belichick likes|work=[[Boston Globe]]}}</ref> After the end of season, Gilman announced that he would forgo his final year of NCAA eligibility to enter the [[2020 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/notre-dame/2019/12/30/notre-dame-football-alohi-gilman-heads-nfl-draft/2780183001/|title=Notre Dame football: Alohi Gilman heads to the NFL Draft|work=[[Indianapolis Star]]}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Pre-draft===
He accepted an invitation to participate in the [[2020 Senior Bowl]] and performed well until a hamstring injury rendered him unable to play.<ref>{{cite web| title=A Strong Combine Is Needed For Alohi Gilman| url=https://www.si.com/college/notredame/football/alohi-gilman-combine-preview| access-date=April 13, 2025| website=si.com| author=Bryan Driskel| date=March 1, 2020}}</ref> Prior to the NFL Combine, Michael Renner of [[Pro Football Focus]] had Gilman ranked as the ninth best safety in the draft.<ref>{{cite web| title=PFF's ranking of the top 10 safeties in 2020 NFL Draft| url=https://247sports.com/longformarticle/2020-nfl-draft-top-10-safeties-grant-delpit-ashtyn-davis-xavier-mckinney-terrell-burgess-kvon-wallace-antoine-winfield-julian-blackmon-jr-reed-alohi-gilman-jalen-elliott-143451550/| access-date=April 13, 2025| website=247sports.com| author=Clint Buckley| date=February 6, 2020}}</ref> He attended the [[NFL Scouting Combine]] and completed all of the combined drills and exercises. Kevin Hanson of ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' had Gilman ranked as the 11th best safety prospect in the draft.<ref>{{cite web| title=2020 NFL Draft Prospect Rankings: Safeties| url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2020/02/21/nfl-draft-2020-safeties-rankings-best-prospects| access-date=April 13, 2025| website=SI.com| date=February 20, 2020| author=Kevin Hanson}}</ref> [[Scouts Inc.]] listed Gilman as the 11th best safety prospect (142nd overall) on their big board.<ref>{{cite web| title=2020 NFL draft rankings: Scouts inc.'s full board, grades| url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/draft2020/story/_/id/41035192/2020-nfl-draft-rankings-top-prospects-scouts-inc| access-date=April 13, 2025| website=ESPN.com| author=[[Scouts Inc.]]| date=April 20, 2020}}</ref> [[NFL.com|NFL media]] analyst [[Daniel Jeremiah]] had him ranked 13th among all safety prospects (143rd overall) available in the draft.<ref>{{cite web| title=Daniel Jeremiah's top 150 prospects in the 2020 NFL Draft class| url=https://www.nfl.com/news/daniel-jeremiah-s-top-150-prospects-in-the-2020-nfl-draft-class-0ap3000001110012|access-date=April 13, 2025|website=NFL.com|author=Daniel Jeremiah|date=April 20, 2020}}</ref> Josh Keatley of ''[[USA TODAY|USA TODAY Sports]]'' ranked him as the 19th best safety prospect.<ref>{{cite web|title=2020 NFL Draft rankings: Safeties|url=https://brownswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/browns/2020/04/13/2020-nfl-draft-rankings-safeties/79285128007/|access-date=April 13, 2025|website=brownswire.usatoday.com|author=Josh Keatley|date=April 13, 2020}}</ref> NFL draft analysts varied on Gilman's draft projections with some projecting him to possibly go as early as the third round with most projecting a fifth or sixth round selection.<ref>{{cite web| title=DraftScout.com: Alohi Gilman, S, Notre Dame|url=https://draftscout.com/dsprofile.php?PlayerId=1020054&DraftYear=2020| access-date=April 13, 2025| website=draftscout.com}}</ref>

=== Los Angeles Chargers ===

==== 2020 ====
The [[Los Angeles Chargers]] selected Gilman in the sixth round (186th overall) of the [[2020 NFL draft]]. Gilman was the 15th safety drafted in 2020. He was reunited with former Notre Dame teammate [[Drue Tranquill]] who suggested to Los Angeles Chargers staff to draft Gilman.<ref name="m143">{{cite web |title=Chargers Select S Alohi Gilman in Sixth Round |website=Chargers.com |date=2020-04-25 |url=https://www.chargers.com/news/chargers-select-s-alohi-gilman-in-sixth-round |access-date=2024-10-22}}</ref>
{{external media 
| video1 =
[https://www.chargers.com/video/chargers-select-notre-dame-db-alohi-gilman-with-no-186-overall-pick-of-the-2020- Chargers select Alohi Gilman No. 186]
| video2 =
[https://www.patriots.com/video/2020-draft-prospects-alohi-gilman-s-notre-dame 2020 Draft Prospects: Alohi Gilman]
}}
On July 22, 2020, the [[2020 Los Angeles Chargers season|Los Angeles Chargers]] signed Gilman to a four–year, $3.48 million [[rookie]] [[contract]] that included a [[signing bonus]] of $187,876.<ref name="spotrac">{{cite web| title=Spotrac.com: Alohi Gilman contract| url=https://www.spotrac.com/nfl/player/_/id/47782/alohi-gilman| access-date=April 13, 2025| website=Spotrac.com}}</ref>

He entered training camp as a backup and competed for a roster spot as a backup strong safety and special teams player against [[Roderic Teamer]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Chargers depth chart 2020: Los Angeles' projected Week 1 starters, 53-man roster heading into training camp |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/chargers-depth-chart-2020-los-angeles-projected-week-1-starters-53-man-roster-heading-into-training/| access-date=April 13, 2025| website=cbssports.com| author=Bryan DeArdo| date=July 20, 2020}}</ref> Gilman secured his roster spot after Teamer was suspended for the first four games due to a substance policy violation.<ref>{{cite web| title=Roderic Teamer has been suspended for the first 4 games of the 2020 season| url=https://www.boltsfromtheblue.com/2020/7/13/21323277/chargers-news-nfl-roderic-teamer-schefter| access-date=April 13, 2025| website=boltsfromtheblue.com| author=Michael Peterson| date=July 13, 2020}}</ref> Head coach [[Anthony Lynn]] named him a backup and listed him as the second strong safety on the depth chart to begin the season, behind starting safeties [[Rayshawn Jenkins]] and [[Nasir Adderley]] and the primary backup [[Desmond King (American football)|Desmond King]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Takeaways from Chargers first depth chart of 2020| url=https://chargerswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/chargers/2020/09/08/takeaways-from-chargers-first-depth-chart-of-2020/79419955007/| access-date=April 13, 2025| website=chargerswire.usatoday.com| date=September 8, 2020| author=Gavino Borquez}}</ref> On September 5, 2020, the Chargers placed their expected starting strong safety [[Derwin James]] on injured reserve due to a torn meniscus.

On September 13, 2020, Gilman made his professional regular season debut in the Los Angeles Chargers' season-opener at the [[2020 Cincinnati Bengals season|Cincinnati Bengals]], but was limited to special teams as they won 16–13. He was inactive as a healthy scratch during a 39–29 victory against the [[2020 Jacksonville Jaguars season|Jacksonville Jaguars]] in Week 7.<ref>{{cite web| title=Chargers Week 7 Inactives: Turner, Bulaga OUT once more| url=https://www.boltsfromtheblue.com/2020/10/25/21533245/chargers-inactives-news-turner-bulaga-tyrod-hill-gilman| access-date=April 13, 2025| website=boltsfromtheblue.com| date=October 25, 2020}}</ref> On January 3, 2021, Gilman earned the first start of his career in place of Rayshawn Jenkins who was inactive due to an ankle injury. He set a season-high with three combined tackles (two solo) during a 38–21 victory at the [[2020 Kansas City Chiefs season|Kansas City Chiefs]]. He played mainly on special teams as a rookie, but began appearing in defense for the last five games. He finished his rookie season with only seven combined tackles (five solo) in 15 games and one start.<ref>{{cite web| title=Pro-Football-Reference: Alohi Gilman Game Logs (2020)| url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/G/GilmAl00.htm| access-date=April 13, 2025| website=pro-football-reference.com}}</ref>

==== 2021 ====
On January 4, 2021, the Los Angeles Chargers [[dismissal (employment)|fired]] head coach Anthony Lynn after they finished the [[2020 NFL season]] with a 7–9 record.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/30650606/los-angeles-chargers-fire-anthony-lynn-four-seasons-coach | title=Los Angeles Chargers fire Anthony Lynn after four seasons as coach | work=ESPN.com | first=Shelley | last=Smith | date=January 4, 2021 | access-date=November 25, 2021}}</ref> On January 17, 2021, the Chargers hired [[2020 Los Angeles Rams season|Los Angeles Rams']] defensive coordinator [[Brandon Staley]] as their new head coach.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chargers.com/news/brandon-staley-head-coach-chargers-agree-to-terms|title=Chargers Agree to Terms with Brandon Staley as Head Coach|last=Communications|first=Chargers|date=January 17, 2021|website=chargers.com|access-date=January 17, 2021}}</ref> Throughout training camp, he competed for a roster spot as a backup safety and special teams player against [[Mark Webb (safety)|Mark Webb]] under new defensive coordinator [[Renaldo Hill]]. He was named the primary backup safety to begin the season, behind starting duo Derwin James and Nasir Adderley.<ref>{{cite web| title=Chargers depth chart 2021: Los Angeles' 53-man roster, projected starters as season approaches| url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/chargers-depth-chart-2021-los-angeles-53-man-roster-projected-starters-as-season-approaches/| access-date=April 13, 2025| website=cbssports.com| author=Jeff Kerr| date=September 1, 2021}}</ref>

On September 26, 2021, Gilman set a season-high with seven solo tackles, made one pass deflection, and led the Chargers to a 30–24 comeback victory at the [[2021 Kansas City Chiefs season|Kansas City Chiefs]] by making his first career interception on a pass thrown by [[Patrick Mahomes]] to tight end [[Travis Kelce]] with 1:55 remaining in the fourth quarter as the game was tied 24–24. His interception led to the game-winning 59–yard drive ending with a four–yard touchdown pass from [[Justin Herbert]] to wide receiver [[Mike Williams (wide receiver, born 1994)|Mike Williams]] to win 27–24. He was inactive for the Chargers' 27–24 victory at the [[2021 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]] in Week 9 due to an ankle injury.<ref name="fox">{{cite web| title=Fox Sports: Alohi Gilman| url=https://www.foxsports.com/nfl/alohi-gilman-player-injuries| access-date=April 13, 2025| website=foxsports.com}}</ref> He was also sidelined for five consecutive games (Weeks 11–15) after injuring his quadriceps. He finished the [[2021 NFL season]] with a total of 42 combined tackles (28 solo), one pass deflection, and one interception in 11 games and three starts.<ref>{{cite web| title=Pro-Football-Reference: Alohi Gilman Game Logs (2021)| url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/G/GilmAl00.htm| access-date=April 13, 2025| website=pro-football-reference.com}}</ref> He received an overall grade of 58.8 from Pro Football Focus in 2021.<ref name="PFF1"/><ref name="PFF"/>

==== 2022 ====
Throughout training camp, he competed for a roster spot as a special teams player and to be the primary backup safety against [[JT Woods]], [[Raheem Layne]], [[Ben DeLuca]], and Mark Webb. Head coach Brandon Staley named him the primary backup safety to begin the season, behind starters [[Derwin James]] and [[Nasir Adderley]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Chargers Release Unofficial Depth Chart Ahead of Week 1| url=https://www.si.com/nfl/chargers/news/chargers-unofficial-depth-chart-week-1-2022-nfl-season| access-date=April 13, 2025| website=SI.com| date=September 6, 2022}}</ref>

Before Week 5, head coach Brandon Staley named Gilman the starting safety in lieu of Nasir Adderley, who he chose to bench after a poor performance in Week 4 against the [[2022 Houston Texans season|Houston Texans]].<ref>{{cite web| title=How Chargers safety Nasir Adderley came back stronger after benching| url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3717683/2022/10/21/chargers-nasir-adderly-keenan-allen/| access-date=April 13, 2025| website=[[The New York Times]]| date=October 21, 2022}}</ref> On October 9, 2022, Gilman earned his first start of the season and had seven combined tackles (four solo), a pass deflection, and helped secure a 30–28 victory at the [[2022 Cleveland Browns season|Cleveland Browns]] by intercepting a pass by [[Jacoby Brissett]] to wide receiver [[Amari Cooper]] with only 2:54 remaining in the game. In Week 12, he set a season-high with ten combined tackles (five solo) and broke up a pass during a 25–24 victory at the [[2022 Arizona Cardinals season|Arizona Cardinals]]. He finished the season with 58 combined tackles (35 solo), three pass deflections, one forced fumble, and one interception in 17 games and three starts.<ref>{{cite web| title=Pro-Football-Reference: Alohi Gilman Game Logs (2022)| url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/G/GilmAl00.htm| access-date=April 13, 2025| website=pro-football-reference.com}}</ref> He received an overall grade of 54.3 from Pro Football Focus in 2022.<ref name="PFF1"/><ref name="PFF"/>

The [[2022 Los Angeles Chargers season|Los Angeles Chargers]] finished the [[2022 NFL season]] second in the [[AFC West]] with a 10–7 record. On January 14, 2023, Gilman started in the first playoff game of his career and had five combined tackles (two solo) and a pass deflection as the Chargers lost 30–31 at the [[2022 Jacksonville Jaguars season|Jacksonville Jaguars]] in the AFC Wild-Card Game.

==== 2023 ====
He entered training camp slated to be the starting free safety under new defensive coordinator [[Derrick Ansley]].<ref>{{cite web| title=5 Chargers training camp battles to watch| url=https://chargerswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/chargers/2024/07/15/los-angeles-chargers-training-camp-battles/74417480007/| access-date=April 13, 2025| website=chargerswire.usatoday.com| author=Alex Katson| date=July 15, 2023}}</ref> Head coach [[Brandon Staley]] named him a starting safety to begin the season and paired him with starting strong safety [[Derwin James]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Chargers Release Unofficial Week 1 Depth Chart for 2023| url=https://www.chargers.com/news/chargers-depth-chart-week-1-2023| access-date=April 13, 2025| website=Chargers.com| author=Eric Smith| date=September 5, 2023}}</ref>

On September 10, 2023, Gilman started in the [[2023 Los Angeles Chargers season|Los Angeles Chargers']] home-opener against the [[2023 Miami Dolphins season|Miami Dolphins]] and set a career-high with 11 combined tackles (nine solo) during a 34–36 loss. He was inactive for three games (Weeks 4, 6–7) due to a heel injury. On December 15, 2023, the Chargers fired head coach Brandon Staley after falling to a 5–9 record and appointed outside of linebackers coach [[Giff Smith]] to interim head coach.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gordon |first1=Grant |title=Chargers fire head coach Brandon Staley, general manager Tom Telesco following blowout loss to Raiders |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/chargers-fire-head-coach-brandon-staley-general-manager-tom-telesco-following-bl |website=NFL.com |access-date=15 December 2023}}</ref> In Week 16, he had three combined tackles (two solo), one pass deflection, and intercepted a pass by [[Josh Allen]] to wide receiver [[Stefon Diggs]] during a 22–24 loss against the [[2023 Buffalo Bills season|Buffalo Bills]]. On January 7, 2024, Gilman made three combined tackles (one solo), tied his season-high with two pass deflections, and set a career-high with his second interception of the season on a pass by [[Blaine Gabbert]] to wide receiver [[Mecole Hardman]] during a 12–13 loss against the [[2023 Kansas City Chiefs season|Kansas City Chiefs]]. He started 14 games while recording 73 combined tackles (49 solo), a career-high ten pass deflections, three forced fumbles, two fumble recoveries, and two interceptions.<ref>{{cite web| title=Pro-Football-Reference: Alohi Gilman Game Logs (2023)| url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/G/GilmAl00.htm| access-date=April 13, 2025| website=pro-football-reference.com}}</ref> He received an overall grade of 86.1 from [[Pro Football Focus]] in 2023.<ref name="PFF1">{{cite web| title=Updated 2024 NFL roster rankings: Strengths, weaknesses and X factors for every starting lineup| url=https://www.pff.com/news/nfl-roster-rankings-all-32-teams-2024-strengths-weaknesses-x-factors| access-date=April 7, 2025| website=PFF.com| author=Jim Wyman| date=September 3, 2024}}</ref>

==== 2024 ====
On March 13, 2024, the Chargers signed Gilman to a two–year, $10.12 million contract extension that includes $5.62 million guaranteed upon signing and an initial [[signing bonus]] of $4.50 million.<ref>{{cite web|title=Los Angeles Chargers Sign Alohi Gilman|url=https://www.chargers.com/news/los-angeles-chargers-sign-alohi-gilman-2024|website=Chargers.com|date=March 13, 2024}}</ref><ref name="spotrac"/>

He returned to training camp slated as the ''de facto'' starting free safety under new defensive coordinator [[Jesse Minter]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Chargers' AJ Finley emerging as front-runner in third-safety battle at training camp| url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5682780/2024/08/05/chargers-training-camp-aj-finley-safety/| access-date=April 13, 2025| website=[[The New York Times]]| date=August 5, 2024}}</ref> Head coach [[Jim Harbaugh]] retained Gilman and Derwin James as the starting safeties to begin the season.<ref>{{cite web| title=Chargers release 1st unofficial depth chart of 2024 season| url=https://www.chargers.com/news/unofficial-depth-chart-2024-season| access-date=April 13, 2025| website=Chargers.com| author=Eric Smith| date=August 6, 2024}}</ref>

He was inactive for the Chargers' 26–3 victory at the [[2024 Carolina Panthers season|Carolina Panthers]] in Week 2 due to a knee injury.<ref name="fox" /> On October 13, 2024, Gilman set a season-high with ten combined tackles (six solo), made one pass deflection, and had his first career sack on [[Bo Nix]] during a 23–16 victory at the [[2024 Denver Broncos season|Denver Broncos]]. In Week 9, he had five combined tackles (four solo), a pass deflection, and had his lone interception of the season on a pass by [[Jameis Winston]] to wide receiver [[Cedric Tillman (American football, born 2000)|Cedric Tillman]] as the Chargers won 27–10 at the [[2024 Cleveland Browns season|Cleveland Browns]]. In Week 12, Gilman made one pass deflection before exiting in the second quarter of a 23–20 loss to the [[2024 Baltimore Ravens season|Baltimore Ravens]] due to a hamstring injury. On November 30, 2024, the Chargers officially placed him on [[injured reserve]] due to his hamstring injury.<ref>{{cite web| title=Chargers' Alohi Gilman: Lands on IR due to hamstring injury| url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/chargers-alohi-gilman-lands-on-ir-due-to-hamstring-injury/| access-date=April 13, 2025| website=cbssports.com| date=December 1, 2024}}</ref> On January 4, 2025, the Chargers activated Gilman from injured reserve and added him back to their active roster after he was inactive for five games (Weeks 13–17).<ref>{{cite web| title=Chargers activate S Alohi Gilman off injured reserve| url=https://www.boltsfromtheblue.com/2025/1/4/24335914/chargers-alohi-gilman-injured-reserve-denzel-perryman| access-date=April 13, 2025| website=boltsfromtheblue.com| date=January 4, 2025| author=Michael Peterson}}</ref> He finished the season with a total of 50 combined tackles (34 solo), four pass deflections, one sack, and one interception in 11 games and 11 starts.<ref>{{cite web| title=Pro-Football-Reference: Alohi Gilman Game Logs (2024)| url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/G/GilmAl00.htm| access-date=April 13, 2025| website=pro-football-reference.com}}</ref> He received an overall grade of 55.3 from [[Pro Football Focus]], which ranked 129th among 171 qualifying safeties in 2024.<ref name="PFF">{{cite web| title=Pro Football Focus: Alohi Gilman| url=https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/alohi-gilman/41662| access-date=April 13, 2025| website=pff.com}}</ref>

====2025====
Gilman made five starts for the Chargers, recording three pass deflections and 22 combined tackles.

=== Baltimore Ravens ===
On October 7, 2025, Gilman and a [[2026 NFL draft|2026]] fifth-round pick (No. 162: [[Chandler Rivers]]) were traded to the [[Baltimore Ravens]] in exchange for [[Odafe Oweh]] and a 2027 seventh-round pick.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Mink|first=Ryan|title=Ravens Trade Odafe Oweh to Los Angeles Chargers|url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/odafe-oweh-ravens-trade-los-angeles-chargers-2025|website=baltimoreravens.com|date=October 7, 2025|access-date=October 7, 2025}}</ref> On December 14, Gilman scored his first NFL touchdown when teammate [[Kyle Van Noy]] picked off [[2025 Cincinnati Bengals season|Cincinnati Bengals]] quarterback [[Joe Burrow]], then handed Gilman the ball, who ran it back for an 84-yard score.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Reedy|first=Joe|title= Lamar Jackson's 2 TD passes, long pick-6 propel Ravens to 24-0 win over Bengals|url= https://www.msn.com/en-us/sports/nfl/lamar-jacksons-2-td-passes-long-pick-6-propel-ravens-to-24-0-win-over-bengals/ar-AA1SkzD0?ocid=BingNewsSerp|date=December 14, 2025|access-date=December 14, 2025}}</ref>

===Kansas City Chiefs===
On March 12, 2026, Gilman signed a three-year, $24.75 million contract with the [[Kansas City Chiefs]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=McMullen |first1=Matt |date=March 12, 2026 |title=Five Things to Know About New Chiefs Safety Alohi Gilman |url=https://www.chiefs.com/news/five-things-to-know-about-new-chiefs-safety-alohi-gilman- |access-date=13 March 2026 |website=Chiefs.com}}</ref>

'''Alontae Devaun Taylor''' (born December 3, 1998) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[cornerback]] for the [[Tennessee Titans]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Tennessee Volunteers football|Tennessee Volunteers]].

==Early life==
Taylor attended [[Coffee County Central High School]] in [[Manchester, Tennessee]]. He played [[quarterback]] in high school and during his career, he had 8,225 yards of total offense and 75 [[touchdowns]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ubben |first=David |date=November 7, 2018 |title=Alontae Taylor's road from a skinny, small-town quarterback to a key piece of Jeremy Pruitt's defense at Tennessee |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/635773/2018/11/07/alontae-taylors-road-from-a-skinny-small-town-quarterback-to-a-key-piece-of-jeremy-pruitts-defense-at-tennessee/ |access-date=January 26, 2023 |website=The Athletic |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kreager |first=Tom |date=July 10, 2017 |title=Tennessee Vols commitment Alontae Taylor of Coffee County is No. 4 on 2017 Dandy Dozen |url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/high-school/2017/07/10/tennessean-dandy-dozen-alontae-taylor/402007001/ |access-date=January 26, 2023 |website=The Tennessean |language=en-US}}</ref> Taylor played in the 2018 [[Under Armour All-American Game]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hilbert |first=Evan |date=November 16, 2017 |title=Alontae Taylor receives Under Armour All-America Game jersey |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2017/alontae-taylor-receives-under-armour-all-america-game-jersey |access-date=January 26, 2023 |website=USA TODAY High School Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> He committed to the [[University of Tennessee]] to play [[college football]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kreager |first=Tom |date=December 22, 2017 |title=Coffee County's Alontae Taylor signs with Tennessee Vols football |url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/high-school/2017/12/22/coffee-countys-alontae-taylor-signs-tennessee-vols/976394001/ |access-date=January 26, 2023 |website=The Tennessean |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Hamilton |first=Gerry |last2=VanHaaren |first2=Tom |date=December 24, 2017 |title=Tennessee secure WR Alontae Taylor (No. 46) after losing two QB recruits |url=https://abcnews.go.com/Sports/tennessee-secure-wr-alontae-taylor-46-losing-qb/story?id=51783876 |access-date=January 26, 2023 |website=ABC News}}</ref>

==College career==
Taylor played at Tennessee under head coaches [[Jeremy Pruitt]] and [[Josh Heupel]] from 2018 to 2021.<ref name="sr">{{Cite web |title=Alontae Taylor College Stats, School, Draft, Gamelog, Splits |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/alontae-taylor-1.html |access-date=January 26, 2023 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Tennessee Volunteers Coaches |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/schools/tennessee/ |access-date=January 26, 2023 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Gallagher |first=Michael |date=July 21, 2021 |title=Alontae Taylor: 'Power T on my chest is bigger than me' |url=https://www.nashvillepost.com/sports/ut/alontae-taylor-power-t-on-my-chest-is-bigger-than-me/article_db0912f6-e9d6-11eb-adff-4fa8b4ed8b13.html |access-date=January 26, 2023 |website=Nashville Post |language=en}}</ref> He originally played [[wide receiver]] at Tennessee before transitioning to cornerback prior to his freshman year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rutherford |first=Nathanael |date=October 16, 2018 |title=Alontae Taylor Has Been Elite to Start His UT Career |url=https://www.rockytopinsider.com/2018/10/16/alontae-taylor-has-been-elite-to-start-his-ut-career/ |access-date=January 26, 2023 |website=Rocky Top Insider |language=en-US}}</ref> He became a starter his freshman year and overall started 31 of 45 career games. Taylor finished his career with 162 tackles, four [[interceptions]], one pick-six, and one fumble recovery for a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tennessee at Auburn Box Score, October 13, 2018 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2018-10-13-auburn.html |access-date=January 26, 2023 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Gray |first=Nick |date=November 6, 2021 |title=See Tennessee Vols football's Alontae Taylor run back interception for TD to change game vs. Kentucky |url=https://www.knoxnews.com/story/sports/college/university-of-tennessee/football/2021/11/06/tennessee-vols-football-alontae-taylor-touchdown-interception-kentucky-wildcats/6325856001/ |access-date=January 26, 2023 |website=Knoxville News Sentinel |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="sr" /> He decided to sit out the [[2021 Music City Bowl]] in preparation for the [[2022 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sparks |first=Adam |date=December 1, 2021 |title=Tennessee cornerback Alontae Taylor forgoing bowl game, declaring for NFL Draft |url=https://www.knoxnews.com/story/sports/college/university-of-tennessee/2021/12/01/tennessee-football-alontae-taylor-declare-nfl-draft-bowl-game/8825646002/ |access-date=January 26, 2023 |website=Knoxville News Sentinel |language=en-US}}</ref>
