===New Orleans Saints===
====2022====
The [[New Orleans Saints]] selected Taylor in the second round (49th overall) of the [[2022 NFL draft]]. He was the eighth cornerback selected in 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 29, 2022 |title=New Orleans Saints select Tennessee cornerback Alontae Taylor with Pick 49 in the 2022 NFL Draft |url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/alontae-taylor-nfl-draft-cornerback-tennessee-new-orleans-saints-draft-pick-49 |access-date=January 26, 2023 |website=NewOrleansSaints.com}}</ref>

On July 19, 2022, the Saints signed Taylor to a four–year, $7.20 million rookie [[contract]] that includes $3.45 million guaranteed upon signing and an initial [[signing bonus]] of $2.41 million.<ref name="spotrac">{{cite web| title=Spotrac.com: Alontae Taylor contract| url=https://www.spotrac.com/nfl/player/_/id/76925/alontae-taylor| access-date=April 24, 2025| website=Spotrac.com}}</ref>

He entered training camp projected to be a backup cornerback and competed to be the third cornerback on the depth chart against veteran [[Bradley Roby]].<ref>{{cite web| title=2022 Saints Training Camp Preview: Cornerback| url=https://www.si.com/nfl/saints/training-camp/saints-training-camp-preview-2022-cornerback| access-date=April 24, 2025| website=SI.com| author=Bob Rose| date=July 20, 2022}}</ref> Head coach [[Dennis Allen (American football)|Dennis Allen]] named him a backup and listed him as the fourth cornerback on the depth chart to begin the season, behind [[Marshon Lattimore]], [[Paulson Adebo]], and Bradley Roby.<ref>{{cite web| title=Saints’ depth chart from top to bottom: Breaking down the team as the 2022 season begins| url=https://www.nola.com/sports/saints/saints-depth-chart-from-top-to-bottom-breaking-down-the-team-as-the-2022-season/article_2a02e6e4-313d-11ed-8000-2faaa84804d1.html| access-date=April 24, 2025| website=Nola.com| author=Terrin Waack| date=September 10, 2022}}</ref>

On September 11, 2022, Taylor made his professional regular season debut in the [[2022 New Orleans Saints season|New Orleans Saints']] season-opener at the [[2022 Atlanta Falcons season|Atlanta Falcons]], but only saw limited snaps on special teams as they won 27–26. On September 24, 2022, the Saints officially placed Taylor on [[injured reserve]] after he injured his knee during practice.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 24, 2022 |title=New Orleans Saints announce roster moves |url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/new-orleans-saints-announce-roster-moves-alontae-taylor-demarcus-fields |access-date=January 26, 2023 |website=NewOrleansSaints.com}}</ref> On October 20, 2022, the Saints activated him from injured reserve and added him back to their active roster after he was inactive for the last four games (Weeks 3–6).<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 20, 2022 |title=New Orleans Saints announce roster moves |url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/new-orleans-saints-announce-roster-moves-x7051 |access-date=January 26, 2023 |website=NewOrleansSaints.com}}</ref> He was immediately named the No. 2 starting cornerback alongside Bradley Roby after Marshon Lattimore was placed on injured reserve due to an abdominal injury he suffered in Week a 5 and Paulson Adebo injured his ankle in Week 6 and was subsequently inactive for Week 7. On October 20, 2022, Taylor earned his first career start and recorded three solo tackles during a 34–42 loss at the [[2022 Arizona Cardinals season|Arizona Cardinals]]. In Week 13, he set a season-high with eight combined tackles (six solo) and made one pass deflection as the Saints lost 16–17 at the [[2022 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season|Tampa Bay Buccaneers]]. The following week, Taylor made four solo tackles and tied his season-high of three pass deflections during a 21–18 win against the Atlanta Falcons in Week 14. In his rookie season, Taylor appeared in 13 games, starting the last nine consecutive games and finished with a total of with 46 combined tackles (39 solo) and 11 passes defended.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alontae Taylor 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/T/TaylAl01/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=January 26, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2023====
He entered training camp slated to be a backup cornerback under new defensive coordinator [[Joe Woods (American football)|Joe Woods]] following the departure of Bradley Roby. He also competed for the role as the starting nickelback against [[Isaac Yiadom]] and [[Lonnie Johnson Jr.]] Head coach Dennis Allen named him the starting nickelback to begin the season and listed him as the third cornerback on the depth chart behind starting tandem [[Marshon Lattimore]] and Paulson Adebo.<ref>{{cite web|title=Saints release first depth chart ahead of Week 1 game vs. Titans| url=https://saintswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/saints/2023/09/07/saints-depth-chart-against-titans-week-1/80140045007/| access-date=March 6, 2025| website=saintswire.usatoday.com| author=John Sigler| date=September 7, 2023}}</ref>

In Week 3, Taylor earned his first start of the season as a nickelback and recorded five solo tackles, set a career-high with five pass deflections, and had his first career sack on [[Jordan Love]] for a 14–yard loss in the second quarter of a 17–18 loss at the [[2023 Green Bay Packers season|Green Bay Packers]]. In Week 7, he set a season-high with six combined tackles (five solo) as the Saints lost 24–31 against the [[2023 Jacksonville Jaguars season|Jacksonville Jaguars]].
On December 31, 2023, Taylor made four combined tackles (three solo), one pass deflection, and had his first career interception on a pass by [[Baker Mayfield]] to wide receiver [[Trey Palmer]] during a 23–13 victory at the [[2023 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season|Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 2, 2024 |title=Saints' Alontae Taylor: Gets first career INT in win| url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/saints-alontae-taylor-gets-first-career-int-in-win/amp/ |access-date=January 5, 2024 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref> On January 7, 2024, Taylor made one solo tackle, one pass deflection, and had another interception for back-to-back games after picking off a pass attempt by [[Desmond Ridder]] to tight end [[Kyle Pitts]] as the Saints routed the [[2023 Atlanta Falcons season|Atlanta Falcons]] 48–17.<ref>{{cite web| title=Pro-Football-Reference: Alontae Taylor Game Logs (2023)| url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/T/TaylAl01.htm |access-date=April 24, 2025| website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> He appeared in all 17 games during the [[2023 NFL season]], starting 13 of them and finished the season with 75 combined tackles (56 solo), two interceptions, 14 passes defended, one sack, and one forced fumble.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alontae Taylor 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/T/TaylAl01/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=January 12, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2024====
Entering training camp, Taylor was projected to return as a backup. He competed to be the third cornerback on the depth chart and starting nickelback against [[2024 NFL draft|2024]] second-round pick [[Kool-Aid McKinstry]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Training camp spotlight: Kool-Aid McKinstry vs. Alontae Taylor| url=https://saintswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/saints/2024/07/24/training-camp-spotlight-kool-aid-mckinstry-vs-alontae-taylor/74527139007/| access-date=April 24, 2025| website=saintswire.usatoday.com/|date=July 24, 2024| author=Darrion Gray}}</ref> He was named the third cornerback on the depth chart to begin the season, behind starting cornerbacks [[Paulson Adebo]] and Marshon Lattimore.<ref>{{cite web| title=Unveiled: Saints' Full Depth Chart for Opening Week Showdown With Panthers| url=https://www.si.com/nfl/saints/news/unveiled-saints-full-depth-chart-opening-week-panthers-rattler-haener| access-date=April 24, 2025| website=SI.com| date=September 3, 2024| author=Bob Rose}}</ref> 

On September 8, 2024, Taylor recorded six combined tackles (five solo), made one pass deflection, and set a new career-high with three sacks on [[Bryce Young]] as the Saints routed the [[2024 Carolina Panthers season|Carolina Panthers]] 47–10.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Gray |first=Carrion |date=2024-09-08 |title=Alontae Taylor makes Saints history in 2024 season opener |url=https://saintswire.usatoday.com/2024/09/08/alontae-taylor-saints-record-sacks-by-defensive-back-panthers-2024-season/ |access-date=2024-09-09 |website=Saints Wire|publisher=USA Today |language=en-US}}</ref> His three sack performance set a Saints franchise record for most sacks in a single game by a [[defensive back]] and tied the NFL record.
<ref name=":0" /> The following week, Taylor set a season-high with nine combined tackles (seven solo) during a 44–19 win at the [[2024 Dallas Cowboys season|Dallas Cowboys]] in Week 2. On October 22, the Saints placed Paulson Adebo on [[injured reserve]] for the rest of the season..<ref>{{cite web|title=Paulson Adebo injury update: Saints CB breaks femur during 'Thursday Night Football' game| url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/saints/2024/10/18/paulson-adebo-injury-update-broken-femur/75728304007/| access-date=March 6, 2025| website=USAToday.com| date=October 18, 2024| author=John McKessy}}</ref> Taylor was subsequently named the No. 2 starting cornerback alongside Marshon Lattimore entering Week 8. In Week 9, he recorded four combined tackles (three solo) and set a season-high with three pass deflections as the Saints lost 22–23 at the Carolina Panthers in Week 8. On November 4, 2024, the New Orleans Saints announced their decision to fire head coach [[Dennis Allen (American football)|Dennis Allen]] after they fell to a record of 2–7 and appointed special teams coordinator [[Darren Rizzi]] to interim head coach for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Saints relieve head coach Dennis Allen of his duties|url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/dennis-allen-saints-head-coach-relieved-of-duties-darren-rizzi-interim-head-coach-november-4-2024|website=neworleanssaints.com|date=November 4, 2024|access-date=November 4, 2024}}</ref> The following day, the Saints traded starting cornerback [[Marshon Lattimore]] to the [[2024 Washington Commanders season|Washington Commanders]], subsequently making Taylor the ''de facto'' No. 1 starting cornerback. He started the next two games alongside [[Shemar Jean-Charles]] due to rookie Kool-Aid McKinstry sustaining a hamstring injury, rendering him inactive for two games.

He finished the 2024 season with four sacks, 89 tackles, 16 passes defended, and two forced fumbles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alontae Taylor 2024 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/T/TaylAl01/gamelog/2024/ |access-date=2025-02-03 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

====2025====
Taylor made 17 appearances (including 16 starts) for New Orleans during the 2025 campaign, recording two interceptions, 11 pass deflections, two sacks, and 83 combined tackles.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Alontae Taylor 2025 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/gamelog/_/id/4369835/alontae-taylor|access-date=May 4, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

===Tennessee Titans===
On March 12, 2026, Taylor signed a three-year, $60 million contract with the [[Tennessee Titans]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Wyatt |first1=Jim |date=March 12, 2026 |title=Titans Sign Cornerback Alontae Taylor |url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-sign-cornerback-alontae-taylor |access-date=13 March 2026 |website=TennesseeTitans.com}}</ref>

'''Allen DeGraffenreid''' (born June 3, 1974) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was an [[offensive lineman]] for one season with the [[Arizona Cardinals]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Vanderbilt Commodores football|Vanderbilt Commodores]]. He was also a member of the [[Denver Broncos]].

==Early life and college==
Allen DeGraffenreid was born on June 3, 1974, in [[Kansas City, Missouri]].<ref name="pfa"/> He has a twin brother, Bryan, who played with him in high school and college.<ref name="auto">{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-tennessean/161903235/|newspaper=[[The Tennessean]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=February 6, 1992|page=16|title=Allen DeGraffenreid, DL}} {{Open access}}</ref> He attended [[Dunwoody High School]] in [[Dunwoody, Georgia]].<ref name="pfa">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/players/d/degr00210.html | title=Allen DeGraffenreid | publisher=profootballarchives.com | accessdate=23 December 2024}}</ref> He only played a single season of high school football, but was nonetheless a top-ranked prospect, being among the top 20 recruits in the state.<ref name="auto"/>

He was a member of the [[Vanderbilt Commodores football|Vanderbilt Commodores]] from 1993 to 1996 and a three-year [[letterman (sports)|letterman]] from 1994 to 1996.<ref name="pfa"/> He was a starter in his [[Junior (education year)|junior]] and [[Senior (education)|senior]] seasons, playing at [[left tackle]] in 1995 before moving to [[Guard (gridiron football)|guard]] in 1996.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-arizona-republic/161903540/|newspaper=[[The Arizona Republic]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=April 24, 1997|page=13|title=Adding bulk}} {{Open access}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-commercial-appeal/161903730/|newspaper=[[The Commercial Appeal]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=August 22, 1996|page=35|title=Vanderbilt}} {{Open access}}</ref> After his senior year, he was invited to the [[NFL Scouting Combine]]; his twin brother received an invite to the event as well.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-tennessean/161903611/|newspaper=[[The Tennessean]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=January 31, 1997|page=17|title=Three players headed to combine|author=Organ, Mike}} {{Open access}}</ref>

==Professional career==
After going undrafted in the [[1997 NFL draft]], DeGraffenreid signed with the [[Arizona Cardinals]] on April 21.<ref name="transactions"/> He quit the team in July but later returned that same month.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-arizona-republic/161903843/|newspaper=[[The Arizona Republic]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=July 30, 1997|page=20|title=Rookie lineman returns to camp after quitting|author=Schoenfeld, Steve}} {{Open access}}</ref> He was released on August 19 and signed to the Cardinals' practice squad on August 26, 1997.<ref name="transactions"/> The next year, he made the team as a third-string [[Center (gridiron football)|center]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-arizona-republic/161903983/|newspaper=[[The Arizona Republic]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=September 16, 1998|page=22|title=Clement likely out for next 2 Cards games}} {{Open access}}</ref> He finished the 1998 season having appeared in five games.<ref name="pfr">{{Cite web |title=Allen DeGraffenreid Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/D/DeGrAl20.htm |access-date=2025-01-22 |publisher=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> DeGraffenreid was released on September 5, 1999.<ref name="transactions"/> He wore jersey number 69 while with the Cardinals.<ref name="pfr" /> He stood 6'4" and was 293 pounds during his professional career.<ref name="pfr" />

DeGraffenreid was signed by the [[Denver Broncos]] on January 18, 2000.<ref name="transactions"/> He was released on August 21, 2000.<ref name="transactions">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/transactions/d/degr00210.html | title=Allen DeGraffenreid NFL Transactions | publisher=profootballarchives.com | accessdate=23 December 2024}}</ref>

'''Allen Justice DeGraffenreid''' (born May 1, 1970) is an American former professional [[gridiron football|football]] [[wide receiver]] who played one season with the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Ohio State Buckeyes football|Ohio State Buckeyes]]. He was also a member of the [[Kansas City Chiefs]], [[Green Bay Packers]], and [[San Francisco 49ers]] of the NFL, the [[Scottish Claymores]] of the [[World League of American Football]] (WLAF), and the [[Winnipeg Blue Bombers]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL).

==Early life==
Allen Justice DeGraffenreid was born on May 1, 1970, in [[Cincinnati, Ohio]].<ref name="pfa"/> He attended [[Princeton High School (Ohio)|Princeton High School]] in [[Sharonville, Ohio]].<ref name="pfa"/> He participated in soccer, track, and football at Princeton High, and in his sophomore year, he was a member of the state title-winning [[3,200 meter relay]] team.<ref name="osu">{{cite web | url=https://ohiostatebuckeyes.com/documents/2023/5/20/1991_guide.pdf | title=1991 Ohio State Football Media Guide | publisher=[[Ohio State University]] |pages=28 | accessdate=December 23, 2024}}</ref> He joined the football team as a [[placekicker]] his junior year.<ref name="wilm"/> He converted seven of nine field goals during his career and also made eight extra points in two games during the playoffs his senior year, helping Princeton win the state title.<ref name="osu"/>

==College career==
By the time he had left high school, DeGraffenreid was 6'0" and 155 pounds.<ref name="wilm"/> The [[University of Tennessee]] offered DeGraffenreid a scholarship to join the school's track team.<ref name="wilm"/> He instead joined the [[Ohio State Buckeyes football|Ohio State Buckeyes]] as a [[walk-on (sports)|walk-on]] placekicker but later converted to wide receiver.<ref name="wilm">{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/wilmington-news-journal/161955234/ | title=The forgotten Buckeye | work=[[Wilmington News-Journal]] | date=July 29, 1993 | accessdate=December 31, 2024 | author=Huber, Mark | pages=6}}</ref><ref name="packers">{{cite web | url=https://247sports.com/nfl/green-bay-packers/article/training-camp-showcases-surprises-104210726/amp/ | title=Training camp showcases surprises | publisher=247sports.com | date=July 17, 2005 | accessdate=December 23, 2024 | author=Huber, Bill}}</ref> After he [[redshirted]] the 1988 season, he played in four games as a redshirt freshman in 1989.<ref name="osu"/> He was then a three-year [[letterman (sports)|letterman]] from 1990 to 1992.<ref name="packers"/><ref name="pfa"/> He did not have a scholarship until 1991.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://ohiostatebuckeyes.com/documents/2023/5/20/1992_guide.pdf | title=1992 Ohio State Football Media Guide | publisher=[[Ohio State University]] |pages=30 | accessdate=December 23, 2024}}</ref><ref name="wilm"/> Overall, he caught one pass for seven yards in 1990, one pass for 15 yards in 1991, and six passes for 65 yards in 1992.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/allen-degraffenreid-1.html?__hstc=223721476.b6fb3e044232ac485df0f8d6b7ffec49.1734974471175.1734974471175.1734978469866.2&__hssc=223721476.2.1734978469866&__hsfp=3011104808 | title=Allen DeGraffenreid | publisher=sports-reference.com | accessdate=December 23, 2024}}</ref> DeGraffenreid majored in psychology at Ohio State.<ref name="osu"/>

==Professional career==
After going undrafted in the [[1993 NFL draft]], DeGraffenreid signed with the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] on April 27.<ref name="transactions">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/transactions/d/degr00200.html | title=Allen DeGraffenreid NFL Transactions | publisher=profootballarchives.com | accessdate=December 23, 2024}}</ref> He had a team-leading three catches for 48 yards in the 1993 preseason opener.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Brennan |first=Jack |date=August 9, 1993 |title=Rookie makes impact |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-cincinnati-enquirer/161955563/ |access-date=December 31, 2024 |work=[[The Cincinnati Enquirer]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> He was released on August 30 but later re-signed on November 27.<ref name="transactions"/> He played in two regular season games for the Bengals during the 1993 season before being released on December 15, 1993.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/D/DeGrAl21.htm | title=Allen DeGraffenreid | publisher=pro-football-reference.com | accessdate=December 23, 2024}}</ref><ref name="transactions"/>

DeGraffenreid was signed to the practice squad of the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] on December 17, 1993.<ref name="transactions"/> He became a free agent after the season and re-signed with the Chiefs on May 18, 1994.<ref name="transactions"/> He was released on August 23 and signed to the team's practice squad on August 31.<ref name="transactions"/> DeGraffenreid was released again on October 12 and signed to the practice squad again on October 19, 1994.<ref name="transactions"/> In 1995, he was allocated to the [[World League of American Football]] (WLAF) to play for the [[Scottish Claymores]].<ref name="pfa"/> He started all ten games for the Claymores during the [[1995 WLAF season]], recording 44 receptions for 624 yards and four touchdowns, 21 kick returns for 490 yards, and eight punt returns for 70 yards.<ref name="packers"/><ref name="pfa"/> The Claymores finished the season with a 2–8 record.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/1995wlafsco.html | title=1995 Scottish Claymores (WLAF) | publisher=profootballarchives.com | accessdate=December 23, 2024}}</ref> He was released by the Chiefs on August 22, 1995.<ref name="transactions"/>

DeGraffenreid signed with the [[Green Bay Packers]] on January 4, 1996, but was released on August 21, 1996.<ref name="transactions"/> He then played in four games for the [[Winnipeg Blue Bombers]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL) during the [[1996 CFL season]], catching eight passes for 132 yards, kicking off once for 61 yards, and returning one kick for five yards.<ref name="pfa"/>

DeGraffenreid returned to the Claymores in 1997, totaling 23 receptions for 450	yards and two touchdowns, one special teams tackle, and one tackle on a turnover.<ref name="pfa">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/players/d/degr00200.html | title=Allen DeGraffenreid | publisher=profootballarchives.com | accessdate=December 23, 2024}}</ref> He was signed by the [[San Francisco 49ers]] on June 26, 1997, but was released on August 19, 1997.<ref name="transactions"/>
